The priorities set in the Strategy for Doubling Farmers Income by 2022 represent the key overarching framework for the agriculture sector. The main objective of the government is to double farmers’ income by solving the twin problems of maximising efficiency and ensuring equity in a sustainable manner. These objectives will be met through diversification into high value fruits and vegetables, increased participation of private players, improved agriculture marketing at state levels, and policy reforms related to leasing. The government is also focussing on boosting productivity through increased adoption of scientifically proven and sustainable agriculture practices such as introduction of improved varieties, integrated soil management, promotion of organic farming and efficient water management practices.
An Inter-ministeral Committee was set up to implement the Strategy. The Committee has identified seven sources of income growth namely, improvement in crop productivity; improvement in livestock productivity; resource use efficiency or savings in the cost of production; increase in the cropping intensity; diversification towards high value crops; improvement in real prices received by farmers; and shift from farm to non-farm occupations. However, the discussion on new programs and initiatives to effective implementation of the strategy is still being under discussion.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved export of processed and/or value added agricultural products even in the event of restriction/ban on export of the related to food staples (Press Information Bureau, 17 January 2013).

To increase the grain national storage capacity through private entrepreneurs, the Government offers a 10-year guarantee to build warehouses under the Private Entrepreneurs Guarantee (PEG) Scheme (Press Information Bureau, 04 March 2013).
Minimum export price (MEP) for basmati rice reduced from Rs$ 1,200 (USD 24) to Rs$ 1,100 (USD 22) per metric tonne.

National Scheme of Welfare of Fishermen - Saving-cum-Relief which operates differently for marine fisherman and inland fisherman. For marine fisherman, Rs.75/- per month shall be collected from eligible marine fishermen for a period of 8 months in a year. A total of Rs.600/- thus collected will be matched with 50% contribution i.e. Rs.300/-, each by the State Government and Central Government separately. In respect of Union Territories, the share of Union Territory Administration would also be borne by the Government of India. The total sum of Rs.1200/- thus collected will be distributed during the four lean months (closed season) to the beneficiaries in four equal monthly installments of Rs.300/- each. The interest accrued will also be disbursed with the fourth installment. For inland fisherman, this component would be applicable to only those inland States, which impose a ban on fishing during the monsoon period either through legislation or through adequate administrative measures including deployment of extension workers to educate the inland fishermen etc. Under this component Rs.50/- per month shall be collected from each eligible inland fisherman for a period of 9 months in a year. A total of Rs.450/- thus collected will be matched with 50% contribution i.e. Rs.225/- each by the State and Central Governments separately. In respect of Union Territories, the share of Union Territory Administration would also be borne by the Government of India. The total sum of Rs.900/- thus collected will be distributed during the three lean months (closed season) to the beneficiaries in three equal monthly installments of Rs.300/- each. The interest accrued will also be disbursed with the third installment.

Increase in the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for wheat  Rs$ 10 000 per tonne in 2008/09 to Rs$ 10,800 per tonne (USD 208) in 2009/10. This measure intends to keep domestic open market wheat prices high.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) today approved the set up of 10 regional labs, 30 State level labs and 120 medical college level labs under the scheme for establishing a network of laboratories for managing epidemics and natural calamities (Press Information Bureau, 28 June 2013)

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the continuation of the ongoing National Food Security Mission (NFSM) targeting a production increase of 25 million tonnes (10 million tonnes of rice, 8 of wheat, 4 of pulses and 3 of coarse cereals) by 2016-17 with a total allocation of INR 123.5 billion during the 12th Five Year Plan. The target will be met  by promoting improved technologies (adoption of quality seeds), enhancing farm efficiency through improved agronomic practices such as line sowing, direct seeding, integrated nutrient management and pest management, water use efficiency and resource conservation technologies among others (Press Information Bureau, 20 September 2013).

The Government has approved an outlay of approximately INR 11 billion (about US$ 180 million) for continuation of the Agriculture Export Promotion Plan Scheme of Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) during the 12th five year plan. The scheme includes four components: infrastructure development, transport assistance, market development and quality development. The main objective of the scheme is to support exporters of agricultural products through need based interventions by APEDA at different stages of the supply chain (Press Information Bureau, 25 November 2013).

Various measures to boost agricultural productivity  with the aim to moderate food inflation. These include: increase of credit subventions (effective interest rate of 4% ),  allocation of USD 87 million to promote vegetable production in urban centers, of USD 65 million  to promote pulses in rainfed areas and of USD 65 million to promote palm oil production.

The Urban Development Ministry will earmark more than 60,000 Crore rupees for the construction of about 11 crore 11 lakh toilets in the country. The Minister also underlined that technology will be used on a large scale to convert residues into wealth in rural India in the forms of bio-fertilizer and different forms of energy.

Ministry of Agriculture and Ministry of Rural Development are taking various actions to conserve degraded lands and improve management of natural resources by partially converting watershed into to cultivation lands (Press Information Bureau, 22 February 2013).

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has approved the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for the 2014/15 rainy crops season, with prices effective from 1 October 2014. Paddy MPS was raised from INR 1 310 to INR 1 360 (US$ 21.89 to 22.73) per quintal for common grade and from INR 1 345 to INR 1 400 (US$ 22.47 to 23.40) per quintal for grade A. Also the sorghum MSP was increased by INR 30 (US$ 0.50) per quintal while MSP of maize, soybean and groundnut-in-shell are maintained at INR 1 310, 2 500 and 4 000 (US$ 21.89, 41.78, 66.85) per quintal, same as in the previous year (PIB, 25 June 2014).

On 19 March 2010, the government approved duty-free wheat imports indefinitely, to boost local supplies and stabilise local prices. The period for tax free imports had been due to expire on 31 March 2010. Additionally, the deadline for the export of 650,000 tons of wheat products by private traders was extended indefinitely.
Import duty on rice abolished.
Basmati rice exports are restricted only to Mundra and Pipavav ports.

National Food Security Mission (NFSM) introduced during 2007/08 as an instrument to provide the States with additional resources on 10 percent grant basis.  NFSM intends to increase the production of rice, wheat and pulses through area expansion and productivity enhancement in a sustainable manner in certain identified districts of the country.  States were given the freedom to address their priorities in agriculture through these new programs, even as the older, more structured schemes were continued.
Import ban on milk and milk products from China id extended until December 2011. It includes any food preparations with milk or milk solids as an ingredient from China.

COVID-19: Government gives benefits to farmers on crop loan repayments due to Covid-19 lockdown. The Government has extended the benefit of 2% Interest Subvention (IS) to Banks and 3% Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI) to all farmers upto 31st May, 2020 for all crop loans up to Rs.3 lakh given by banks which have become due or are becoming due between 1st March, 2020 and 31st May, 2020.
Partially lift of the export ban by allowing  exports  of 400 000 tonnes of wheat and 100 000 tonnes of rice to Bangladesh.

The governemnt of India issued the Draft National Forest Policy, 2018. The overall objective and goal of the present policy is to safegard the ecological and livelihood security of people, of the present and future generations, based on sustainable management of the forests for the flow of ecosystem services in order.

Minimum support price for wheat for the marketing year 2010/11 (April/March) has been increased to INR 11 000 (USD 247) per tonne, up by INR 200 from the previous year. The Government has planned to buy 24 million tonnes of wheat at the new price by March 2011. The minimum support price for rice has been increased by INR 50 to INR 10 000/tonne for common grades (USD 210/tonne) and to INR 10 300 for superior grades (USD 224/tonne).

In view of high prices of onion in the market, imports requirements regarding fumigation and endorsement of Phytosanitary Certificate (PSC) as per the Plant Quarantine Order 2003, are derogated up to 30 November 2013. Consignments of imported onions without fumigation and PSC must be fumigated in India by the importer through an accredited treatment provider, inspected by quarantine officials and released only if found free from pests and diseases (Press Information Bureau, 23 October 2013).

Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) to increase the minimum support price (MSP) for common paddy during the 2015/16 kharif marketing season (October September) by about Rs.50 per quintal (around $7.8 per ton) or about 3.6% to around Rs.1,410 per quintal (around $220 per ton), according to local sources.

On March 25,2013, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry extended the export ban on pulses by one more year till March 31, 2014. However, exports of garbanzo bean (kabuli chana) and 10,000 metric tons of organic pulses continue to be exempted from the ban.
Amendment to the policy for casein and casein product exports, that moves these products from the “prohibited” to the “restricted” category, permitable under license.

Increase in the Minimum Support Price (MSP) of paddy (un-milled rice) for MY 2009/10 by Rs. 1,000 per metric ton (including a bonus of Rs. 500 per ton) to Rs. 10,000 (USD 215) per ton for Common varieties and Rs. 10,300 (USD 221.5) per ton for Grade A varieties.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), which is addressing the nutritional gap in the population through fortification of various foods, has now constituted a Scientific Panel on “Food Fortification and Nutrition” to take the program further.

The Department of Animal Husbandry, Dairying, and Fisheries (DADF) published a notification for importing livestock (except live shrimp), which requires an import license issued by the Ministry of Commerce and complying with sanitary conditions as specified in the applicable veterinary health certificate. Although not notified to the WTO, the notification includes pre-export and post-import requirements.

The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today has given its approval for extension of validity of Central Order No.SO.2559 (E) dated 30.9.2014 for a further period of one year, that is from 1st October, 2015 to 30th September 2016 in respect of pulses, edible oils and edible oilseeds. 
This will enable States to regulate trade of these essential commodities and to continue to take effective operations under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955. They can impose stock limits/licensing requirements etc. to curb unscrupulous trading, hoarding and profiteering. The extension will also help the States in tackling the problem of ensuring adequate availability of these commodities in the domestic market and keep prices under control.

The Government of India decided to revise the buffer norms for rice and wheat in the Central Pool (food grains stocks procured by Central Government and State Governments through minimum support price operations), which remained unchanged since 2005.

On 28 November 2013, the Cabinet extended the stockholding limits imposed on pulses, edible oils and edible oilseeds up to 30 September 2014 and of rice and paddy up to 30 November 2014, in an effort to prevent hoarding and ensure stable prices. Stocks of edible oil, edible oilseeds and rice meant for export are excluded from the stock holding limit under the Essential Commodities Act (Press Information Bureau, 17 January 2014).
State-owned trading firms are allowed to import a quota of 500 000 tonnes of pulses , but the 15 percent import subsidy to cover possible offloading losses  is suspended.
Minimum price export (MPE) on non- basmati and basmati rice increased from US$ 650 to US$ 1000  and from US$ 950 to US$ 1,100 per metric ton respectively.

The Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act

On 1 July 2017, the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act 2017 came into force across India which introduced a goods and services tax of 28% on all goods [including aerated waters], containing added sugar or other sweetening matter or flavour with a further 12% cess added on top of the tax. This Act replaces all other GST laws at State level and is applied across India. It is the highest GST rate for goods in India.
Reduction of the Minimum Export Price of three superior non basmati rice varieties (approved in early 2011) to USD 600 per tonne from USD 850 per tonne.

In order to take part in this global programme of REDD+, India develops the National REDD+ Strategy or Action Plans on reducing emissions from deforestation, forest degradation and fulfilling the role of conservation of forest carbon stocks and sustainable management of forests. The Strategy builds upon existing national circumstances and in line with India’s National Action Plan on Climate Change, Green India Mission and India’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC). 
The overarching objective of National REDD+ Strategy (NRPS) of India is to facilitate implementation of REDD+ programme in the country in conformity with relevant decisions of UNFCCC, in particular the Cancun. REDD+ activities are defined and implemented in three phases: (i) Phase 1 is the development of national strategies or action plans, policies and measures, and capacity-building; (ii) Phase 2 is the implementation of national policies and measures and national strategies or action plans that could involve further capacity-building, technology development and transfer and results-based demonstration activities; (iii) Phase 3 is the evolvement into results based actions that should be fully measured, reported and verified. The strategy will follow the sub-national approach to implement the Sub-national REDD+ Action Plans. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change will coordinate relevant agencies in developing and implementing appropriate policies, methodologies, procedures and technologies relating to REDD+ implementation in the country.

On 2 July 2014, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the distribution of an additional 5 million tonnes of rice from government stocks between July 2014 and March 2015, in an attempt to counter the potential for domestic price inflation. Tied to worries about weak monsoon rains and potentially higher domestic prices, the government announced on 16 July that more than 10 million tonnes of centrally-held wheat stocks would be sold to bulk users. The sale was approved on 24 July 2014.
Zero import duty regime for wheat extended indefinitely.

The Government of India introduced additional input subsidies in response to drought: (i) Diesel subsidy scheme, that provides 50 percent of the cost of diesel for supplementary and protective irrigation will be provided as financial assistance to farmers; and an (ii) Enhanced subsidy scheme, ceiling on seeds subsidy is enhanced for cereals, pulses and oilseeds under on-going schemes (Press Information Bureau, 31 August 2012).

India acts to seize gap in wheat export market left by Ukraine war.

India is rolling out ambitious measures over the coming weeks to try to establish the country as a dominant exporter of high-quality wheat as importers scramble for supplies following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

The Union Cabinet has approved the construction of 69 Bridges including Approach Roads on the Tamu-Kyigone-Kalewa (TKK) road section of the Trilateral Highway in Myanmar at a cost of Rs.371.58 crore. It will improve connectivity between India and Myanmar and facilitate movement of goods and traffic.

The Government fixed the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for Rabi (winter) crops of 2013-14 season starting in October to be marketed in 2014-15 as follows: • Wheat MSP is fixed at INR 1400 (US$ 22.8) per quintal, marking an increase of INR 50 (US$ 0.8) per quintal over the last year's
• Barley MSP is fixed at INR 1100 (US$ 18) per quintal (INR 120 per quintal increase)
• MSPs of gram and masur (lentil) set at INR 3100 (US$ 50.5) and INR 2950 (US$ 48) per quintal respectively, raised by INR 100 and INR 50 per quintal respectively 
• Rapeseed/mustard MSP at INR 3050 (US$ 49.7) per quintal, increased by INR 50 (US$ 0.8) per quintal
• Safflower MSP, raised by INR 200 (US$ 3.3) per quintal, is fixed at INR 3000 (US$ 49) per quintal (Press Information Bureau, 17 October 2013).

COVID-19: Uninterrupted Food grain supplies: Food Corporation of India (FCI) is ensuring uninterrupted supply of wheat and rice throughout the country during the lockdown period. FCI is fully prepared to meet not only the food grain requirement under National Food Security Act (NFSA) @5 KG/Month/Beneficiary but also any additional demand including supply of 5Kg/Person for next 3 months. 
FCI is conducting e-auctions under Open Market Sales Scheme (OMSS) for providing Wheat to the empanelled Roller Flour Mills/State Government to ease the supply constraint in the market.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has approved the implementation of the National Mission on Agricultural Extension and Technology (NMAET) with a total outlay of INR 130.73 billion (US$ 2.13 billion) to restructure and strengthen agricultural extension and enable delivery of appropriate technology and agronomic practices to farmers. This will be achieved by a mix of extensive physical outreach and interactive methods of dissemination of modern technologies, capacity building and institution strengthening to promote mechanization and inputs availability and encourage aggregation of farmers into Interest Groups to form Farmer Producer Organizations. The NMAET is seen as a way to improve and amalgamate several previous schemes of the Department of Agriculture & Cooperation (PIB, 05 February 2014).
Adoption of the Model Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee (APMC) Act by 25 States Union Territories through the amendment of their APMC acts.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved measures to partially deregulate sugar market including (i) the suspension of the Regulated Release Mechanism, (ii) the elimination of the obligation for sugar mills to supply sugar to Public Distribution System (PDS) for sugar produced after September, 2012 (sugar for PDS will be procured by the states through open market) and (iii) the continuation of the fixed retail price policy of INR 13.50 per kg (USD 0.25) under the PDS with the related subsidy for the difference between the retail issue price and the current ex-mill price, provisionally calculated at INR 32 per kg, or USD 0.32 (Press Information Bureau, 05 April 2013).

The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister has given its ex-post facto approval for interest waiver for the two months of November and December, 2016 for farmers accessing short term crop loans from Cooperative Banks. The decision also provides for interest subvention to National Bank for Agricultural and Rural Development (NABARD) on additional refinance by NABARD to Cooperative Banks.
Partial lift of export ban by allowing the export of 300 000 tonnes of non-basmati rice and of 200 000 tonnes of wheat to Bangladesh.

National Policy for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship 2015 supersedes the policy of 2009. The primary objective of this policy is to meet the challenge of skilling at scale with speed, standard (quality) and sustainability. It aims to provide an umbrella framework to all skilling activities being carried out within the country, to align them to common standards and link skilling with demand centres. In addition to laying down the objectives and expected outcomes, the policy also identifies the overall institutional framework which will act as a vehicle to reach the expected outcomes.
Export ban on pulses.

In order to increase availability and access of institutional credit to farmers the government has taken several policy measures (i) setting an annual target for the flow of credit to the agriculture sector of INR 5.75 trillion (USD 103 billion); (ii) implementation of an interest subvention scheme for short-term crop loans up to IND 300,000 (USD 5,300); (iii) advising banks (public and private) to waive security requirements for agricultural loans; and (iv) issuing credit cards (Press Information Bureau, 30 August 2012).
Futures trading banned in wheat.

The target for institutional credit flow to farmers for fiscal year 2012/13 was raised by over 21 percent to INR 5 750 billion (USD 115 billion). A short term Regional Rural Bank Refinance Fund will be set up to enhance the capacity of the Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) to disburse crop loans to small and medium farmers. The government will allocate INR 100 billion (USD 2 billion) to the National Bank for Agricultural and Rural Development (NABARD) for refinancing the RRBs through this fund.

In order to increase the availability of pulses, especially for the people living under the low poverty line, the government has resumed import of pulses (and related subsisides) through State Governments for distribution under Public Distribution System (Press Information Bureau, 22 January 2013).

COVID-19: Ministry of Shipping has now issued specific guidelines to Major Ports on Exemptions/Remissions on penalties, demurrages charges, fee, rentals levied on any Port user for any delay in Berthing/Loading/Unloading operations or evacuation/arrival of cargo caused due to lockdown measures from 22nd March, 2020 to 14th April, 2020.

The Union Cabinet has given its approval for determination of marketing margin for supply of domestic gas to urea and LPG producers. This decision is a structural reform. Currently, different transporters are charging different marketing margins for supply of natural gas. With this decision, there would be uniformity in the marketing margin on domestic gas charged by gas marketers for the regulated sectors, namely, Urea and LPG. There would be a reduction in marketing margin paid by Urea and LPG producers as a result of this decision.

The National Agroforestry Policy, which deals with the practice of integrating trees, crops and livestock on the same plot of land, was launched February 10, the first day of the World Congress on Agroforestry, held in Delhi. The policy, approved by the Cabinet on February 6, deals with problems agroforestry sector is facing at present, including adverse policies, weak markets and a dearth of institutional finance. Agroforestry has the potential to achieve sustainability in agriculture while optimising its productivity and mitigating climate change impact.
National Dairy Development Board is allowed to import 30 000 tonnes of milk powder and 15 000 tonnes of butter oil exempted of duties.

The interest subvention scheme for providing short term crop loans at 7 percent interest will be continued in fiscal year 2012/13 and a 3-percent interest subvention on post-harvest loans up to 6 months will be available to farmers. The existing Kisan Credit Card, an instrument for making agricultural credit available to farmers, will be modified to smart cards that can be used in ATMs.

The Ministry for Rural Development, Sanitation and Drinking Water has approved 28 rural road projects worth INR 438 crores for building roads in Jammu and Kashmir under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojna (PMGSY) programme. A total of 350 Km of rural road network will be built under these projects in proposals for which were submitted by the state government.
Export tax  of 10 percent imposed on bran oil cake in order to discourage export, and  import tariff of 15 percent removed  to increrase domestic availability of cattle feed.

The ban on export of certain edible oils was partially lifted as per the following conditions:  (i) Permission of edible oil exports from Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) to Special Economic Zones (SEZs) to be used for manufacture of processed food products; (ii) Allowing coconut oil exports from all the ports and through Land Customs Stations; (iii) Permission to export edible oils with a Minimum Export Price (MEP) of USD 1500 per tonne, in branded packs of up to 5kg, without any quantitative limit (an Inter-ministerial Committee will be set up to calibrate the MEP from time to time) (Press Information Bureau, 31 January 2013).
Extension of the 15 percent import subsidy on pulses, that was to expire on March 31, until September 30 to augment domestic supplies and ease pressure on prices.

COVID-19: Government has granted relaxation in the nationwide lockdown for activities related to agriculture-farming and allied activities with a view to address problems being faced by the farming community. This will also ensure uninterrupted harvesting of crops. Prime Minister requires the states to think of other platforms for procuring grains apart from APMC, and explore the possibility of creating pooling platforms for rural areas, like that in ride sharing apps, which can be used for this purpose. 
The States and Centre also need to strengthen the lockdown more strictly in some states and must formulate a common exit strategy to ensure staggered re-emergence of population once lockdown ends.

Duty-free import of raw sugar by sugar mills are allowed  until September 2009, under the Advance Authorization Scheme. Duty-free import of white or refined sugar by State companies are allowed up to 1 million tonnes until August 2009, under the Open General License.

During 2011-12, the share of agriculture credit allocated for small farmers in farm loans increased by 45 from a year earlier. The Government has also taken several measures to improve access to credit for small and marginal farmers, by (i) fixing annual targets for improving agricultural credit flow;  (ii) providing crop loans up to IND 300,000 (USD 5,400) at a 4 percent rate per annum; (iii) extending the interest subvention scheme to small and marginal farmers; (iv) facilitating storage in warehouses against negotiable warehouse receipts; (v) providing collateral free loans up to IND 100,000 (USD 1,800) (Press Information Bureau, 23 November 2012).

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has approved the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of sugarcane payable by sugar mills for the 2014-15 marketing season at INR 220 per quintal, marking an increase of INR 10 (UD$ 0.16) over the FRP set in the previous season (PIB, 06 February 2014).
Import tariff of 15 percent  on bran oil cake removed  to increase domestic availability of cattle feed and export tax  of 10 percent imposed in order to discourage export.
Export of  500 000 tonnes of sugar allowed under open general licence (OGL). This normal export quota had been on hold since the beginning of 2011 due to high food inflation.

As per the existing procurement policy, the Central Government extends price support to paddy and wheat through the Food Corporation of India (FCI) and State Agencies. The farmers have the option to sell their produce to FCI/State Agencies at the MSP or in the open market as is advantageous to them. Procurement of coarse grains including maize is being undertaken by State Governments and their agencies under MSP operations. The State Governments retain the quantity procured to the extent of their requirement for the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) and the balance is disposed of by the Food Corporation of India (FCI) through tender (Press Information Bureau, 28 August 2012).

The Ministry of Agriculture and Food Processing Industries developed food processing units, under the Mega Food Park Scheme to provide remunerative price to farmers, reduce food losses, develop producers and processors capacities and create efficient farm to market linkages along the supply chain (Press Information Bureau, 08 March 2013).

Integrated Pest Management is a broad ecological pest control approach aiming at best mix of all known pest control measures to keep the pest population below economic threshold level (ETL). Subsidy is available under the Scheme on various components including Plant Protection Equipments and Biopesticides. Subsidy is also available on IPM demonstrations. Subsidy per farmer or per activity should not exceed 25% of the cost or the present subsidy level approved under the schemes, whichever is lower.

Institutional link: Ministry of Agriculture.
Additional export quota of 74 136 tonnes of wheat flour approved to the Maldives, through bilateral agreement.

On 18 June, the Food Minister announced that 5 million tonnes of rice (milled basis) from government stocks would be released onto the domestic market in a bid to curb price inflation. The move comes to mitigate possible effects of El Niño and reduced monsoon precipitation which could result in a production shortfall and inflationary pressures. The rice will be distributed to Below Poverty Line (BPL) families at subsidized prices and Above Poverty Line (APL) price for July 2014 to March 2015 or till implementation of the National Food Security Act (NFSA) by the respective States whichever is earlier. This will mitigate the problems of the people due to inflation in food prices, particularly in those States/UTs where the NFSA has not been implemented so far (PIB, 02 July 2014).
Export ban on onions, imposed in December following increasing prices, has been lifted but a minimum export price (MEP) of USD 600 per tonne was imposed.

According to a media report, the Finance Ministry excluded milled rice from the “agricultural produce” category and deemed ineligible for exemption of service tax of 12.36 percent. Rice for export will not be taxed on transportation to port of loading (Oryza, 21 January 2014).

The General Council of the National Food Security Mission (NFSM) approved action plans of different States for a total INR 21 billion for 2014/15 (US$ 350 million) to increase national production of oilseeds and pulses. The Council also approved the inclusion of pulses under the NFSM programme in selected States and the conduction of trainings on inter-cropping (food grains with oilseeds) and improved technologies for pulses production in rain-fed areas (PIB, 25 June 2014).

A per reports received from the State Governments, till yesterday, 1,12,545.96 MT pulses seized under de-holding operations have been auctioned or offloaded through other options in the market to increase availability. This will help to moderate the prices further.

COVID-19: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has decided to provide rental waiver to these units housed in STPI premises in the country from 01.03.2020 till 30.06.2020 i.e. for 4 months period as of now. This effort aims to strengthen the e-platforms for normalizing supply chains and is also in the larger interest of around 3,000 IT/ ITeS employees who are directly supported by these units.
Export tax of Rs$ 8,000 (USD 200) per ton is imposed on basmati rice.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs increased the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for 2013-14 season for jute (TD-5 grade) by INR 1000 per tonne (USD 13) to INR 23 000 per tonne (USD 422) (Press information Bureau, 02 April 2013).

The exports of rice and wheat through diplomatic channels to neighboring countries have been suspended. Although the country's food stocks were at a comfortable level, the annual monsoon rains were 19 percent below normal, affecting the planting of summer-sown rice.

COVID-19: On May 12, 2020, the government announced a special COVID-19 economic relief package of INR 20 trillion (USD 263 billion), equivalent to almost 10 percent of India’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP). Instead of extending short term fiscal relief to the Indian farm sector, the agricultural portion of the package includes long-term measures to address some critical infrastructure gaps and strengthen credit supplies, and proposes long-pending policy reforms that should, over time, significantly help Indian farmers.
Non-basmati rice exports completely banned.

The Union Cabinet has approved a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), which has been signed in October, 2015, between Indian and Germany, to expand bilateral development cooperation in the field of Solar Energy by increasing use of solar energy in India through technical as well as financial cooperation. The MoU would lead to cooperation in the field of solar rooftops; the development of solar parks or solar zones (if possible in close proximity to the Green Energy Corridors financed by KfW under Indo-German Financial Cooperation) and solar off-grid applications to improve the access to clean and sustainable energy.

Accident insurance coverage of Rs  25,000 per grower is provided under the price stabilization fund scheme (PSF) under the Janata Personal Accident Insurance from United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Entire premium has been paid by PSF.
Futures trading banned in chickpeas.

To curb soaring onions prices, the National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation (NAFED) will import onion for domestic consumption and procure 4 to 5 tonnes onion per day from mandis of Rajasthan to supply it through its retail outlets in Delhi. In addition, the agency will procure onion from mandis of Lasalgaon/Pimpalgaon (Maharashtra) at best prevailing rates to offer it to all the State marketing and supply federations at a nominal service charge of 2 percent (Press Information Bureau, 14 August 2013).

The Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) programme will be modified  in during the 12th Fine Year Plan  by including three main focuses: (i) production growth for increasing production and productivity; (ii) development of agricultural infrastructure and assets; and (iii) specific interventions and sub-schemes. The 20 percent of the annual outlay will be earmarked budget will be allocated for the sub-schemes and the 40 percent each  for production growth and infrastructure development respectively (Press Information Bureau, 19 March 2013).

Import ban on milk and milk products from China has been extended for six months until June 24, 2012. The ban includes milk, milk products and food preparations with milk originated in China. The prohibition on import of milk and its products from China was originally imposed on 24 September 2008, following reports that the milk products imported from China contain melamine – a banned substance injurious to health. The ban was extended since then time to time.
Minimum export price (MPE) on non- basmati rice increased from US$450 to US$500 per metric ton.

COVID-19: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare held a video conference with the exporters to identify the problems and initiate necessary steps by making meaningful interventions to help them sustain though the current Covid-19 crisis. Exporters, representatives of Associations of producers/exporters of agri commodities namely, Fruits, Vegetables, Basmati and Non-basmati Rice, Seeds, Flowers, Plants, Organic produce, Agriculture Equipment and Machinery participated in the meeting. 
The common issues highlighted by exporters of all agri commodities related to availability and movement of labour, inter-state transport bottlenecks, shortage of raw materials due to closure of Mandis, phyto-sanitary certification, closure of courier services thereby hampering movement of shipping documents, availability of freight services, access to ports/yards and clearance of goods for imports/exports. Transportation and online certificate will be supported.

The Union Cabinet has given its approval for signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between India and Israel in the field of water resources management and development cooperation. 
The bilateral cooperation will benefit both the countries in strengthening the techniques in efficient use of water, micro-irrigation, recycling/re-use of waste water, desalination, aquifer recharge and in-situ water conservation techniques. A Joint Working Group shall be formed to monitor the activities to be carried out in fulfilment of the MoU.

COVID-19: The government notified a decrease in the basic import duty on lentils for all origins, except the United States, from 30 to 10 percent until August 31, 2020. The basic import duty on lentils from the United States has been lowered from 50 to 30 percent. The government also announced imports of 200,000 metric tons of pigeon peas and other pulses from Mozambique, under the Memorandum of Understanding between the two governments for the Indian fiscal year 2020/21 (AprilMarch) outside the quota limits announced for the select four pulses for other origins.
National anaemia control programme distributes 100gr. tablets of iron and folic acid to pregnant and lactating women and children

The Weekly Iron Folic Acid Supplementation Programme for Adolescents (WIFS) will be launched nationwide on 17 July 2013, covering adolescent population aged 10 to 19 years, for a total 130 million beneficiaries. The key features of WIFS are: (i) administration of supervised Weekly Iron Folic Acid Supplements of 100mg elemental iron and 500mg folic acid, (ii) screening of target groups for moderate/severe anemia and referring these cases to an appropriate health facility, (iii) biannual de-working (Albendazole 400mg), six months apart, for control of helminthes infestation and (iv) information and counseling for improving dietary intake and prevention of intestinal worm infestation (Press Information bureau, 15 July 2013).

According to a media report, the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) recommended an increase in the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for paddy from the summer’s (Kharif) crop beginning in July, from the current price of INR 1 310 per 100kg (US$ 218 per tonne) to INR 1 360 per 100kg (US $226 PMT). In the past, the government has tended to implement the CACP recommendations on MSP. A final decision will be made after the general elections; voting will take place 7 April-12 May (Oryza, 31 March 2014).

In an effort to boost production of the 2012 Kharif season crops, the minimum support prices (MSP) were incresed:  for common grade paddy by 15% to USD 235/tonne , for soyabeans by 33% to USD 394/tonne, for sunflowerseeds by 32% to USD 667/tonne, for maize by 20% to USD 212/tonne, and for sorghum by 53% to USD 270/tonne. The new MEPs apply to the period July 2012 through June 2013.

The stock-holding limit on sugar, edible oils and pulses for traders and wholesale dealers is extended untill September to control inflation. The measure was first introduced in 2006 to prevent hoarding and to facilitate state procurement.
On 19 August 2014, India announced that all State Governments had been directed to cap the levy on rice procurements from millers at 25 percent for the Marketing Year 2014/15 (October/September).

The Union Cabinet has given its approval to sign Memoranda of Understanding (MOU) on the Conservation of Migratory Birds of Prey in Africa and Eurasia, also called the 'Raptor MOU' with the Convention on Conservation of Migratory Species (CMS). With the signing of this MOU, India will become the 54th signatory to the MOU.

A  contingency plan is launched to boost pulses production in the coming Rabi season to offset losses in the previous Kharif season. The plan targets an additional output of 2.78 million tonnes of pulses such as pigeon pea, gram, pea and lentil by expanding area and enhancing productivity. As part of the  plan, the Government has made an additional allocation of Rs 800 million (USD 17.3 million), under the National Food Security Mission-Pulses programme, to 12 States including Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.

A new SMS portal for farmers, the Kisaan SMS Portal, will be launched on 16 July 2013, aimed to provide information, advisories and services through SMS to more than 120 million farmers across the country and enable them to take informed decisions relating to different aspects of farming including crop production and marketing, animal husbandry, dairying and fisheries (Press Information bureau, 11 July 2013).
Export ban on non-basmati rice is replaced by a minimum export price (MEP) of USD 450 per metric tonne, subsequently  increased to USD 500 per tonne on December 27, 2007.

A new tool, the Food Product Approval System (FPAS) has been launched by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to allow companies to apply online to seek approval for new food product imports.

The Indian government has designed contingency plans for dealing with El Nino, likely to cause poor monsoon rains. All the States are advised to maintain buffer stocks of food grains, including rice, and to keep aside 10 percent of agricultural funds for undertaking appropriate interventions in case of a drought-like situation They should also initiate mitigation measures such as promotion of soil moisture conservation methods and restoration of irrigation infrastructure. The Department of Agriculture and the multi-departmental Crop Weather Watch Group are regularly monitoring rainfall, area under sowing, water storage and input availability at district level (PIB, 09 June 2014).

The State Governments implemented a centrally sponsored scheme via a decentralized and demand driven extension mechanism called Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA) in 614 districts of 28 States and 3 Union Territories to support extension system and introduction of new agricultural technologies in different agro-climatic conditions. In some cases, extension activities are provided in partnership with the private sector (Press Information Bureau, 01 March 2013).

On 1 June, India increased the minimum support price (MSP) of some basic 2020/21 kharif crops. The MSP was increased by 3 percent for paddy rice to INR 1 186 per 100 kg (USD 157 per tonne), by 5 percent for maize to INR 1 850 per 100 kg (USD 245 per tonne), and by 5 percent for soybeans to 3 880 per 100 kg (USD 513.8 per tonne).

The National Wildlife Action Plan 2002-2016 and Wildlife Conservation Strategy were adopted in January, 2002 for strengthening and enhancement of the protected area network based on scientific management. Identification of endangered species of flora and fauna and their effective conservation is a priority area under the strategy. This plan highlights the role of local communities in participatory conservation.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has approved the continuation of the “Sustainable and Inclusive Development of Natural Rubber Sector” scheme with an outlay of INR 9.6 billion (156.8 million) in the 12th Plan (2012-17). The main objective of the scheme is to enhance natural rubber production and productivity through expanding planted area, accelerating rubber plantation development programmes in non-traditional regions, intensifying research to evolve appropriate technologies and extension services (PIB, 12 February 2013).
Minimum price export (MPE) on basmati rice increased from US$ 1,100 to US$ 1,200 per metric ton.

Since the new government has taken office, the following key developments have taken place in the Ministry of Food Processing: 1. Special fund of INR 2000 crore set up in NABARD to provide affordable credit to agro-processing units (announced in the budget 2014-15), 2. Reduction in excise duty from 10 to 6 percent for food processing machinery (budget 2014-15) 3. A new help desk “Investors Portal” has been set up to assist the prospective investors/entrepreneurs to facilitate investments in the Food Processing sector. 4. Skill Development initiative taken by the Ministry in consultation with National Skill Development Council and  identified 7 sectors ( Bakery, Dairy, Grain Processing, Poultry, Refrigeration, Packaging, Quality Control) with the help of reputed industry partners to train 10 000 people in the next 12 months. 5. E monitoring of National Mission on Food Processing (NMFP) - Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched.  6. Five Mega Food Parks approved in the states of Bihar, Maharashtra, Himachal Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. 7. Twenty new cold chain projects been sanctioned.

On June 28, 2013, the government announced the minimum support prices (MSP) for the kharif crops of the upcoming crop year 2013/14.  MSP for paddy rice has been raised by about 5 percent over last year to INR 13 100 per tonne (USD 217), while MSPs for maize and pigeon pea have been raised by over 11 percent to INR 13 100 (USD 217) and 43 000 (USD 700) respectively.
Partial lif of  the ban on rice exports by allowing exports of  one million tonnes of non basmati rice, subject to a minimum export price of USD 400/tonne.

On 3 December 2009, the Food Ministry decided to end a concession that had effectively reduced the basmati rice export floor price. Foreign commission of 12.5% which was included in the calculation of the minimum export price (MEP) was to be withdrawn.

A budget allocation of Rs. 142.00 crore has been provided for the Biogas Programme for the current year, 2016-17. A target of 1,00,000 biogas plants has been fixed for the current year.The family type biogas plants generate clean gaseous fuel particularly for cooking and meeting lighting needs and replaces use of fuel wood, avoid cutting of trees thereby reducing pressure on forests. Biogas plants help in reducing emission of Green House Gases (GHGs).

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the allocation of 5 million of food grains (rice and wheat) to States/ Union Territories (UTs) during 2013-14 to meet requirements for Below Poverty Line (BPL) families. This additional allocation will remain valid for lifting up to 31st March, 2014 or till the National Food Security Bill is passed by Parliament and implemented in the respective States/UTs. The estimated subsidy on the additional allocation at BPL prices will be INR 947.122 (USD 15.5 million) million (Press Information Bureau, 17 July 2013)

The Prime Minister (PM) created an Executive Committee on Climate Change to focus on: (i) Assisting the PM’s Council on Climate Change  on issues relating to climate change at the national level; (ii) monitoring the implementation of the eight national missions and other initiatives on climate change; (iii) advising the PM’s Council on Climate Change on modifications in the objectives, strategies and structure of the missions; (iv) co-ordinating with various agencies on climate change-related issues (Press Information Bureau, 31 January 2013).
India and China signed a series of memorandum of understandings to promote trade of buffalo meat, fisheries, feed and feed ingredients and address the growing trade deficit.
The Government of India is for the third time extending the deadline to implement the National Food Security Act (NFSA) by an additional 6 months.

The Government of India approved strengthening and restructuring the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) with special focus on pregnant and lactating mothers and children under three, through strengthening care and nutrition counseling services and care of severely underweight children, improving Supplementary Nutrition Programme including cost revision and provision for additional Nutrition Counselors, among others. The restructured ICDS will be rolled out in three phases with focus on the 200 high burden districts for malnutrition during 2012-13 and additional 200 districts in 2013-14  and including districts from the special category States and NER and the remaining districts in 2014-15 (Press Information Bureau, 22 February 2013).
Duty free imports for maize.

The government of the India's Eastern state Odisha has approved for large scale hybrid seed production under the Central government's Rashtriya Krishi Vikash Yojna (RKVY) scheme. The State is  keen on enhancing hybrid rice seed  to help boost rice productivity. The government will invite private seed companies to produce hybrid rice seeds in the state while it would encourage farmers to take part in the hybrid rice seed production by providing them subsidies of about INR 20 000 per hectare (around US$325). The government is planning to introduce this scheme in about 12,000 hectares for the upcoming Rabi season (November - March).
Basmati rice exports are restricted only to Kandla, Kakinada, Kolkata, JNPT Mumbai, Mundra and Pipavav ports.
Export ban for wheat and wheat products has been re-imposed due to food inflation concerns. However the GOI permitted exports of 650,000 tons of wheat through March 2010.

COVID-19: Indian Railways have worked tirelessly since 28th March 2020 to provide hot cooked meals to needy people after the lockdown due to COVID-19. Indian Railways crosses 2 million mark in distribution of free meals during lockdown at approximately 300 locations across the country to thousands of people everyday.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has approved the implementation of the National Mission on Oilseeds and Oil Palm (NMOOP) during the 12th Plan Period with financial allocation of INR 35.07 billion (US$ 1.12 billion). The objective of the scheme is to enhance production of oilseeds by 6.58 million tonnes and bring additional area of 125 000 hectares under oil palm cultivation with increased productivity of fresh fruit bunches and collection of tree borne oilseeds. The implementation strategy places emphasis on increasing the Seed Replacement Ratio (SRR) with focus on varietal replacement, increasing irrigation coverage under oilseeds from 26 percent to 38 percent, diversification of area from low yielding cereals crops to oilseeds crops,  inter-cropping of oilseeds, increasing availability of quality planting materials among others (Press Information Bureau, 03 October 2013).
Partially lift of the  wheat exports ban by allowing  the export  of 100 000 tonnes of wheat  to Afghanistan, through bilateral agreements.
Cotton  Corporation of India (CCI) decided to intervene to tackle weak cotton prices by beginning the procurement under minimum support price (MSP) operations.
The basmati rice minimum export price (MEP) had been reduced to IDR 41 400/tonne (about USD 900),  from the previous USD 1 100.

The Government adopted several measures to increase institutional credit flow and improve small and marginal farmers access to credit. Among them, (i) the fixation of annual targets of agricultural credit flow, (ii) provision of crop loans up to INR 300 000 (USD 5 500) at 4 percent per annum to farmers respecting repayment schedule fixed by banks, and (iii) extension of interest subvention scheme under the “Kisan Credit Card” to small and marginal farmers for production storage (Press Information Bureau, 08 March 2013).

The National Policy for Farmers (NPF) (2007) aims to improve economic viability of farming and increase net income of farmers. Policy provisions in NPF-2007 include, inter-alia, asset reforms in respect of land, water, livestock, fisheries and bio-resources; supply of good quality seeds and disease-free planting material, issue of soil health passbooks to the farmers and integrated pest management system; region and crop specific implements and machinery; support services for women; timely, adequate and easy reach of institutional credit at reasonable interest rates and farmer-friendly insurance instruments; support services and inputs like application of frontier technologies; agricultural bio-security system; use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) and setting up of farm schools to revitalize agricultural extension; coverage of farmers under a comprehensive national social security scheme; effective implementation of Minimum Support Price (MSP) across the country and establishing community foodgrain banks; development of agricultural market infrastructure and terminal markets for agriculture; curriculum reforms in agricultural universities; special categories of farming like organic farming and contract farming; rural non-farm employment initiative for farm households; and integrated approach for rural energy, etc.

The Food Corporation of India reportedly does not have a robust procurement mechanism in these states and often forces farmers to go for a distress sale. In order to avoid such a situation and help farmers receive the minimum support price (MSP), the Food Ministry has decided to involve private players in the rice procurement process. As per the new directive, private players would buy paddy from various clusters (of farmers) identified by the respective state governments and deliver the custom milled rice (CMR) to the FCI or state government-owned agency godowns. A cluster would be formed wherever there is a possibility of procuring about 100,000 tons of rice (paddy equivalent) and covering about 500 to 1,000 hectares of land. Private parties are allowed to open as many purchase centers as possible in the allotted cluster.

The Union Cabinet approved a centrally sponsored scheme for the marketing of Minor Forest Produce (MFP) and development of a value chain through public purchase of the MFP at a minimum support price. The measure will ensure remunerative prices, social safety and alternative employment avenues for the MFP gatherers and forest dweller who are primarily tribal population (Press Information Bureau, 02 August 2013).

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved the export of additional 2.5 million tonnes of wheat from central pool stocks of the Food Corporation of India (FCI) as per the following, subject to the floor price of USD 300 per  tonne, to be completed by June, 2013. The measure will make available more space for storage of foodgrains in the godowns of FCI (Press Information Bureau, 26 December 2013).

In order to lay special emphasis on farm mechanization and to bring more inclusiveness, a dedicated Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization has been proposed for the XII Plan (2012-17) with an estimated outlay of INR 2000 crores for the entire plan period. It will provide assistance for promotion and strengthening of agricultural mechanization through training, testing and demonstration, post-harvest technology and management; establishment of farm machinery banks for hiring (PIB, 23 August 2013)

The Food Safety and Standards Regulation

In August 2015, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India revised the maximum permitted amount of trans fat content in edible fats and oils, including hydrogenated vegetable oils, margarine and fat spreads, from 10% to 5%. Amendments were made to the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additive) Regulation, 2011 and the new 5% limit came into effect on 27 February 2017.

Import tariff of 5 percent on onions suspended, arrangements for new imports and ban on exports until January 15, 2011. In addition, the Government eliminated the 4 percent countervailing duty on onions.

COVID-19: India will spend INR 35 billion to provide free food grain rations to nearly 80 million migrant workers over the next two months. The measure is aimed to support workers affected by the Covid-19 induced lockdown.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the extension of government guarantee of INR 17.81 billion (USD 330 million) along with waiver of one percent guarantee fees to enable the National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED) and Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) to undertake price support operations for procurement of oil seeds, pulses and cotton (Press Information Bureau, 02 May 2013).

The Strategy lays down a roadmap for effective action, among both implementers and practitioners, in achieving the national nutrition objectives. The National Nutrition Strategy is committed to ensuring that every child, adolescent girl and woman attains optimal nutritional status- especially those from the most vulnerable communities. The focus is on preventing and reducing undernutrition across the life cycle- as early as possible, especially in the first three years of life. This commitment also builds on the recognition that the first few years of life are forever - the foundation for ensuring optimum physical growth, development, cognition and cumulative lifelong learning.
The nutrition strategy envisages a framework wherein the four proximate determinants of nutrition - uptake of health services, food, drinking water and sanitation and income and livelihoods – work together to accelerate decline of under nutrition in India. The National Nutrition Strategy will contribute to key national development goals for more inclusive growth, such as the reduction of maternal, infant and young child mortality, through its focus on the following targets
•	To prevent and reduce undernutrition (underweight prevalence) in children (0- 3 years) by 3 percentage points per annum.
•	To reduce the prevalence of anemia among young children, adolescent girls and women in the reproductive age group (15- 49 years) by 30%.

The New Food Security Law proposed and under approval will create a legal entitlement to subsidize food grains for 63.5 percent of India’s population, whith an annual cost about INR 1 trillion (USD 20 billion) starting in FY 2012. This amount compares to current outlays of INR 670 billion. Total annual deliveries under the Public Distribution System are projected to rise from 39 million tonnes to nearly 64 million tonnes. Additionally budget (about USD 70 million) allocated to boost agricultural production and to improve storage and transportation infrastructure.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs fixed the fair and remunerative price of sugarcane payable by sugar mills for 2013-14 marketing season, at INR 2,100 (USD 39) per tonne (Press Information Bureau, 31 January 2013).

Plan to release 5 million tonnes of wheat and rice from government reserves , under the Open Market Scheme starting from July, to sell about 5 million tonnes of wheat and rice at below market prices. This is in order to offload cereals from warehouses and mitigate domestic food inflation.
Development of marine fisheries: Subsidy to poor fishermen for motorizing their traditional craft, which increases the fishing areas and frequency of operation.

According to a media report, India’s Southern State of Andhra Pradesh is planning to offer high quality rice at subsidized rates through fair price shops (FPS) to make rice affordable for consumers. Government has already begun providing high quality rice in the capital city of Hyderabad at around INR 30 per kilo (US$ 0.5), 40 percent lower than the current market price of around INR 50 per kilo (US$ 0.8) (Oryza, 8 October 2013).

The Union Cabinet approved the implementation of the multi-sectoral programme in the 12th Five Year Plan, to address the maternal and child under-nutrition in 200 high burden districts. The objective is to bring coherence within nutrition interventions and include specific pro-nutrition actions in different national and sub-national programmes. The programme focuses in particular on the (i) prevention and reduction in child under-nutrition (underweight prevalence in children under 3 years of age) and (ii) reduction in levels of anemia among young children, adolescent girls and women (Press Information Bureau, 24 September 2013).

COVID-19: Extension of Lockdown up to May 31, 2020. National Directives for COVID-19 Management continue to be in force throughout the Country. Night Curfew to continue to remain in force from 7.00pm to 7.00am. States to decide various zones and activities to be allowed reopen. Local shops and markets reopen with maximum serving 5 persons at the same time.

The government has allocated INR 1.15 trillion (US$ 19.1 billion) for food subsidies in its 2014/15 budget to ensure wheat and rice price subsidies to the country’s most vulnerable populations. The allocation includes a provision of INR 885 billion (US$ 14.7 billion) for implementation of the National Food Security Act (NFSA) and INR 45 billion (US$ 478 million) for subsidizing sugar. Under the NFSA each eligible person can purchase 5 kilos of cereals per month at INR 3, 2 and 1 per kilo of rice (US$ 0.05, 0.03, 0.02), wheat and millet respectively.
The minimum support price for the 2012 wheat crop, about to be planted, has been increased  by some  10 percent  to INR 12 850/tonne (USD 258/tonne) for 2012/13 marketing year (April/March).

India’s Ministry of Finance has approved the sale of 2 million tonnes of rice buffer stocks under the Open Market Sale Scheme (OMSS) to bulk buyers, including millers and traders, through e-auctions starting in April 2015.
The minimum support price for the 2011  "kharif" season soyabeans has been increased  by 17.4 percent to INR 1690/100kg (USD 376/tonne) for the 2011-12 marketing year (October/September).

In March 2016, Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare launched Project ‘Clean Street Food’. The project of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) aims at to raise the safety standards of foods sold on streets across the capital city of New Delhi by training 20 000 roadside vendors on aspects of health and hygiene, in the first phase.

The Government of India introduced additional input subsidies in response to drought: (i) Diesel subsidy scheme, that provides 50 percent of the cost of diesel for supplementary and protective irrigation will be provided as financial assistance to farmers; and an (ii) Enhanced subsidy scheme, ceiling on seeds subsidy is enhanced for cereals, pulses and oilseeds under on-going schemes (Press Information Bureau, 31 August 2012).

The Government of India has instituted a High-Level Committee to provide recommendations for restructuring the Food Corporation of India (FCI) to ensure the efficient management of food grain reserves and reduce costs. FCI has vital responsibilities, such as grains procurement, management of Central Pool stocks and distribution of food grains to State Government Agencies for food security programmes.
Despite the export ban in place, an export quota of 150 000 tonnes of three premium non-basmati rice varieties  has been allowed,  subject to a minimum export price of USD 850/tonne.

The National Livestock Policy (2013) has been formulated to have a policy framework for improving productivity of the livestock sector in a sustainable manner, taking into account the provisions of the National Policy of Farmers (2007) and the recommendations of the stakeholders, including the States. The National Livestock Policy aims at increasing livestock productivity and production in a sustainable manner, while protecting the environment, preserving animal bio-diversity, ensuring bio-security and farmers’ livelihood.

India prepared an addendum in 2014 to the National Biodiversity Action Plan (NBAP) 2008 consisting of 12 national biodiversity targets developed within the framework of the Aichi Biodiversity Targets. These national targets are mapped to the achievement of the latter as well as complemented by indicators and a monitoring framework.
This notification is made under the Biological Diversity Act 2002, notifying the species of plants and animals which are on the verge of extinction.

Under recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP), the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs announced the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) of some agricultural commodities for the next marketing season. MSP of cotton has been increased for medium staple from INR 3 600 to INR 3 700 (US$ 59.6) per quintal and for long staple from INR 3 900 to INR 4000 (US$ 64.5) per quintal in 2013-14. MSP for copra for the 2014 season is retained at the level of the previous year of INR 5 250 per quintal or US$ 84.6 (milling copra) and INR 5 500, or US$ 88.6 per quintal (ball copra). Jute MSP is set at INR 2 400 per quintal (US$ 38.7), up INR 100 per quintal over the last season (Press Information Bureau, 10 December 2013).

The Government of India (GOI) notified its Draft Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Amendment Regulations, 2016, regarding standards for fortified milk and edible lactose to the World Trade Organization (WTO). The comment period deadline for trading partners is May 15, 2016.

On March 19, the Indian Cabinet approved the amendments to the National Food Security Bill, including: (i) simplification to a single category of food distribution beneficiaries, constituting 75 percent of the rural population and 50 percent of the urban population, (ii) reduction of the food grain entitlement from 7 to 5 kilograms of grain per capita, (iii) delegation of powers to identify, implement the system to the state governments (a proposed National Food Commission will not be instituted), (iii) uniform subsidized prices for rice, wheat, and coarse grains (millet) of INR 3, 2, and 1 per kilogram respectively, will be applied for the first three years then they will be linked “suitably” to the Minimum Support Price (MSP). The estimated food grain requirement for the act is 61.23 million tonnes at a cost of about INR 1.247 trillion (USD 23.1 billion), implying an increase of INR 238 billion (USD 4.4 billion) over the current expenditures.

The government of India has decided to restrict rice seeds exports. It will now allow seed-quality rice exports with licence permits. The Director General of Foreign Trade reportedly noted in the statement that exports will be permitted under licence subject to certain conditions such as submission of proof of dealer in seeds; declaration that the export consignment of seeds has been chemically treated and is not fit for human consumption. Export packets have to be labelled with the above declaration.

COVID-19: Transportation of essential items like medical supplies, medical equipment, food, etc. in small parcel sizes is going to be very important during the lockdown in the wake of COVID19.  In order to fill in this vital need, Indian Railways has made railway parcel vans available for quick mass transportation across the nation.

Under the Rural Connectivity Investment Programme, the Government will construct 3 461 km of all-weather rural roads in the five States, benefiting nearly 1 600 rural households by December, 2015. In addition, it will  improve the capacity of implementing agencies through rural connectivity training and research centers and rural roads network management units (Press information Bureau, 02 April 2013).

The Ministry of Human Resources Development will implement a system to monitor the Mid Day Meal school feeding scheme on a daily basis, through latest communication system, the Inter Voice Response System. Every school will upload data and details on children receiving food on a timely manner (Press Information Bureau 19 June 2013).

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved continue the ban on export of edible oils with certain exemptions effective from 1 October 2012 till further orders (Public Information Bureau, 4 October 2012).

To support edible oil prices for farmers (oil palm), the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) decided to (i) increase on import duties for crude edible oils from 0 to 2.5 percent; and (ii) maintain the import duties for refined edible oils (7.5 percent). The implementation of these measures is expected to reflect in a oil palm price at INR 150 (USD 2.7) per MT.
(Press Information Bureau, 17 January 2013).
Export ban on skimmed milk powder lifted. The product is also included in the export promotion measures  which provide a  duty credit  of 5 percent of the FOB value of the exports.
Export ban on non-basmati rice; exports under food aid programmes exempted from ban.

The government is creating additional storage capacity for food grains. However is not considering involving the private sector for the procurement of food grains. Yet, the government formulated the Private Entrepreneurs’ Guarantee (PEG) Scheme for construction of storage god owns through private entrepreneurs, Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) and State Warehousing Corporations (SWCs). A series of meetings of the High Level Committee (HLC) under the PEG Scheme have been held to review the requirement and creation of additional storage capacity for different states. So far, the High Level Committee has approved a total capacity of 181.08 LMT under this scheme in 19 States (Press Information Bureau, 14 August 2012).

Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana project, launched during 2007-08 , with the objective to boost agriculture production from a state level perspective. This scheme incentives states to increase public investment in Agriculture and allied sectors. The goal is to achieve at least 4.1% growth in agriculture by the end of XI Plan and, additionally, to maximize returns to the farmers.
Non- basmati exports are banned.

Food Corporation of India (FCI) has supplied 16 500 packets of rice in 10 kg for distribution in flood affected regions of Jammu & Kashmir on the request of State Government. So far, 21 000 tone rice offtake has been reported this month.

COVID-19: Government of India issues Orders prescribing lockdown for containment of COVID-19 Epidemic in the country. The Order shall remain in force, in all parts of the country, for a period of 21 days with effect from 25.03.2020.

The priorities set in the Strategy for Doubling Farmers Income by 2022 represent the key overarching framework for the agriculture sector. The main objective of the government is to double farmers’ income by solving the twin problems of maximising efficiency and ensuring equity in a sustainable manner. These objectives will be met through diversification into high value fruits and vegetables, increased participation of private players, improved agriculture marketing at state levels, and policy reforms related to leasing. The government is also focussing on boosting productivity through increased adoption of scientifically proven and sustainable agriculture practices such as introduction of improved varieties, integrated soil management, promotion of organic farming and efficient water management practices.
An Inter-ministeral Committee was set up to implement the Strategy. The Committee has identified seven sources of income growth namely, improvement in crop productivity; improvement in livestock productivity; resource use efficiency or savings in the cost of production; increase in the cropping intensity; diversification towards high value crops; improvement in real prices received by farmers; and shift from farm to non-farm occupations. However, the discussion on new programs and initiatives to effective implementation of the strategy is still being under discussion.

COVID-19:  Department of Fertilizers is closely monitoring the production, movement and availability of Fertilizers in the country to ensure sufficiency of ferilisers to the farmers. The interventions at highest level in Department is ensuring required availability of fertilisers to the farmers across India.

On June 11 2013, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India extended the import prohibition on milk and milk products from China for an additional year, until June 22 2014 (USDA Gain Report, 12 June 2013).

Various measures to boost agricultural productivity  with the aim to moderate food inflation. These include: increase of credit subventions (effective interest rate of 4% ),  allocation of USD 87 million to promote vegetable production in urban centers, of USD 65 million  to promote pulses in rainfed areas and of USD 65 million to promote palm oil production.
Export ban on maize lifted.

COVID-19: On 14 April 2020, The government has decided to extend the nationwide lockdown up to 3rd May. 
On 25 March 2020, The Ministry of Home Affairs has written to the States/UTs to guide that the transportation/interstate movement of animal feed and fodder has been exempted as an essential service, from the restrictions under Disaster Management Act, 2005

National iodine deficiency disorders control programme (NIDDCP)' tasks are focused on coordination, technical guidance, training and monitoring procurement and distribution of demand and supply of iodated salt.

Partial lift of the wheat export ban, by allowing an export quota of 650 000 tons of wheat products, including flour and semolina until 31 March 2012.

The government has been providing relief of two percentage points in the interest rate on the principal amount up to Rs.$ 1 lakh on each crop loan granted by commercial banks during Kharif and rabi on 2005-06. Government of India had provided Rs.$ 1100 crore for reimbursing the claims submitted by Banks in this regard. This subvention is available on condition that the banks make available short-term credit at ground level at 7 per cent per annum.
Export ban on milk powders, casein, and casein products in an effort to control rising milk prices.

National Scheme of Welfare of Fishermen - Provision of land for development  houses, drinking water and commonplace for recreation and work. The plinth area and cost of construction of a house would be limited to 35 Sq. mts. And Rs.S40,000/- respectively.

The minimum support price  of wheat for marketing year 2011/12 (April/March) increased by 4.5 percent to 11 700 rupees (USD 264) per tonne. The measure aims to support farmers' income following a bumper harvest.

According to a media report, the government has developed a contingency plan for over 500 districts of the country to help overcome crop losses during the main (Kharif) rice crop season (June - December) in the event of weather disturbances. The plan envisages rainfall and soil map for each district and action points for different levels of rainfall deficiency or excess or other weather-related contingencies, such as cyclone or flood. States are also tasked to stock adequate seeds of short-duration crops, ensure timely availability of fertilizers and provide sufficient credit to farmers (Oryza, 28 February 2014).
Additional 5 million tonnes of wheat and rice will be provided through state-run welfare programmes at subsidised prices by March 2012.

The government will import 100 000 tonnes of rice from Myanmar for public distribution in the north-eastern states of Manipur and Mizoram, despite having abundant central stocks. Moving rice domestically from other states, such as Punjab or Andhra Pradesh, by road has proven costlier than importing it. This is the first time in three decades India is importing rice.

During 2011-12 the Central Government implemented a scheme on Vegetables Initiative for Urban Clusters (VIUC) within the overall Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) Scheme. The Scheme covers all aspects relating to formation of farmer's association/groups, training/capacity building of farmers, linking farmers group with aggregators/markets, vegetable production under supply to urban centers starting from planting material to marketing to retail level. In addition, several States have promoted farmers-consumers markets to to facilitate the farmers to sell their products to direct consumers and reducing intermediations and marketing costs (Press Information Bureau, 8 March 2013).

On July 8, 2013, the Government raised the import duties for raw and refined sugar from 10 percent to 15 percent in an effort to protect domestic sugar prices and to help millers clear their debts to farmers (USDA, 23 October 2013)

The Food Corporation of India allocated additional wheat  (5 MMT) and rice (5 MMT) to retail consumers through State/UT governments and national cooperatives under the Open Market Sale  Scheme (OMSS) to increase its availability in the market and moderate prices. An additional amount of 6.5 MMT of wheat has been allocated for tender sales to major consumers/traders (Press Information Bureau, 10 November 2012).

In order to provide relief to the consumers, the Government has launched sales wheat flour under the Kendriya Bhandar brand at subsidised prices of INR 144.5 (USD 2.6) per 10 kg. Kendriya Bhandar is central-sponsored Welfare Project that moderates prices of essential commodities for the welfare of consumers. The Department of Food and Public Distribution, has released wheat under Open Market Sale (OMS) Scheme to Kendriya Bhandar for this purpose, which are sold at Minimum Support Prices (MSP) respectively (Press Information Bureau, Government of India, 23 May 2012).

Government subsidized maize exports by imposing a 5 percent duty credit scrip on the "free on board" (f.o.b.) value of exports under a special agricultural product scheme: the Vishesh Krishi Upaj Yojana (VKUY).

Development and Strengthening of Infrastructure Facilities for Production and distribution of Quality Seeds Scheme. Its objective is to distribute seeds at 50 percent of the cost. User charges for BPL (Below Poverty Line) are Rs$20 a month while for non-BLP are Rs$60 a month.

Export ban on pulses imposed in June 2006, and due to expired on March 31,  extended by one more year untill March 2012.
Farm support for losses during extreme weather events has been increased for Indian farmers. Small and marginal farmers will receive more financial support, according to a government's  announcement.

The scheme aims to streamline the cooperatives marketing structure, capacity building and manpower development, enabling cooperatives to have storage/cold storage facilities and supporting their activities in related areas such as dairy, poultry and fishery among other sectors (Press Information Bureau, 12 December 2013).

The merging is expected to leverage their combined assets and capital for increased production of quality seeds for a larger number of farmers (Press Information Bureau, 26 December 2013).

According to Oryza, the eastern state of West Bengal will provide financial support to enterprises interested to build about 165 new rice mills expected to begin functioning in 2014. The local government will cover the 25 percent of the expenses or about INR 5.5 – 8 million (US$ 87 000 - 126 000) for the construction of the new mills that will reduce transportation costs and post harvest losses (Oryza, 11 November 2013).

the government of India issued the Guidelines on Access to Biological Resources and Associated Knowledge and Benefits Sharing Regulations, 2014, which implements the Biological Diversity Act 2002.
