Under the FIELDS Programme, since 2001, an amount of PHP 79.7 billion has been released for the restoration and rehabilitation of national and communal irrigation systems nationwide, generating 140,042 hectares of new areas. A total of 1,480,826 hectares located in the four super regions were also restored and rehabilitated.

The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) has approved the release of a combined PHP 1.92 billion to the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) and the Department of Agriculture (DA) for flood control intervention though investments in public infrastructure , including rehabilitation and construction of flood-control systems and farm-to-market road projects to provide better accessibility for farmers’ products (Department of Budget and Management, 25 March 2013).

The Department of Agriculture increased by 61 percent the budget in 2011 to PHP 48.7 billion (USD 1.1 billion), in order to increase coconut production in the next 3 years. The majority of the 2012 budget will be used for improving rural infrastructure including irrigation, farm-to-market roads, and post-harvest facilities. The Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA),has  allocated PHP 838 million (USD 19.5 million) to fund its planting/replanting efforts and PHP 502 million (USD 11.7 million) for its fertilization program in 2012.

The Department of Agriculture (DA) targets an additional 64,170 hectares planted to hybrid rice this year to offset projected production losses from the El Nino. These additional areas that will be planted to hybrid rice are on top of the 96,888 ha that the GMA Rice Program is targeting for the 2010 wet cropping season.

According to Oryza, the Philippines National Food Authority (NFA) council has approved rice imports of up to 500 000 tonnes to improve buffer rice stocks in the aftermath of typhoon Haiyan that struck the country on 8 November. Rice is expected to be imported from Thailand, Viet Nam and Cambodia in November or December. Rice crop losses due to the typhoon are estimated at 2 million tonnes of paddy, according to local sources (Oryza, 19 November 2013).

Starting from January 2009 and until October 2009, through the Land Bank, around PHP 8.02 billion was released to 257,198 farmer-beneficiaries for palay production.   The Agricultural Guarantee Fund Pool (AGFP), which was established to encourage financial institutions to lend to farmers by providing guarantee cover of up to 85 percent of the unsecured loans extended to them, has so far provided PHP 4.88 billion-worth of guarantee lines to farmers.

A total of P1.203 billion was released to 31,769 farmers/fisherfolk under the various lending facilities of the Agro-Industry Modernization Credit and Financing Program. During 2009, DA released P481.13 billion as loans to agricultural sector.

Around 100 hundred hectares of cacao farm will be linked by the soon-to-be constructed farm-to-market (FMR) in Asuncion, Davao del Norte. The P78.8 million FMR is part of the Philippine Rural Development Project (PRDP) which covers rehabilitation and concreting of 7.8 kilometers access road in the villages of New Visayas and Binancian. PRDP is a special project of the Department of Agriculture (DA) and jointly funded by the World Bank, the national and local government units.

Agriculture Secretary launched the nationwide Program for Unified Lending to Agriculture (PUNLA) in Northern Samar (Catarman) on September 15 and Eastern Samar (Borongan) on September 16, which aims to address the financial needs of the marginal farmers and fishers of the country. PUNLA, which has an initial funding allocation of P200-million (US$ 4.28 million)), will provide non-collateralized loans for agri-fishery production and agri-microfinance. The Second National Plan of Action for Children (2nd NPAC) for 2011-2016 sets the agenda towards the progressive realization of the rights of Filipino children and the fulfilment of the commitment of the Government of the Philippines to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The government confirmed on 4 September 2014 that crude palm oil exports would be exempt from taxes during September and October in efforts to draw down stocks.

Intention to allow private sector to import an additional 200,000 tonnes of rice.

According to a media source, in the framework of the rice self-sufficiency programme, the government is planning to increase hybrid rice acreage by 200 000 ha in the 2014/2015 cropping season. It will provide hybrid seeds free of cost to farmers and provide them with fertilizers.

According to a media news, the Philippine Rice Research Institute (PhilRice) signed a memorandum of understanding with a rural development organization to promote hybrid rice cultivation by providing loans to farmer cooperatives that are involved in inbred and hybrid rice production (Oryza News, 14 June 2013)

Distribution of "milking" goats, imported from Australia, to farmers. They  can produce about 2 liters of milk daily compared with native breeds that have lower yields.

The Philippine Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (PBSAP) is the country’s roadmap to conserve its biodiversity and achieve its vision - “By 2028, biodiversity is restored and rehabilitated, valued, effectively managed and secured, maintaining ecosystem services to sustain healthy, resilient Filipino communities and delivering benefits to all.”
The PBSAP covers seven major chapters with Chapter 1 providing an overview on the status and trends of Philippine biodiversity. In this chapter, the country’s biodiversity and its corresponding ecosystem services, the economic gains derived from conserving biodiversity and its impact on Philippine development are all discussed. Chapter 2 describes how the PBSAP is anchored in the Philippine Development Plan (PDP). While the PDP adopts the framework for inclusive growth, the PBSAP articulates the same direction of pursuing economic growth while protecting the environment. Chapter 3 focuses on the policy, governance and financing of biodiversity in the Philippines with key environmental laws, technical agencies with resource management functions and programs on biodiversity and the country’s commitments to international conventions. Chapter 4 deals with the principal pressures of biodiversity loss - habitat loss and degradation, overexploitation, pollution, climate change and IAS – that were captured from series of regional and national consultations which were later analyzed by experts using mind mapping that subsequently classified the direct and indirect pressures. Chapter 5 examines how the current PBSAP was formulated, the regional and national consultations for PBSAP updating process and the Project Steering Committee behind this. The gaps in the previous PBSAP iterations are also discussed in this chapter. Chapter 6 identifies the Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan with nine priority strategies developed from the regional and national consultations. Chapter 7 discusses the implementation needs of the PBSAP and the learning from previous PBSAP implementation.

To mitigate the impacts of climate change on rice production and food security, the Department of Agriculture (DA)-PhilRice and the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) are developing varieties that could withstand multiple biotic and abiotic stresses. The collaborative project titled, ‘Accelerating the development and adoption of next-generation (NextGen) rice varieties for major ecosystems in the Philippines’ aims to fast-track the introduction and adoption of higher yielding inbred and hybrid rice varieties resistant to major pests and diseases and tolerant to adverse environments.

Launch of a milk feeding program for selected pupils affected by last year’s typhoons Ondoy and Pepeng. The program will supplement the pupils’ daily dietary needs from November  2010 to January 2011 and will cover 81 718 Grade one students from 265 public elementary schools in Regions I, III, IV-A and, the National Capital Region. Each student will be served daily with 195 ml UHT chocolate milk and fortified biscuits during the project’s span.

The Philippine Council for Agriculture, Forestry and Natural Resources Research and Development (PCARRD) announced last November 2005 its plan to undertake a series of consultations to craft the Science & Technology (S&T) Agenda. This agenda would 
allow agriculture, forestry and natural resources (AFNR) sectors to flourish within the context of the Philippine Agriculture (PA) 2020.  The overall structure of the Integrated S&T Agenda in Agriculture, Forestry and Natural Resources for CY 2006–2010 is anchored on the four banner programs of PCARRD. This paradigm integrates knowledge and technology generation, the utilization of the generated R&D results, policy formulation and advocacy program, and capability building and governance.

The government has earmarked PHP 86.1 billion for the Agricultural Development Program, designed to ensure food security and further improve self-sufficiency. In particular the allotment will be used to boost rice production and improve irrigation and drainage areas (PHP 26 billion) on the top 33 rice-producing provinces, and to strengthen research and development, credit services and construct of farm-to-market roads (PHP 14.5 billion).
The government has raised its import quota for 2008 to 2.4 million metric tons from 2.1 million last June in a bid to ensure at least a 30-day stockpile until the end of the year.

The Department of Agriculture provides an additional supply of rice and basic food items to Tawi-Tawi, Sulu, and Basilan provinces  to meet the increased demand due to the influx of returning Filipinos and refugees from Sabah (Official Gazette, 11 March 2013).

Under the FIELDS Programme, from 2001 to 2009, a total of PHP 28.8 billion was released under the Agro-Industry Modernization and Credit Financing Program and Quedancor to farmer-beneficiaries. Including palay production loans released by the Land Bank and other financial institutions the total would amount to PHP 465 billion.

The Department of Agriculture (DA) and the International Rice Research Institution (IRRI) announced a joint research initiative to achieve food staple sufficiency by developing cutting-edge rice technology, producing and distributing climate change resistant seeds, and expanding current production areas. It is expected that farm families also improve their income and contribute to improve Pinoy rice varieties competitiveness in global markets (Official Gazette, 3 December 2012).

With the updating of the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2011-2016 the Government has taken stock of the results, identified gaps and refined the strategies to achieve Philippine's 2016 development targets. The Results Matrix (RM) flows logically from the PDP which analyzed the country’s state of development and specified the desired future situation. The PDP update highlights high and sustained economic growth, growth that generates mass employment, as well as growth that reduces poverty. Good governance, national security and ecological integrity remain to be the platform on which the PDP is anchored on.
Temporary suspension of the 3 percent tariff on imported wheat for the next 6 months in order to stabilize prices of bread and  other wheat products

The Department of Agriculture has prioritized the rehabilitation of the crop, livestock and fishery sector in Yolanda-stricken areas through its Reconstruction Assistance on Yolanda (RAY) programme. Corn, rice and vegetable seeds and other planting materials will be provided to ensure that affected farmers can immediately plant/catch up with the cropping season.

The Agricultural and Fisheries Mechanization (AFMech) Law was signed on 5 June with the aim to further modernize the agriculture and fisheries sector through the adoption of modern, cost-effective and environmentally-safe agricultural and fisheries machinery and equipment. Under this law, the Department of Agriculture will draft a five-year National Agri-Fishery Program (Philippines Information agency, 17 June 2013)

The Department of Agriculture (DA) 10 has allocated PHP 460,000 to finance 23 sites were the reservoirs will be established within the framework of the Small Farm Reservoir (SFR)  project. The requirements: the recipients are first endorsed by the LGUs concerned and pre-qualified and validated by DA 10.  Criteria to qualify for the project are: 1) the recipient must have an area to develop as a pond either 500 sqm and 1 meter deep or 250 sqm  and 2 meters deep; 2) the area to be developed as a reservoir must have a service area of at least  2500 sqm or 1/4 hectare; 3) the dike must be at least 1 meter.

The National Convergence Initiative for Sustainable Rural Development (NCI-SRD) is developing an action plan for the implementation of water harvesting facility projects and the adoption of Cistern Technology System which is commonly used in areas where water is scarce.

On August 5th, the Department of Agriculture in partnership with the Province of Negros Occidental launched a P180-million ~ US 4.25  million crop insurance programme that is expected to benefit 10,000 rice farmers. The joint initiative, called the Negros First Universal Crop Insurance Programme (NFUCIP). Under the programme, the provincial government of Negros Occidental agreed to shoulder 60 percent or P500 of the insurance premium worth P840 per hectare per cropping. The balance of P340 is paid by the farmer. The PCIC indemnifies the farmer of up to P17,680 when his rice crop is totally damages by pests, diseases or flood (Department of Agriculture, 15 August 2011).

The Department of Agriculture’s Philippine Rural Development Project (DA-PRDP) in Region 9 is now implementing over P272 million (M) worth of farm-to-market roads in four municipalities of Zamboanga Sibugay.

The Bureau of Agricultural Research (BAR) launched a pilot programme “Adoption of the Bhoochetana Principles and Approach in Boosting Agricultural Productivity in the Philippines” with the primary focus of developing a resilient rainfed agriculture sector and increasing agriculture productivity of selected crops by 20 percent in three years. The main principles driving the initiative are (i) improvement of livelihoods of smallholder farmers by a mission mode programme (ii) rejuvenation of soils and development of new technologies to improve crop productivity and (iii) empowerment of stakeholders in the farming sector through a holistic approach (Official Gazette, 26 September 2013).

In March 2015, the Tacloban School Milk Programme in the Philippines was soft launched and in June the actual programme was rolled out. More than 1 000 children in kindergarten and schools will be provided milk every day during the 2015-2016 and 2016-2017 academic years. The launch activities included milk consumption by children, an exercise on how to fold empty packages for disposal and a presentation to parents on how they could support program implementation. In addition, representatives of the Tacloban Department of Education, the Alaska Milk Corporation and Tetra Laval participated in a ceremonial signing of the Memorandum of Agreement for the program. The programme has already demonstrated effect by increased school attendance compared to previous years.

In response to the damage caused by recent typhoons, the Department of Agriculture announced to link up with fertilizer and seed companies and encourage them to implement a plant-now, pay-later scheme, coupled with a rice marketing tie-up with the National Food Authority. DA will also implement a PHP 400 million credit program through cooperative rural banks in typhoon-affected provinces to provide farmers crop production loans (Department of Agriculture, 14 October 2011)

The National Tobacco Administration (NTA) has given a total of P5.4 million to the tobacco–growing farmers of Abra this cropping season. The loan package is part of the production assistance given to farmers under the Tobacco Contract Growing System of the NTA to sustain the tobacco industry. Furthermore, NTA signed an agreement on the use of tobacco dust as organic pesticide, fishfood, and soil conditioner (Official Gazette and Department of Agriculture, 18 January 2012).

The National Tobacco Administration has doubled the number of scholarships for deserving and qualified dependents of tobacco-growing farmers under its Tobacco-Free Education Program (TFEP).
284 scholarships are available for incoming college freshmen of school year 2015-2016, or nearly twice last year’s 138 grants.

Iron fortified rice (IFR) added to the distribution of more than 6.7 million under the Food for School Program (since it was implemented in 2004). IFR is now also available in NFA accredited outlets such as Tindahan Natin, Tindahan sa Parokya, Bigasan sa Palengke, etc.

On 6 February, the National Food Authority of Philippines announced the 2014 rice import quota under the WTO’s minimum access volume (MAV) for the private importers at 163 000 tonnes, with the highest allocation to Thailand (98 000 tonnes) intended to take advantage of current low prices of Thai rice. The import duty is set at 40 percent, against 50 percent for imports outside MAV (IGC, 27 February 2014).

The Department of Agriculture has earmarked PHP 24 million for the restoration of typhoon-damaged portions of the Banawe rice terraces, and another PHP 10 million to further develop and increase the production of traditional or ‘heirloom’ rice varieties for both domestic and export markets.

The National Food Authority has distributed more than 6.7 million bags of Iron fortified rice (IFR) under the Food for School Program, implemented since 2004. IFR is now also available in NFA accredited outlets such as Tindahan Natin, Tindahan sa Parokya, Bigasan sa Palengke, etc.

The Department of Agriculture (DA) allocated  PHP 500 million (USD 12 million) to increase hybrid rice utilization, as integral part of the Food Staples Sufficiency Program (FSSP). The DA will promote technology-demonstrations farms in top rice-producing provinces and provide loans of up to PHP 50 000 (USD 1200) per hectare to farmers adopting plant hybrids under the expanded PHP 400-million (USD 9.7 million) ‘Sikat-Saka’ credit programme (Official Gazette, 08 April 2013).

The Department of Agriculture allocated an additional amount of PHP 74 million (USD 1.7 million) in Camarines Norte to support agricultural production through irrigation-rehabilitation projects and machinery investment for agriculture and fisheries activities (Official Gazette, 30 May 2012).

Rehabilitation and relief operations’ to cushion the impact of the earthquake that hit Cebu and Bohol are ongoing. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) is distributing family food packs, rice bags, potable water and shelter box tents while the Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) ordered the release of about PHP 8.2 million funds (US$ 200 000) to 4 500 coconut farmers in the affected areas (Official Gazette, 25 October 2013).

The Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) extended its project IP Outreach Program (IPOP) for 2013 targeting a cultivation area of 4 900 hectares, up by 620 hectares from the previous year. The scheme benefits about 1.5 million indigenous people, 35 percent of the total population of Region XII – Soccsksargen, through the provision of seedlings, planting materials and a cash incentive of PHP 20 per coconut seedling planted (Official Gazette, 20 September 2013).

Close to achieve rice self sufficiency, the Philippines resumed rice exports for the first time in 40 years, by signing an export contract of 35 tonnes of aromatic, long-grain, and organic black rice with United Arab Emirates. Additional 80 tonnes of aromatic and heirloom rice varieties are set for export in the next months (Official Gazette 7 May 2013).

The Philippine Carabao Center, an attached agency of the Department of Agriculture, is set to conduct a study that will explore the use of a common fungus as a bio-control agent to address liver flukes that infest an estimated 2.8 million carabaos in the Philippines. This is made possible by a research grant from the Department of Agriculture Biotechnology Program Office, which is mandated to support initiatives on the safe and responsible use of biotechnology in the area of agriculture and food production.

The Central Bank, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, (BSP) implemented a set of “relief measures” to facilitate loans from commercial banks to farmers adversely affected by tropical depression Quinta which devastated several areas on December 2012. The relief measures (effective on 3 January 2013) include, among others: (i) Exclusion of existing loans of borrowers in affected areas from the computation of past due ratios; (ii) Reduced general loan loss provision from 5 to 1 percent for restructured loans of borrowers in the affected areas; (iii) Moratorium on monthly payments due to BSP for banks with ongoing rehabilitation programs; (iv) Permission for banks to provide financial assistance to their officers and employees affected by the calamity. (Official Gazette, 11 January 2013).

The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) identified 5 additional local government units (LGUs) to undertake land titling activities and signed memorandum of partnership agreement with them for implementing the initiative (Official Gazette, 14 August 2013).

The National Food Authority announced that it will allow private-sector traders to import up to 563,000 tons rice annually.  The move is aimed at enhancing market participation ahead of liberalization of the sector, including the removal of quantitative restriction on imports in 2012. Of the total, 163 000 tonnes are allocated for country-specific import quotas arranged with Australia, China, India, Pakistan, Thailand and US.

The Government published the new 2016 Plan. The National Priority Plan (NPP) is a list of the government’s priority programs, projects and activities in the areas of education, health, youth and sports development, human settlements, science and culture, and economic development. The National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA) issues this list annually.

The Philippine Coconut Authority will implement the “SAGIP” Programme in the Calabarzon Region (PHP 41.2 million or USD 970 000) to control the outbreak of scale insects affecting coconut trees by (i) cutting  senile and infested trees (ii) massive spraying of cochin plus pesticide, (ii) fertilizing of pruned trees (iv) releasing of bio-control agents (predators in low and moderately affected areas) (Official Gazette, 29 May 2013).
Trade agreement signed with Thailand to import 360 000 tonnes of Thai rice every year until January 2015, with a 40 percent import tariff.

As a result from the thypoon Pablo, the Government is implementing measures to facilitate banana growers meeting the overseas contracts by sourcing bananas from unaffected plantations. Reconstruction materials for fish farmers were also distributed (The Official Gazette, 10 December 2012).

Provision of “ Extension Services and Trainings” to equip farmers with knowledge on new technologies and practices in modern agriculture, under the FIELDS program. From 2001 to 2009, a total of 377 299 farmers, agricultural extension workers , and farmer entrepreneurs went through 6759 various agricultural technology trainings and orientations.

The Department of Agriculture’s Philippine Rice Research Institute (PhilRice) has started the introduction and pilot testing of a machine that processes rice hull into biochar which can be used for cooking, baking, sterilizing and heating brooding chicks.

The Department of Agriculture (DA) and the National Tobacco Administration (NTA) opened the PHP 165 million (US$ 3.8 million) food processing and trading center, as part of the NTA Agri-Pinoy Project aimed to improve economic conditions of tobacco farmers in the northern provinces of the country. The project responds to the marketing needs of farmers by eliminating layers of middlemen both in buying agricultural inputs and in selling their products, resulting to lower production cost and higher income (Department of Agriculture, 04 November 2013).

Nutrient content lists – Philipines 

In the Philippines, producers and retailers are required by law to provide a list of the nutrient content of pre-packaged food products (with limited exceptions), even in the absence of a nutrition or health claim. The rules define which nutrients must be listed and on what basis (eg per 100g/per serving).

The Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) suspended the import of all live shrimps and crustaceans indefinitely, in a move to prevent Early Mortality Syndrome (EMS) and other shrimp diseases from spreading in the country (Official Gazette, 30 April 2013).

Thought FIELDS Programme, completion of the PHP 4.12-billion Agno River Basin Flood Control Project Phase II-A by end-June 2010. This project, started in 1998 with the support of the Japan International Cooperation Agency, is under the objective of implementing flood control projects to mitigate flooding that damage communities, including investments in agribusiness.

According to a media report, the Philippines have sought approval from the World Trade Organization (WTO) to continue with quantitative restrictions (QR) on rice imports until 2017. Under the QR system, the country is allowed to import 350 000 tonnes of rice annually under the Minimum Access Volume (MAV) with a duty of 40 percent, while imports above the MAV quota are levied a 50 percent import duty. In 1995, the WTO allowed the Philippines to impose a 10-year quota system for its rice imports. In 2004, the WTO extended the quota system for another five years until 2012. Since then, the Philippines has been requesting for a further extension of the quota system until 2017 to protect local farmers. So far, China, India, Indonesia and Vietnam have supported the Philippines, but negotiations are on with Australia, Canada, Thailand and the U.S. (Oryza, 01 May 2014).

The Institute of Plant Breeding (IPB) of the University of the Philippines Los Baños (UPLB) has developed tomato breeding lines resistant to Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV) in the hope of reviving tomato’s robust production in the country.
The Department of Agriculture implemented on Monday, April 20, 2015, a lower retail price (SRP) for chicken in Metro Manila markets.

The Department of Agriculture (DA) requested an additional budget of PHP 1.6 billion (USD 40 million) to support the rehabilitation of the typhoon affected agricultural areas in Davao Region in view that as of January 8, 2013, the distribution of various agriculture inputs, farm tools and equipment to typhoon-affected farmers’ groups totalled PHP 155 (USD 3.8 million) (Department of Agriculture, 15 January 2013).

Meat processing training to farmers on new technologies and practices to enhance the meat processing livelihood project of backyard livestock raisers to add more value to their meat products. Now women in the area are empowered to earn additional income for their family.

Department of Agriculture will assist farmers affected by Tropical Storm Sendong via a Palit-tanim scheme. Beneficiaries if whose farms were totally damaged will be entitled to a 100-percent seed subsidy for palay/corn; while those whose farms were partially damaged, will receive 50 percent subsidy (Official .Gazette, 20 December 2011).

At the evacuation centers in the towns of Linamon and Baloi in Lanao del Norte. Agriculture Secretray led the distribution of food aids together with the Department of Social Welfare and Development. The Department of Agriculture proposes a medium-term nationwide rural development programme, called the Philippine Rural Development Program (PRDP), initially covering six regions (4A, 4B, 5, 6, 7, and 8) in Luzon and Visayas, in addition to all provinces covered under the current Mindanao Rural Development Program Phase 2 (MRDP2). After passing a series of testing and careful evaluation by the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) of the Bureau of Plant Industry (BPI), Asha peanut (Arachis hypogaea) is now certified seeds and could be commercially viable in the Philippines.

Philippine Agriculture (PA) 2020 is a medium term strategic plan for the agriculture and natural resources sector articulated by scientists, farmers, entrepreneurs, non-government workers, people in the bureaucracy, and other stakeholders in a series of consultations and workshops convened by the National Academy of Science and Technology (NAST). The plan envisions a sector that shall have a major role in reducing poverty, achieving food security, global competitiveness, sustainability and justice and peace. It looks forward ten years hence to a vision of robust and vibrant agricultural and natural resources production systems and ecosystems services that improve and sustain well being in the Philippines/

The Department of Agriculture’s Philippine Rice Research Institute (PhilRice) has started the introduction and pilot testing of a machine that processes rice hull into biochar which can be used for cooking, baking, sterilizing and heating brooding chicks.

The Department of Environment and Natural Resources made available over 21 million tree seedlings for the coming planting under the National Greening Program (NGP) to take advantage of the approaching rainy season and to ensure to meet the NGP’s target for 2013 fixed at 170 million seedlings on 300 000 hectares of land (Official Gazette, 28 May 2013).

Several emergency responses have been implemented for people affected by natural disasters and calamities.  The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) allotted PHP 82.3 million in food packs and other no-food items for families to face the Tropical Depression Caloy, which entered the country’s area on 21 March. The Department of Labor and Employment in Central Visayas has released a total of PHP 3.7 million in grants for 17 livelihood projects in various municipalities during the first two months of 2014 in favour of the survivors of natural disasters, such as the earthquake in Bohol and super Typhoon Yolanda (Official Gazette, 23 March 2013).

The National Framework Strategy on Climate Change (2010-2022) serves as basis for climate change planning, research and development, extension, and monitoring of activities to protect vulnerable communities from the adverse effects of climate change. Formulated based on climate change vulnerabilities, specific adaptation needs, and mitigation potential, and in accordance with international agreements. The framework aggressively highlights the critical aspects of adaptation meant to be translated to all levels of governance alongside coordinating national efforts towards integrated ecosystem based management which shall ultimately render sectors climate resilient.

The tariff of 7 percent on feed wheat imports, suspended in January 2009, has being restored. The import duty suspension for food wheat was extended for a further six months.

The Bureau of Agricultural Research (BAR) officially sealed its support to the project “Establishment of Plant Genetic Research (PGR) Laboratory and Training Center” at the Central Bicol State University of Agriculture (CBSUA) by signing the Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) for the PhP 5M-project.

The Department of Agriculture is promoting Philippine mangoes to be at par with the international market. As such, the food agency is prioritizing measures that would enable local growers to grow high quality mangoes that conform with international standards.

The Department of Agriculture jointly with the Philippine Center for Postharvest Development and Mechanization (PhilMech) will establish 28 rice processing centers (RPC) and provide technical assistance on post-harvest technology in order to reduce postharvest losses and dependence of farmers on private millers (Official Gazette)

COVID-19:  Office of the Secretary, Government of Philippines issues the provisions related to continue agriculture production as follows:
1. All farming and fishing activities shall continue. 
2. All farmers, farm workers, fisherfolk and agribusiness personnel shall be exempted from home quarantine. Provided that they observe safety protocols and number is at a minimum
3. All Agricultural supply stores, outlets nationwide and animal clinics must be allowed to operate under a skeletal force
4. Essential farm personnel (including veterinarians, farm hands, farm and fisher folks) that works at production areas, bearing proper documentation, are also requested passage at quarantine checkpoints

As few farmers or farm workers have Farmer ID’s and business permits (the latter is required to obtain  passes), they should first be endorsed by the barangay captain to get a pass. The National Food Authority has released a total of 2 788 bags of rice to various relief agencies including DSWD, Office of Civil Defense (OCD), Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction Management Council (PDRRMC), and concerned Local Government Units (LGUs).

The Department of Agriculture through the National Irrigation Administration (NIA), for 2012 has allocated PHP 24.5 billion (USD 553.6 million) to construct new irrigation systems, and restore and rehabilitate existing ones, servicing a total of 224,850 hectares (has) (Department of Agriculture, 04 January 2012).

Out of the 1,380 packages, 428 or 31 percent were distributed in the Mindanao Agribusiness Super Region, 315 in the North Luzon Agribusiness Quadrangle, 430 in Central Philippines , 204 in the Urban Luzon Beltway and 3 in the National Capital Region (NCR).

The move will lower the cost of transporting goods and people, support agricultural productivity, reduce risks from disasters and generate economic investments and employment (Official Gazette, 12 August 2013).

The Tax Reform for Acceleration and Inclusion (TRAIN) Programme

On 1 January 2018, the Philippines government implemented a sweetened beverage excise tax of six pesos per litre (around $0.12) on products using purely caloric and purely non-caloric sweeteners or a mix of both as part of the Tax Reform for Acceleration and Inclusion (TRAIN) tax reform programme under Republic Act 10963. It also implemented a 12 pesos per litre (around $0.24) excise tax on drinks using purely high-fructose corn syrup or in combination with any caloric or non-caloric sweetener. The products taxed include non-alcoholic beverages that contain caloric sweetener (defined as a substance that is sweet and includes sucrose, fructose or glucose) or non-caloric sweetener (defined as a substance that is artificially or chemically processed that produces a certain sweetness, and includes aspartame, sucralose, saccharin, acesulfame potassium, neotame, cyclamates and other non-nutritive sweeteners). Taxed sweetened beverages include the following: sweetened juice drinks; sweetened tea; all carbonated beverages; flavoured water; energy and sports drinks; other powdered drinks not classified as milk, juice, tea or coffee; cereal and grain beverages; and other non-alcoholic beverages that contain added sugar. 100% natural fruit and vegetable juices, milk products, and meal replacement and medically indicated beverages are exempt from the tax.

The Department of Agriculture, through its Agricultural Credit Policy Council (ACPC), will implement a P100 million quick response calamity assistance program (CAP) for small farmers and fisherfolk affected by typhoon Lando.

The Department of Agriculture (DA) is providing PHP 41 million (USD 1 million) in rehabilitation assistance to high-value crops farmers (cacao, banana, coffee and rubber) affected by last year’s Typhoon Pablo, in Compostela Valley province (Department of Agriculture, 03 March 2013).

National Economic and Development Authority announced that infrastructure and value-chain developments will be strengthened during 2013 to sustain growth in agriculture and fisheries sector. Initial assistance consists in provision of replacement seeds and materials along with training courses measures to prevent huge damages on crops. As a long-term solution, water-impounding facilities will be constructed strategically in frost-prone areas. DA will also establish additional rain-shelters and greenhouses so that farmers can grow and harvest crops even during rainy and cold seasons (Department of Agriculture, 08 January 2014)

1. The PNP designated a ‘Cargo Lane’ for agriculture and fisheries inputs and food products transported through all forms of conveyance (air, water, and land), across all modes of deliveries. Priority for entry to cargo lanes shall be given to truckers/suppliers with Food Pass
2. Food pass accreditation is free of charge
3. DA accredits suppliers and trucks to use the ‘Food Lane’ (Cargo Lane)
4. DA identifies a list of food items that must be allowed unhampered and unimpeded in all quarantine checkpoints 
a. All vehicles carrying crop commodities, and fishery and other aquatic products with carriers must be allowed passage. 
b. Live poultry and livestock, including meat and meat products, are allowed passage only when with proper documentation as in DA MC No. 5 series of 2020. 
c. Movement of products and services related to farm inputs is requested for unhampered passage on quarantine checkpoints.

COVID-19: The Department of Agriculture (DA) is forging stronger ties with the LGUs to ensure that households affected by the enhanced community quarantine will have access to the food supply.

Under the DA’s proposed Distribution and Marketing System, a two-mode KADIWA ni Ani at Kita is being rolled out, where DA will find suppliers to the food requirements of the residents of areas affected by the imposed Luzon-wide quarantine. The DA, as the agency mandated to ensure sufficient supply and efficient delivery of food items, will find a source for different agri-fishery products and link it with the LGUs. 

The 'KADIWA ni Ani (harvest) at Kita (income)' system which identifies drop-points where farmers can directly sell their goods for the retail price, and where people can buy major agricultural goods at reasonably low prices. Kadiwa, which stands for “Katuwang sa Diwa at Gawa para sa Masanang Ani at Mataas na Kita”, is a marketing strategy of the DA which directly connects the food producers to the consumers, thereby lessening the cost of the products. It links the LGU in urban centers to farmer-producers in the different parts of the country to ease the delivery and distribution of food supply.

The Philippine Master Plan for Climate Resilient Forestry Development (2016-2028) is the third formulated after the first one in 1990 and the second in 2003.  The Plan proposes programs and strategies to a) strengthen resilience of forest ecosystems and communities to climate change, b) effectively respond to demands for forest ecosystems goods and services and c) promote responsive governance; and list of priority actions. 
The total budgetary requirement for implementing the Philippine Master Plan for Climate Resilient Forestry Development is 135.16 billion pesos over a period of 13 years. About 69% of the budget will support programs related to responding to demands for forest ecosystems goods and services while about 28% of the total budget is allocated to strengthen resilience of ecosystems and communities to climate change. The rest will support strategies to promote responsive governance and other support programs.

The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) allocated PHP 160.35 million (USD 3.7 million) in emergency relief resources such as food packs (worth P12.84 million), non-food items and standby funds for households affected by typhoon Labuyo (Official Gazette, 13 August 2013).

The Institute of Plant Breeding (IPB) of the University of the Philippines Los Baños (UPLB) has developed tomato breeding lines resistant to Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV) in the hope of reviving tomato’s robust production in the country.

On 14 February, the Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP) launched the Agriculture and Fisheries Financing Program (AFFP), a flexible credit facility scheme to benefit 40 000 marginalized farmers and fishermen from the 20 poorest provinces of the country. AFFP has an outlay of PHP 550 million (US$ 12.4 million) earmarked by the Department of Agriculture and the Agricultural Credit Policy Council (Department of Agriculture, 18 February 2014).

The Department of Agriculture and the Province of Negros Occidental will jointly implement P166-million~ US 3.9 million worth of irrigation projects next year that will irrigate an additional area of 2,675 hectares, benefiting 2,920 farm families (Department of Agriculture 13 August 2011)

Allocation of PHP 1.670 million (USD 38 000) worth of assistance to families displaced by flooding in Cotabato and Maguindanao. In addition, the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) announced continuation of food assistance to households displaced by typhoon Pablo until August (Official Gazette 31 July).

The Philippines Agriculture Department (DA), the Philippine Rice Research Institute (PhilRice), International Rice Research Institute (IRRI), International Rice Genebank of IRRI and several nongovernment organizations are jointly launching a project to preserve, nurture and market the historical heirloom rice varieties that grow in the northern Cordillera region.

Department of Agriculture (DA) provided 1.68 million bags of hybrid and 12.5 million bags of certified palay seeds from 2001 to 2009 to farmers nationwide. The DA also established the development of climate-ready seeds including saline-, drought-, and flood-resistant varieties.

The Department of Agriculture distributed PHP 321-million (USD 7.8 million) worth of farm machinery and equipment to farmers in Region 12 (Soccsksargen) under the framework of agriculture and fishery sector modernization programme (Department of Agriculture, 21 February 2013).

The Department of Agriculture recently turned over to the Caraga region agricultural support amounting to P216 million. The support package includes P208-million worth farm-to-market road (FMR) subprojects under the Philippine Rural Development Project (PRDP). Besides the support from DA-PRDP, DA also turned over farm equipment amounting to P7.8 million, among them rice reaper, corn picker, and a hand tractor to various farmers’ associations and cooperatives.

The Philippine Coconut Authority will implement the “SAGIP” Programme in the Calabarzon Region (PHP 41.2 million or USD 970 000) to control the outbreak of scale insects affecting coconut trees by (i) cutting  senile and infested trees (ii) massive spraying of cochin plus pesticide, (ii) fertilizing of pruned trees (iv) releasing of bio-control agents (predators in low and moderately affected areas) (Official Gazette, 29 May 2013).

Minister for Agriculture of Fiji signed a MOU with Philippine for agricultural training and commercial agriculture. Under the terms of the MOU the Ministry of Agriculture will be able to use the expertise of PSAU to identify Fijian agricultural products for commercial development and actually assist the private sector in Fiji, to fully develop these for commercial markets in Fiji and overseas. The Ministry staff will undertake exchange study programs at the university and the university will assist in providing technical expertise in various field of agriculture in Fiji.

The Department of Agriculture allocated an initial PHP 28.8 million (USD 700 000) to promote agri-tourism sites under a multi-sectoral collaboration called “Green Initiative”. The amount will finance the construction of farm-to-market roads (PHP 20 million) and irrigation systems (PHP 1.2 million) and the implementation of agricultural production and livelihood projects for livestock, organic vegetables, fisheries, high value crops, rice and coconut (Department of Agriculture, 10 May 2013).

According to a media report, the country has decided to import 200 000 tonnes of rice from Viet Nam, in addition to the 800 000 tonnes agreed in April. Increased imports are prompted following concerns over El Niño effects on this year’s rice production and recent price spikes in the domestic markets (Oryza, 27 June 2014).

The construction of a P71-million rainfed reservoir and irrigation dam in Itbaya is expected to be completed by 2013. The irrigation project will expand the current service area of 33 hectares to over 300 hectares, and enable Itbayat farmers to plant two rice crops a year. Estimated  palay production by 2014 and onwards at two croppings a year would total at least 1,800 metric tons, enough to feed Batanes’s 16,000 population.

An initial PHP 10 million were allocated to support national mango farmers and fund the Philippine Mango Industry Foundation project for this year that includes planting of recommended mango seedlings, provision of postharvest equipment and facilities, marketing assistance, and capacity-building provincial mango growers’ associations and cooperatives (Official Gazette).

The Agricultural Credit Policy Council (ACPC) approved a Resolution that mandates the release and use of an additional  PHP 100 million for the ACPC and People’s Credit and Finance Corporation (ACPC-PCFC) Agro-Microfinance Program (AMP) to address the credit requirements of farmers and fisherfolk affected by El Niño and other calamities associated with climate change.

The Department of Agriculture promotes the productivity and incomes of farmers through several agricultural infrastructure projects. The first initiative under implementation in Quezon province, initially amounting to PHP 65 million (USD 1.6 million), includes a PHP 45 million (USD 1.1 million) farm-to-market road, a rice processing complex, and small water impounding project (Department of Agriculture, 04 March 2013).

COVID-19: The Department of Agriculture, Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), and the Department of Health (DOH) issued a joint memorandum circular imposing a 60-day price freeze for basic goods and agriculture products nationwide. Price is being monitored by DA (some spot-checks are being done jointly by DA and DTI) and information is released every 2 days.

FDA voluntary front of pack label

On 13 December 2012, the Philippines Food and Drug Administration issued FDA Circular No. 2012-015 which set out guidelines for a voluntary front of pack label that applies to FDA-CFRR regulated products (processed and prepackaged food products). The label must appear on the lower right hand portion of the principal display panel and must outline the amount of energy per serving of the food, and the percentage of the calorie value based on the Recommended Energy and Nutrient Intakes (RENI) for energy. Producers need to submit their labels to the FDA for approval before they can be displayed.

The Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PPAN) 2017-2022 is an integral part of the Philippine Development Plan 2017-2022. It is consistent with the Duterte Administration 10-point Economic Agenda, the Philippine Health Agenda, and the development pillars of malasakit (protective concern), pagbabago (change or transformation), and kaunlaran (development), and the vision of Ambisyon 2040. It factors in and considers country commitments to the global community as embodied in the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals, the 2025 Global Targets for Maternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition, and the 2014 International Conference on Nutrition.

The Department of Agriculture (DA), National Food Authority (NFA) and the Bureau of Customs and rice millers agreed to effectively monitor and stop the entry of smuggled rice and other farm products into the country, in order to protect domestic farmers and ensure the DA’s rice sufficiency programme, In particular, the NFA becomes the sole importer of the ordinary rice and farmer groups, previously allowed to import rice as part of the private sector allocation, are now allowed to distribute imported rice under the Institutionalized Farmers as Distributors (IFAD) programme of the NFA. Rice millers and processors will have brand name registered with NFA so that smuggled rice can easily be tracked down (Department of Agriculture, 25 February 2013).

The Department of Agriculture has enhanced the crop insurance system,functioning through the Philippine Crop Insurance Corporation (PCIC), a government-owned and controlled corporation under the DA that has a mandate of providing insurance protection to agricultural producers against losses of crops and non-crop agricultural assets due to natural calamities, pests and diseases, and other risk factors.

In lieu of rice seed subsidy, the Department of Agriculture will shift its support to other interventions with more long-term impact on farmers’ productivity and incomes. The remaining seed subsidy for 2010 worth PHP 1.3 billion will be spent on eight other interventions. The bulk will be spent on irrigation, particularly in the repair and rehabilitation of communal irrigation systems (CIS) through the DA’s National Irrigation Administration (NIA) in partnership with local government units (LGUs) through counterparting scheme or public-private partnership. Other interventions comprise: post-harvest support; seed production assistance; organic fertilizer assistance; development on new varieties of rice; extension, education and training; and a production loan through the Land Bank of Philippines (public).

The Government issued rice import licences for 187 000 tonnes of rice to private trading companies under the WTO Minimum Access Volume rules. These imports are in addition to 500 000 tonnes of duty-free imports that have already taken place.

The Philippine Crop Insurance Corporation (PCIC) has recently launched the pilot of the Weather Index-Based Crop Insurance (WIBCI) in Dumangas to help farmers recover from crop loss caused by abnormal rain patterns. The insurance provides payment if rainfalls are too low or if they exceed significantly the average level, upon certified occurrence of weather event to which insurance relates. WIBCI which was designed and developed in 2012 is now at its first implementation phase and it is set to expand in 2015 (Department of Agriculture, 04 June 2014).

For a faster and more efficient reporting and data sharing within the Department of Agriculture, the DA-Philippine Rural Development Project (PRDP) has developed a web-based management information system (MIS) for use of concerned DA family agencies

The wholesale price of NFA rice has been increased from PHP 23.50 (USD 0.53) to PHP 25.00 (USD 0.57) per kilogram, effective from December 7, 2010.  On the retail level, this will effectively increase the price from PHP 25.00/kg (USD 0.57) to PHP 27.00/kg. (USD 0.61). The move is among the measures government is undertaking to ensure the viability of the agency and continue fulfilling its mandate of supporting farmers to produce enough for self-sufficiency.

The Department of Agriculture repairing facilities and equipment to rehabilitation and strengthen the country’s repository of genetic resources (crops) for agriculture and food security purposes. The project involves the upgrading of the National Plant Genetic Resources Laboratory (NPGRL). Project completion is envisaged by April 2012 and the allocated resources reach PHP 5-million (USD 117,000) (Official Gazette, 27 January 2012).

As of 19 November, nearly 700 000 food and rice packs have been distributed by the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) in Leyte, Eastern Samar and Tacloban City communities affected by the Typhoon Hayan. DSWD has also provided the displaced families with about 220 000 liters of bottled water, 41 000 pieces of canned goods and 125 000 pieces of high-energy biscuits. Relief operations by the Government will continue and along with support from international partners. DA staff and the Philippine Coconut Authority are facilitating transport and delivery of food items from food producing areas to Tacloban (Department of Agriculture 20 November 2013).

The Department of Finance authorized the implementation of measures aimed at curbing the smuggling of oil and other goods into the country, such as the port accreditation (only particular ports will be accredited for sensitive commodities such as oil), the submission of rolling import plans by importers, trade statistics reconciliation through monthly list of imports and special monitoring of oil smuggling cases (Royal Gazette 14 April 2013).

The Philippine Council for Agriculture, Forestry and Natural Resources Research and Development (PCARRD) announced last November 2005 its plan to undertake a series of consultations to craft the Science & Technology (S&T) Agenda. This agenda would 
allow agriculture, forestry and natural resources (AFNR) sectors to flourish within the context of the Philippine Agriculture (PA) 2020.  The overall structure of the Integrated S&T Agenda in Agriculture, Forestry and Natural Resources for CY 2006–2010 is anchored on the four banner programs of PCARRD. This paradigm integrates knowledge and technology generation, the utilization of the generated R&D results, policy formulation and advocacy program, and capability building and governance.

Under the program, farmers will be given site specific and appropriate training and extension services and production inputs such as drought and flood tolerant seeds to enhance crop production. Food–based dietary guidelines – Philippines

In 2012 the Philippines published the revised '2012 nutritional guidelines for Filipinos' aimed at the general population.  The Philippines uses the daily nutritional guide pyramid and has developed pyramids for different population groups. The pyramid is divided into levels of recommended consumption. Messages about exercise and personal and environmental hygiene serve as support messages for the pyramid. The healthy food plate for Filipino adults (Pinggang Pinoy) completes the messages of the pyramid by showing adequate distribution of nutritious foods in a meal.

To give farmers better income and entice them to sell their produce to National Food Authority, the agency grants an additional PHP 0.70 per kg incentives in addition to the PHP 17 per kilogram buying price for clean and dry palay. These include PHP 0.30 per kg for cooperative development and PHP 0.20 per kg each for drying and transport incentives. The 2010 palay procurement target is set at 11.6 million bags.

The Organic Agriculture Act of 2010 (or RA 10068) is aimed at developing, enhancing and supporting activities for the formulation and implementation of unified and integrated organic agriculture research and development and extension (RD&E) plans and programs from the national down to the field level. Specifically, the law seeks to promote, propagate and further develop the practice of organic farming in the Philippines which is expected to: 1) increase farm productivity; 2) reduce environmental degradation and prevent the depletion of natural resources; 3) protect the health of farmers, consumers and the general public; and 4)help cut expenses on imported farm inputs.

The National Economic and Development Authority approved the Philippine Rural Development Program (PRDP) of the Department of Agriculture, for a total outlay of PHP 27.54 billion (USD 620 million). PRDP will cover all of the country’s 80 provinces and it will be implemented over six years as DA’s platform for inclusive growth, value-chain oriented and climate-resilient agri-fisheries sector. The program will engage local government units, farmer groups and other private sector players as partners in infrastructure development that support priority commodities (Official Gazette, 29 April 2013)

In response to the damage caused by recent typhoons, the Department of Agriculture announced to link up with fertilizer and seed companies and encourage them to implement a plant-now, pay-later scheme, coupled with a rice marketing tie-up with the National Food Authority. The Department of Agriculture will provide an initial assistance of over PHP 116 million (US 27 million) to farmers whose rice, corn crops and irrigation facilities were damaged by typhoons ‘Pedring’ and ‘Quiel’ (Department of Agricutlure, 23 October 2011).

The National Food Authority (NFA) signed earlier today (5 June 2015) a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) on improving rice quality in the Philippines.

The government will pour investments in the countryside for economic empowerment of rural poor and to encourage its dwellers to stay in these communities and avoid congesting the Metropolis. These are the paramount goals of the National Convergence Initiative for Sustainable Rural Development (NCI-SRD), led by four of the biggest departments of the government: Agriculture, Agrarian Reform, Environment and Natural Resources, and Interior and Local Government.

With this sub-project, coffee farmers in the community will no longer need to bring their harvests to Tuguegarao City or Isabela for selling. The association will directly buy coffee beans for processing from local farmers.

In June 2017 fishing communities in Midsayap, North Cotabato, received 34 units of motorized bancas and 80 000 tilapia fingerlings from the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR). Almost 50 farmer-groups also received different farm machines worth P8.9-M from the Bottom-Up Budgeting (BUB) program to boost their production.

1. Attainment of nutritional well-being is a main responsibility of families
2. It is the duty and obligation of government to assist those who are unable to enjoy the right to good nutrition
3. Priority given to those with less access and most nutritionally at-risk

The Philippines government signed a government-to-government (G2G) deal for importing 500 000 rice, after rejecting all offers in the tender closed on 27 August because the prices were too high, exceeding the government’s set budget of PHP 10.3 billion. The G2G modality would narrow down the supply competition between Cambodia and Vietnam, the only two countries with supply agreements with the Philippines. This tender will take total NFA imports in 2014 to 1.3 million tonnes. NFA is also authorized to import additional 500 000 tonnes for emergency needs.

The Soccsksargen Region earmarked more than PHP 21 million to expand organic farming activities in accordance with the Organic Agriculture Act of 2010, which institutionalized the adoption and development of organic agriculture in the country to convert five percent of the total agricultural land to organic.

During the meeting of the National Food Authority (NFA) Council on 6 December it was decided that the country will import an initial 500,000 metric tons (MT) of rice in 2012; which will be 360,000 MT less than 2011. Private sector and farmers’ groups to import 250,000 MT each.(Official Gazette, 06 December 2011).

Issuance of certificate of land ownership awards (CLOAs) from the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) in Agusan del Norte and Agusan del Sur.

Department of Agriculture (DA)signed under the Philippine Rural Development Project (PRDP) the construction of P182M Farm to Market Roads in Negros Occidental

A total of P1.52 billion (B) in farm machineries and project grants were awarded to farmers/fishers-beneficiaries from the rural communities of the SOCCSKSARGEN Region, during a Mass Distribution of farm equipment and various agricultural assistance on July 30, 2015 at the regional center in Carpenter Hill, Koronadal City.

The Philippine Rural Development Program (PRDP) is a six-year national government development platform with a multi-sectoral approach. It aims at contributing towards achieving an inclusive, value-chain oriented, and climate resilient agriculture and fisheries sector. It provides an operational Agriculture and Fisheries Modernization Plan (AFMP) for an integrated technical support service delivery at the local and national levels, build strategic network of rural logistics infrastructure within priority value chains in targeted program areas, strengthen and develop viable rural enterprises through efficient supply and value chain of key agricultural and fishery products in targeted program areas, implement and model innovations towards more effective and efficient institutional support systems for programme implementation, and institutionalize stakeholder engagement. The thrust of PRDP to develop a market-oriented and climate-resilient agriculture and fishery sector will be articulated through its four (4) components: i) Local and National Level Planning (I-PLAN), ii) Infrastructure Development (I-BUILD), iii) Enterprise Development (I-REAP) and, iv) Project Implementation Support (I-SUPPORT).The document aims at making agriculture, forestry and fisheries more productive and sustainable.

AmBisyon Natin 2040 represents the collective long-term vision and aspirations of the Filipino people for themselves and for the country in the next 25 years. It describes the kind of life that people want to live, and how the country will be by 2040. As such, it is an anchor for development planning across at least four administrations.

A legislation to promote urban farming in the metropolis has been adopted. It directs the Department of Agriculture and the Department of Science and Technology to campaign for urban agriculture and vertical farming in metropolitan areas to address food security concerns and regenerate ecosystem functions in the country (Department of Agriculture, 06 March 2014). COVID-19: The Philippine Department of Agriculture will be implementing a P31 billion (USD 608 million) ‘Plant, Plant, Plant Program’ to enhance food security concerns amidst the country's coronavirus disease (COVID-19) outbreak. The Program aims to raise paddy production to 22.1 million tons (13.5 million tons milled rice), which would be 93 percent of the country’s total demand of 14.5 million tons. Parallel to the Program is the Philippine government’s plan to import 300 000 tons of rice through a government-to-government purchase arrangement.

The Department of Social Welfare and the Development-Information Communications Technology Management Service jointly developed an Online Geographic Information System (WebGIS), as a map to visualize reports on disaster-affected areas and population and location of evacuation centers during disasters and emergency situations (Official Gazette, 23 August 2013).

The Bureau of Plant Industry (BPI) and the KaMMMPi,  a farmer’s organization, reached an agreement to extend financial assistance to small farmers for them to operate their own seed bank that will supply certified seeds of rice to other farmers via equal exchange or barter basis or direct sales. The seed bank will also provide farmers easy access to high quality seeds. The project, which will be initially implemented in Region 1, has a total cost of PHP 18 million and will run for two years. BPI targets to procure a total of 3,600 bags of high quality seeds to be distributed by KaMMMPi to their identified farmer–beneficiaries.

COVID-19: The Department of Agriculture is implementing its Food Resilience Plan which seeks to ensure enough food supply for all and stabilize prices during these times. The DA has also issued separate Memorandum Circulars (MCs) in relation to the provisions of the Food Resiliency Plan.

The Department of Agriculture (DA) allocated an initial PHP 80 million (USD 2 million) for different agricultural and fishery projects to increase the productivity and income of small farmers and fishermen in the Polillo group of islands (Quezon). An amount of PHP 54.7 million (USD 600 000)  is allotted to the DA’s Philippine Crop Insurance Corporation (PCIC) for crop insurance coverage, PHP 14 million (USD 340 000) worth assistance in form of coconut seedlings and processing facility is provided through the Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) and PHP 5 million (USD 120 000) is allocated for distributing fishnets, fishing gears and paraphernalia. In addition, two village food terminals worth PHP 2 million will be established, while PHP 1.5 million (USD 36 000) worth of farm equipment (hand tractors, water engine pumps, and coffee dryer), native pig and chicken, and a training module is provided under the DA’s organic agriculture program (Royal Gazette, 17 April 2013)

Initial allocation of PHP 882.18 million for the implementation of mitigation measures for farmers and fisherfolk in 14 provinces of Luzon and the Visayas, affected by the latest El Niño. Measures range from cloud seeding to the provision of shallow tube wells and open source pump irrigation systems to close monitoring of a possible drought-triggered outbreak of pests and diseases. The DA's regional field units (RFUs) in the El Niño-hit regions have drawn up with local government units (LGUs) their respective master lists of affected farmers eligible for food aid under the Emergency.

A total of P8.9 billion is included in the government’s spending program this year to implement two anti-hunger initiatives aimed at establishing a free feeding program in all public schools and provide children full support from conception up to two years old. The two initiatives, which have been Sen. Grace Poe’s advocacies since joining the legislature in 2013, are funded in the 2017 budgets of the departments of Education (DepEd); Health (DOH); Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) and the National Nutrition Council (NNC).To implement the free feeding program, P4.2 billion has been allocated to the DepEd, the implementing agency of the school-based feeding program, while P4.4 billion has been earmarked for the DSWD to implement the supplemental feeding program.

Kalinga coffee farmers will receive a funding assistance from the Department of Agriculture’s Philippine Rural Development Project (DA-PRDP). The fund consists of P14.8 million for the Kalinga Integrated Coffee Processing and Marketing Enterprise project. The funding assistance from DA is expected to ultimately improve the production of coffee beans in the highlands which has been undergoing a few tweaks under the supervision of PRDP.

The Philippines’ state procurement agency the National Food Authority (NFA), despite having authority to import additional 500 000 tonnes of milled rice, it is unlikely to do so by the end of 2014, unless another typhoon hits the country. This year has recorded the highest amount of imports over the last four years, reaching a total of 1.8 million tonnes milled over the last 10 months.

The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) released PHP 1.50 billion (USD 36 million) to the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) of the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM) for the implementation of various public works initiatives to develop national roads, bridges and other strategic infrastructure (Royal Gazette, 22 April 2013).

For the first quarter of 2010 the National Food Authority - NFA distributes a total of 8.9 million bags of rice equivalent to 76 percent of the 11 million bags target for the period, to stabilize prices after the recent weather events (El Niño). The NFA distributes rice through its 24,524 existing active market outlets.

The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) has released funds amounting to PHP 4.98 billion to the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) for the repair, rehabilitation, and construction of the Department of Agriculture’s (DA) farm-to-market roads (FMRs) nationwide. This will sustain the livelihood and food security of farmers by facilitating the movement of goods to market areas, and it is also a significant boost to local infrastructure development.

On 20 June 2014, the Department of Agriculture announced that existing quantitative import restrictions on rice (minimum access volume - MAV) are set to remain in place until 2017, with formal World Trade Organization (WTO) approval expected in July. These quantitative restrictions protect Filipino rice farmers and rice, the only commodity that enjoys the special treatment in the WTO, given its relevance for the country food security. According to some media reports, the government would lower the tariff of privately imported rice under MAV from 40 percent to 35 percent and increase the MAV to 805 200 tonnes from the current 350 000 tonnes. The tariff for imported volumes beyond the MAV level would remain at 50 percent (IGC, 26 June 2014).

The National Food Authority will aggressively buy palay from local farmers. The target is 13.4 million rice bags. The NFA is taking necessary steps to encourage more farmers to sell their produce by implementing new procurement strategies, such as lending empty sacks to farmer organizations using their Cooperative Development Incentive Fund (CDIF); opening buying stations in far-flung areas where NFA’s chance of being able to buy is greater; coordinating with the Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO) and surveying areas where harvesting is on-going; and deploying mobile procurement teams especially in areas where ex-farm prices are low (Official Gazette, 22 November 2012).

The Department of Agriculture has intensified its interventions to mitigate the effects of the El Niño phenomenon in the country, based on the assessment of the Philippine Atmospheric Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) and field monitoring reports from the DA regional offices.

The Department of Agriculture (DA) in Region XI has outlined strategies to mitigate impact of climate change in agriculture. Among them, a climate change information system is being strengthened  to generate timely and reliable data and infrastructure is being redesigned to make it more climate-resilient.

In the earthquake-stricken province of Bohol, the Department of Agriculture (DA) is developing the Philippine Rural Development Program, a six-year initiative aimed to establishing inclusive and market oriented agri-fishery sector through strategic investments in priority commodity value chains, expanding market access, and improving competitiveness among others (Official Gazette, 23 March 2013).

The National Food Authority has to date issued a total of 3,737 bags of rice to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) and the local government units for relief operations in areas severely affected by Tropical Storm Sendong (Official Gazette, 20 December 2011).
The Department of Agriculture implemented on Monday, April 20, 2015, a lower retail price (SRP) for chicken in Metro Manila markets.

Food security and fishery leaders and policy-makers from Asia Pacific economies have formally adopted the Iloilo Plan of Action that strongly promotes climate resiliency and inclusive growth in the sector.

The Department of Agriculture (DA) has lifted the temporary ban imposed earlier on the entry of birds and poultry, including their products, from Turkey following official confirmation by global animal health authorities of the eradication of the avian influenza (AI) or bird flu virus in that European country.

To reverse the spike in garlic prices, the Department of Agriculture announced it would augment supplies in major markets, and sell garlic at wholesale prices ranging between PHP 100-200 (US$ 2.31-4.61) per kilo depending on the bag size. Furthermore, a PHP 1.3 million (US$ 29 981) storage facility was recently built to support farmers tilling more than 1 000 hectares of onion and garlic in the Ilocos Region (Department of Agriculture, 17 June 2014)

Filipino livestock and hog raisers, and meat processors can now export ‘Pinoy’ livestock and pork products to the rest of the world, as the entire Philippines was recently certified free from the dreaded foot and mouth disease (FMD) without vaccination by the Office International des Epizooties (OIE) or World Organization for Animal Health.

The National Food Authority Council approved during a special meeting on September 17, 2015 the awarding of contract for the supply of 750,000 metric tons of long grain white rice 25% brokens to Thailand and Vietnam based on the results of the Government-to-Government Procurement held on September 17, 2015. The importation is intended to beef-up government inventory in preparation for the looming impact of the El Niño phenomenon.

Within the framework of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), the European Union (EU) has been regulating plant health and variety. The main legislation with regards to plant health and variety is Council Directive 2000/29/EC (amending Council Directive 77/93/EEC).
The main objective of EU plant health legislation is to protect the safety of food derived from plants and to secure the health and quality status of crops in the EU. The legislation regulates the trade of plants and plant products within the EU as well as imports from the rest of the world in accordance with international plant health standards and obligations. This is partially done through providing protective measures against the spread of harmful organisms. The legislation contains a list of harmful organisms that threaten plant health in the EU. This includes the establishment of the European Union Notification System for Plant Health Interceptions (EUROPHYT), which is a rapid alert system dealing with interceptions for plant health reasons of plants and plant products imported into the EU or being traded within the EU itself. EUROPHYT also contributes to the implementation of preventative measures by ensuring that the data on risks to plant and plant products is up-to-date and accurate. 
The legislation with regards to plant health is known as the Common Plant Health Regime (CPHR). The Common Plant Health Regime (CPHR) looks towards contributing to sustainable production through plant health protection; ensuring competitiveness of the agriculture complex; contribute to the protection of public and private green, forests, and the landscape, and to ensure food security. 
The selling and use of plant protection products and their residue in food is also regulated.  Council Directive 91/414/EEC is concerned with the placing of plant protection products on the market. No plant protection product may be used within the EU unless it has been scientifically established that the products have no harmful effects on consumers, farmers, and local residents and passers-by; they do not cause unacceptable effects on the environment; and that they are sufficiently effective against pests. 
Regulation (EC) No 396/2005 currently governs the maximum residue levels (MRLs) of pesticides in food and feed in order to protect the health of consumers. These are controlled by the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA). If any infringements of the Regulation are found, these shall be countered by sanctions of the product.

Within the framework of the Common Agricultural Policy, the European Union has set up programmes to help the EUs outermost regions in the agricultural sector, known as POSEI programmes. The main legislation which sets out the rules with regards to the POSEI programmes is Council Regulation (EC) No 247/2006. These programmes are designed to take account of their geographical and economic handicaps, such as remoteness, insularity, small size, difficult topography and climate, and economic dependence on a few products. The programme functions by specific supply arrangements, aimed at mitigating the additional costs for the supply of essential products for human consumption, for processing and as agricultural inputs, and measures to support the local agricultural production. 
The outermost regions of the EU, as identified in Art 349 of the Treaty for the functioning of the European Union (TFEU) are Guadeloupe, French Guyana, Martinique, Réunion, Saint-Barthélemy and Saint-Martin, for France; the Azores and Madeira for Portugal; and the Canary Island for Spain. 
The annual maximum funding for the measures provided by the EU are € 84,7 million for the French overseas departments, € 77,3 million for Azores and Madeira, and € 127,3 million for the Canary Island.
