Taxes on wheat and barley exports increased respectively by 40 and 30 percent.

The government approved the action plan (“road map”) for the development of the production of mineral fertilizers for the period until 2025 (hereinafter referred to as the Plan).

The plan, in particular, provides for the stimulation of investment activities of producers of mineral fertilizers; the development of the domestic market of mineral fertilizers, including the promotion of the use of mineral fertilizers in crop production and the development of a national logistics infrastructure for the mineral fertilizer sub-sector; state support for export deliveries of domestic mineral fertilizers in agreed areas (refusal to introduce export duties that negatively affect the competitiveness of Russian products on the foreign market).

The plan includes 16 positions aimed at improving the mechanisms of state regulation of the development of the production of mineral fertilizers in Russia.

The implementation of the Plan will create conditions for increasing the volume of production of mineral fertilizers by 2025 - 7.3 million tons more compared to 2016, increase the share of exports in the structure of production of mineral fertilizers by 4% and increase the consumption of mineral fertilizers by agricultural producers.

Maritime Doctrine of the Russian Federation is a fundamental document defining the state policy of the Russian Federation in the field of maritime activities - national maritime policy of the Russian Federation. Functional areas of the national marine policy: the activities of the state and society in the field of maritime transport, development and conservation of resources and ocean spaces, marine science, naval and other areas of maritime activity. Russian Federation is one of the leading countries in the world of fishing. Fisheries played a significant role in the food sector of the country and is one of the sources of employment in many coastal regions. In the short term, the bulk of the fish raw material will form the biological resources of the exclusive economic zone of the Russian Federation.

Allocation of an extra 25 billion rubles from the reserve fund to provide preferential loans to agricultural producers. The preferential loan programme for farmers was launched in 2017. Within its framework, agricultural producers can take out a short-term or investment loan at a rate of up to 5% for the development of crop production and animal husbandry, as well as for the construction, reconstruction or modernization of agricultural raw materials processing enterprises. A preferential short-term loan is issued for a period of up to 1 year, an investment loan - from 2 to 15 years.

On 6 November 2009, the government increased its rice import duty to € 120/ton ($179/ton), from € 70 previously, a measure aimed at promoting domestic rice production and reducing its dependence on imports. The higher import tariff was scheduled to become effective one month after the official announcement and will remain in place for a period of nine months.

The Government has implemented a program called "Technical and Technological Modernization and Innovative Development of Agriculture" (sub-program of the State Program 2013-2020). The Government has allocated 2.15 billion rubles (US$36.000.000).

The Government of the Russian Federation commenced the procurement of the 2016 grain crops, including wheat, rye, barley and maize. It plans to purchase up to 1 million tonnes of grain by the end of 2016, and a total of 2 million tonnes in the 2016/17 marketing year.

The objectives of the State Program are the following: meeting the needs of the domestic market in a reliable, high-quality and economically sound supply of electricity; improving the efficiency of extraction, manufacturing and processing of hydrocarbon resources to meet internal and external demand for them; increasing the efficiency of production, mining and processing of coal raw materials to meet domestic and foreign demand for them; and assistance to innovative and digital development of the fuel and energy complex.

The government approved the state program "Integrated development of rural territories" (hereinafter - the state program). The implementation period of the state program is 2020–2025.

The main objectives of the state program are to maintain the share of the rural population in the total population of Russia at a level of at least 25.3%, achieve a ratio of the average monthly disposable resources of rural and urban households to 80%, increase the share of the total area of ​​comfortable residential premises in rural areas to 50%.

The state program consists of design and process parts.

Five departmental projects are included in the project part of the state program: “Development of housing construction in rural areas and improvement of home improvement standards”, “Promotion of rural employment”, “Development of engineering infrastructure in rural areas”, “Development of transport infrastructure in rural areas”, “Improvement rural areas. "

Three departmental target programs are assigned to the process part of the state program: “Ensuring state monitoring of rural territories”, “Analytical and informational support of the integrated development of rural territories”, “Modern appearance of rural territories”.

The state program includes information on the priority development of priority territories - constituent entities of the Federation, members of the Far Eastern and North Caucasian Federal Districts, the Republic of Crimea, Sevastopol, the Kaliningrad Region, constituent entities of the Federation, some of which are part of the Arctic zone of Russia.

The total amount of financing of the state program in 2020–2025 is about 2.3 trillion rubles, including 1 trillion rubles from the federal budget.

The Strategy was developed in accordance with Federal Law dated June 28, 2014 No. 172-ФЗ “On Strategic Planning in the Russian Federation”, taking into account the decrees of the President of Russia dated January 16, 2017 No. 13 “On approval of the Fundamentals of State Policy for Regional Development of the Russian Federation for the period up to 2025 ”and dated May 7, 2018 No. 204 “ On national goals and strategic objectives of the development of the Russian Federation for the period up to 2024 ”, as well as in accordance with the Regulation on the content, composition, procedure for the development and approval of the strategy for development of Russia and the proposals prepared as part of it to improve the resettlement system in Russia and the priority areas for the deployment of productive forces (approved Government Decision of August 20, 2015 No. 870 ).

The objectives of the Strategy are to ensure sustainable and balanced spatial development of Russia, reduce inter-regional differences in the level and quality of life of people, accelerate the pace of economic growth and technological development, ensure national security.

The strategy defines the tasks, principles, priorities and main directions of the spatial development of Russia, the scenarios of spatial development, including the priority (target) scenario, promising centers of economic growth, macro-regions, promising economic specializations of the constituent entities of the Federation, target indicators of spatial development of Russia.

As part of the implementation of the Strategy, it is planned to increase the availability and quality of the main transport, energy, information and telecommunication infrastructure, reduce the level of inter-regional differentiation in the socio-economic development of the constituent entities of the Federation, reduce intra-regional socio-economic differences, expand geography and accelerate economic growth, scientific, technological and innovative development of Russia due to the socio-economic development of promising centers of economic Skogen growth, outstripping the average Russian rates of socio-economic development of the Far East, to ensure sustainable growth of the resident population in this macro-region.

The list of promising centers of economic growth includes promising cities that form large urban agglomerations and the largest urban agglomerations, which will provide a contribution to economic growth of more than 1% annually (20 centers); promising centers for economic growth of the constituent entities of the Federation, which will provide a contribution to economic growth from 0.2% to 1% annually (44 centers); promising centers for economic growth of the constituent entities of the Federation, which will provide a contribution to economic growth of up to 0.2% annually (31 centers); promising mineral resources and agro-industrial centers (27 centers); promising centers of economic growth, in which conditions have arisen for the formation of world-class scientific and educational centers (20 centers).

The strategy provides for the creation of a new mechanism for the development of territories (investment sites) with a special regime for doing business, taking into account the promising specializations of the subjects of the Federation and other features of the territories. In order to avoid duplication of state support measures, federal authorities with state support for the sectors of the economy of each specific subject of the Federation will take into account promising economic specializations of the subjects of the Federation bordering on it and which are part of one macroregion.

Infrastructural support for the socio-economic development of territories will be carried out as part of the implementation of the Comprehensive Plan for the Modernization and Expansion of the Main Infrastructure until 2024 (approved by Government Decree No. 2101-r of September 30, 2018, hereinafter referred to as the Comprehensive Plan) and national projects.

In order to mandatory include measures of the comprehensive plan and comprehensive plans for the development of infrastructure of the constituent entities of the Federation in the investment programs of natural monopoly entities, the Government of Russia will develop a procedure for the approval and approval of investment programs (plans) of natural monopoly entities, including, among other things, participation in such coordination of executive bodies of the constituent entities of the Federation.

As part of the implementation of the Strategy, it is also planned to develop and approve a set of measures to attract people in areas with significant economic potential, characterized by an unfavorable demographic situation, by stimulating internal and external migration.

The government approved the implementation plan of the Fundamentals, which aims at improving the legal regulation in the field of ensuring chemical and biological safety, including the adoption of federal laws and regulations ensuring their implementation. It is also planned to develop a state program “Ensuring the chemical and biological safety of the Russian Federation”, which will be the main document of strategic planning in the field of ensuring chemical and biological safety.

The fundamentals of the state policy of the Russian Federation in the field of ensuring chemical and biological safety for the period up to 2025 and the future perspective (hereinafter referred to as the Basics) were approved by Decree of the President of Russia dated March 11, 2019 No. 97. 

The State policy in the field of ensuring chemical and biological safety is a combination of legal, biomedical, sanitary and epidemiological, veterinary, sanitary, phytosanitary, administrative and organizational, military, financial, communication, information and other measures aimed at protecting the population and the environment from the negative effects of hazardous chemical and biological factors, the prevention of chemical and biological threats, the creation and development of a chemical monitoring system and Biological risks.

Sales would be made by the United Grain Company in tenders beginning on 4 August 2010, although on 23 July the Minister of Agriculture stated that the starting date could be postponed after taking into account the latest conditions in the drought-affected regions.

On January 29, 2018, the Government of the Russian Federation issued Resolution No. 81 “On Amending the Resolution of the Government of the Russian Federation No. 839 of September 23, 2013.” The amendment “grand-fathered” registrations of feeds that were launched prior to July 1, 2017, waiving prior registration of each GE organism for such feeds. Russia continues the ban on cultivation and breeding of genetically engineered (GE) plants and animals in the Russian Federation per Federal Law No. 358-FZ of July 3, 2016. While imports of registered GE products are permitted, currently there are no methodological guidelines for registering GE events for feed use as well as for stacked events, making it impossible for those events to be registered and in some cases preventing their import. There is a mechanism for registration of GE products for food use.

COVID-19: The government adopted "Methodical Recommendations No. МР 2.3.0171-20 Food Hygiene. Specialized diet for children and adults in self-isolation or quarantine at home in connection with COVID-19." 

These guidelines are directed on the possibility of elimination or considerable decrease in negative influence of the specified factors on the health of the population by optimization of nutrition and food consumption in connection with COVID-19 and can be used by citizens, doctors-dieticians, experts of bodies and organizations of Federal Service for Supervision of Consumer Rights Protection and Human Welfare and other persons and organizations concerned. In order to maintain normal body weight and maintain balanced body composition, it is necessary to maintain a full, adequate diet with a caloric value reduction of 200-400 kcal compared to the usual diet. At the same time, it is important to preserve the maximum variety of foodstuffs - sources of protein, fats, carbohydrates, and micronutrients, to ensure the consumption of water at least 2 liters per day. Indicatively, a child of preschool age needs at least 1 liter of free liquid per day, and children from 12 to 18 years old need 1.5 liters. All drinking water and all beverages in the diet should be considered. It is recommended to include all major traditional products in the diet: (a) bread, flour, cereals; (b) milk and dairy products; (c) meat, poultry products and fish products (fish products must be included in the diet at least twice a week); (d) oils; (e) eggs; and (f) sufficient fresh fruits and vegetables.

The comprehensive plan for the modernization and expansion of the main infrastructure for the period until 2024 was developed in accordance with Presidential Decree of May 7, 2018 No. 204 “On National Goals and Strategic Tasks of the Development of the Russian Federation for the Period until 2024”. 

The plan includes 11 federal projects. Nine projects are aimed at modernization and expansion of transport infrastructure, two federal projects are aimed at modernization and expansion of energy infrastructure. The implementation of the Comprehensive Plan will ensure the development of the West-East and North-South transport corridors for the transportation of goods, increase the level of economic connectivity of the territory of Russia through the expansion and modernization of railway, aviation, road, sea and river infrastructure.

Under the state policy of the Russian Federation in the field of public health nutrition refers to a set of measures aimed at creating conditions for the satisfaction in accordance with the requirements of medical science needs of different groups of the population in a healthy diet, taking into account their traditions, habits and economic situation. The objectives of the state in the field of healthy eating policy is the preservation and promotion of health, prevention of diseases caused by defective and unbalanced nutrition.
The main tasks of the state policy are: the expansion of the production of basic food commodities that meets modern requirements of quality and safety; the development of food products enriched with essential components, specialized products of baby food, functional purpose products, health food products and dietary supplements; development and implementation of agriculture and food industry of innovative technologies, including bio and nanotechnologies; improving nutrition in organized groups, to ensure adequate nutrition for pregnant and lactating women and children under the age of 3 years, including through special items of food and shops, improving the diet in medical institutions as an integral part of the treatment process; the development of educational programs for different groups of people on a healthy diet; monitoring of the state of nutrition.
Russian Government increased import tariffs (from 5% to 15%) on wheat and silo harvesters, for nine months from 14 February 2009.

The Government has signed a government directive approving a programme to support the transport machine manufacturing sector in 2016. The programme is designed to ensure the comprehensive development of the sector. The programme plans to support investment projects to modernise and expand capacity to cast large-sized railway car components, as well as joint projects with foreign railway machinery manufacturers. This will improve the safety of rail carriers, primarily rail freight, facilitate the optimisation of the manufacturing capacities of many enterprises and upgrade the rolling stock.

The goal of the Program is to ensure integrated and sustainable socio-economic development of the Kaliningrad region. The objectives are the following: improvement of environmental situation and ensuring achievement of environmental standards; ensuring energy security of the Kaliningrad region through the reconstruction of existing energy sources and commissioning of new energy sources; development of tourism and recreational complex and infrastructure; development of energy and transport infrastructure and communications infrastructure; creation of the conditions for ensuring highly efficient agricultural production; construction and modernization of health facilities.
Import taxes on some basic foodstuffs have been reduced.

Government policy is aimed at preservation and enhancement of forests, meeting the needs of the citizens of the Russian Federation in quality products and useful properties of forests, as well as the creation of conditions at the state level, for the sustainable and dynamic development of the forestry sector. For the implementation of the state policy in the area of ​​use, preservation, protection and reproduction of forests is necessary to achieve the following objectives: a) in the economic sphere - the effective management of the forest sector of the economy and an increase in gross domestic product, based on market demand in the forest sector; b) in the environmental field - a favorable environment for the citizens and the preservation of biosphere role of forests of Russia; c) in the social sphere - the growth of living standards of citizens related to forests and sustainable socio-economic development of forest areas.

The federal target program “Development of the water management complex of the Russian Federation in 2012–2020” (approved by Government Decree No. 350 of April 19, 2012, hereinafter referred to as the Program) is included in the state program “Reproduction and Use of Natural Resources”.

In order to implement the Decree of the President of Russia dated May 7, 2018 No. 204 “On national goals and strategic objectives of the development of the Russian Federation for the period up to 2024”, starting in 2019, measures for the restoration and environmental rehabilitation of water bodies that have lost the ability to clean themselves, as well as Prevention of depletion of water bodies, elimination of their clogging and pollution are financed within the framework of the national project “Ecology” and the federal projects “Recovery of the Volga” and “Preservation of Unique Water ’objects.”

The strategy is designed to respond to the challenges and opportunities in the challenges of youth development, define goals, priorities and instruments of the state youth policy. Strategy is cross-cutting nature, requires close interagency cooperation in its implementation. released "youth dimension" in the performance of each federal department. The purpose of the state youth policy in the medium and long term - the formation of the younger generation of Russians competitive, achieving economic, social and cultural competitiveness of Russian youth. The strategy was developed by the Ministry of Natural Resources of Russia pursuant to the order of the President of the Russian Federation dated September 18, 2012 No. Pr-2506.

The conservation strategy for rare and endangered species of animals, plants and mushrooms in the Russian Federation for the period up to 2030 (hereinafter referred to as the strategy) is aimed at ensuring the conservation and restoration of the most vulnerable part of Russia's biological diversity, their habitats, and the improvement of the Russian Red Book.

This regional Law attributes to local government plenary powers related to prevention and liquidation of animal diseases, cure thereof and protection of the population against diseases common to animals and human beings as regards capture and keeping stray animals. The Government cancelled customs duties on wheat exports, which were in place since 1 February 2015 and were due to last until the end of June. The measure aims to increase incomes of producers to cover costs of the spring crops planting campaign. It is expected that the decree will support grain prices during the period of the winter crops harvesting. A new formula for calculating the wheat exporting duty might come into effect at the beginning of the new agricultural year, on 1 July.
Import duties on soybean set up at 5 percent. Import duty on rice increased by 70 percent to USD 150 per tonne, the measure is valid until 10 September 2010.

Russia’s Federal Veterinary and Phytosanitary Surveillance Service (VPSS) announced temporary restrictions for imports of US poultry, poultry by-products, and prepared products from poultry, citing detections of harmful and banned substances in poultry products imported from the U.S. Additionally, on December 17, 2014, VPSS issued field instructions to its regional offices, introducing temporary restrictions as of December 18, 2014, on imports of nonheat-treated U.S. poultry and related goods, as well as imports of live poultry and hatching eggs from Washington State, due to HPAI detection in Washington State.

In July 2012, the Russian Government adopted the State Program for Development of Agriculture and Regulation of Agricultural Commodities Markets in 2013-2020. The Program plans to allocate 2.28 trillion rubles ($76 billion) for the development of agriculture and food markets during the period 2013-2020, including 1.5 trillion rubles ($50 billion) from the federal budget and 777 billion rubles ($26 billion) from provincial budgets. The development of the livestock industry will remain the top priority for the Ministry of Agriculture. One major change in the State Program is the method of support to agriculture will shift from subsidized interest rates toward direct income support for farmers. The Program emphasizes a social and rural development orientation, although the planned funds for these sub-programs are small. Staple food prices, including wheat and rye, frozen until 1 May 2008.

The Government introduced a special transshipment regime for Ukrainian products destined for Kazakhstan. Previously, Kazakhstan and Belarus refused to join Russia in the FTA cancelation. All truck drivers would have to receive special slips when entering the Russian territory and surrender those slips at exit points.

On August 15, 2019, Russia approved a long-term grain industry development strategy. The strategy aims to strengthen Russia's position as a global grain market producer and supplier by 2035. The strategy highlights priorities of investments in research, production, processing, storage and marketing of grain and grain products. In particular, according to the strategy, by 2035, Russia will be harvesting on average 140 million tons of grain per year, up 24 percent as compared to the 2018 level. By this time, domestic consumption should reach around 86.2 million tons per year, while exports of grains, legumes and products of their processing should reach 55.9 million tons versus 54.9 million tons of similar exports in 2018.

The strategy envisages around 281 billion rubles (or around $4.3 billion) of investment into various infrastructure projects, including the building of grain terminals in Russian seaports, and some storage facilities for grain and feed. These investments should improve logistics in the Russian grain and feed industries, according to the document. An additional 3.3 trillion rubles (over $50 billion) are to be invested in the purchasing of new agricultural equipment, including harvesters and tractors. These are private investments, as the strategy provides no details regarding the planned state aid to Russian grain producers during the coming years. According to news outlets, overall, the 2035 strategy will cost more than 4.4 trillion rubles (or $70 billion) in funds drawn from private investors, loans and government financing.

The strategy is the basis for the formation and implementation of state policy in the field of geological exploration of the subsoil, reproduction and use of the mineral resource base at the federal and regional levels.

For the purposes of the Strategy, a mineral resource base is a combination of explored and estimated mineral reserves, as well as localized and predicted resources.

The strategy provides for increasing the mineral resource base by increasing the investment attractiveness of geological exploration at all stages, increasing the quality of forecasting and searching for new deposits, increasing the efficiency of developing known, including undeveloped, deposits by introducing modern technologies for processing, integrated mineral extraction , increasing the level of geological exploration of the country.

In accordance with the needs of the economy, the economic conditions of development and the geological prospects of building up, all strategic and most significant types of minerals are divided into three groups: minerals, the provision of reserves of which under any scenario of economic development will satisfy the necessary needs until 2035 and beyond; minerals, the achieved production levels of which are not adequately provided with reserves of developed deposits for the period until 2035; scarce minerals, the domestic consumption of which is largely provided by forced imports and / or stockpiles.

For each of these groups of minerals, the indicators of reproduction of their reserves are determined, taking into account the state of the resource base and the rate of repayment in the bowels. The reproduction of mineral reserves is envisaged on the basis of intensification of regional geological study of the subsoil, intensification of exploration and subsequent stages, taking into account the geological prospects and territorial features of the country's development.

The strategy also provides for economic incentives for geological exploration of the subsoil, reproduction and development of the mineral resource base, the formation of a system of information, scientific, technological and personnel support for the development of the mineral resource base.

For the development of new industrial territories, support is provided for geological exploration of the early stages at the expense of the federal budget and the creation of a special tax regime to attract private investment.

Within the framework of the Strategy, it is planned to develop planning for geological exploration within the natural boundaries of the mineralogical provinces and mineral resource centers, distinguished taking into account the possibilities of transport and energy infrastructure of the territories.

The implementation of the Strategy is foreseen in two stages.

At the first stage (until 2024), in particular, it is planned to increase state funding for large-scale regional geological explorations, create a unified fund of geological information on the subsoil, develop the necessary program and design documents to ensure the concentration of financial resources, technological and human potential to achieve indicators of the development of mineral raw materials base. At the end of the first stage, the Strategy will be updated based on the results achieved and the forecast of mining for the period after 2024.

At the second stage (2025–2035), it is planned to continue the work necessary to increase the investment attractiveness of Russian subsoil. Based on this, a model of a self-regulatory system to achieve the optimal balance of growth and repayment of mineral reserves will be created. It is also planned to complete the transformations associated with improving the system for collecting, processing, analyzing, storing and providing geological information for use, and strengthening scientific, technical and personnel support for geological exploration.

The strategy is aimed, inter alia, at improving the scientific and technical support for geological exploration, increasing the availability of geological organizations with geological specialists on the basis of the development and implementation of a training and retraining program.

COVID-19: On 26 March 2020, a Federal Law came into force allowing the Russian government to set maximum prices for any medicines and medical devices for up to 90 days in case of an emergency or the threat of the spread of dangerous diseases (including COVID-19).

According to the new Law, if after 30 days of monitoring retail prices for pharmaceuticals and medical devices the government detects price increases of 30% or more, it can then introduce restrictions on the prices of these products.

In particular, the government will have the right to determine, for a period of up to 90 days, a list of medicines and medical devices for which it can set manufacturers’ maximum selling prices and maximum wholesale and retail mark-ups.

Maximum prices set by the government will apply to manufacturers, distributors and pharmacies.

It is important to note that this right is granted to the government for any medicine and medical device without exception.

In addition, the Russian State Duma is considering a bill to increase penalties and sanctions for any company violating these rules.

The government approved the Export Development Strategy for the agricultural engineering industry until 2025 (hereinafter - the Strategy).

The strategy characterizes the state of the industry and determines the basic principles of state policy in the field of supporting the export of agricultural machinery for the medium term.

The draft Strategy was developed in accordance with Federal Law dated June 28, 2014 No. 172-ФЗ “On Strategic Planning in the Russian Federation”, taking into account the Forecast of the Long-Term Socio-Economic Development of the Russian Federation for the Period until 2030, and the Forecast of Scientific and Technological Development of the Russian Federation until 2030 year , government programs "development of industry and increase its competitiveness" , "development of foreign economic activity" , Strategies for development of agricultural engineering of Russia on the item IRS until 2030 (approved by the Decree of the Government on July 7, 2017 No. 1455-p).

The purpose of the Strategy is accelerated export growth in the agricultural engineering industry.

The strategy envisages providing support to Russian manufacturers of agricultural machinery, expanding the range of products, creating conditions for sustainable growth in exports of Russian agricultural machinery products.

Strategy Objectives:

- an increase in the volume of deliveries of products of Russian agricultural engineering in traditional markets;

- expansion of the geography of deliveries of products of Russian agricultural engineering;

- involvement of new domestic manufacturers in export deliveries.

As a result of the implementation of the Strategy, it is planned to increase the volume of export of agricultural machinery - from 10,255 million rubles in 2018 to 30,220 million rubles by 2025. The number of enterprises exporting domestic agricultural machinery products should increase from 48 in 2018 to 70 by 2025 (more than 80% of all domestic enterprises). The number of countries - importers of Russian agricultural engineering products should increase from 35 countries in 2018 to 65 by 2025. It is planned that each of the market segments individually will show a two-fold or more increase in exported products.

The implementation of the Strategy will allow for the formation of a structured approach to solving the key problems facing domestic manufacturers and exporters, and will contribute to an increase in the load of production capacities and production volumes of agricultural machinery, and an increase in demand for raw materials, components and materials of Russian production.

The plan includes 16 positions aimed at improving the mechanisms of state regulation of the development of the production of mineral fertilizers in Russia.

The implementation of the Plan will create conditions for increasing the volume of production of mineral fertilizers by 2025 - 7.3 million tons more compared to 2016, increase the share of exports in the structure of production of mineral fertilizers by 4% and increase the consumption of mineral fertilizers by agricultural producers.

The main objective of the Programme, which updates and replaces measures of the previous State Policy on Energy Efficiency Increase through the Use of Renewables for the Period up to 2020 (2009), is to “ensure reliable supply of the country’s fuel and energy resources, increase the efficiency of their use, and reduce of anthropogenic impacts of the energy sector on the environment”.

This new version keeps the target of a 40% decrease of energy intensity of the economy between 2007 and 2020, but alters the 4.5% share of electricity generation from renewable energy sources target to 2.5% by 2020 (excluding large hydro over 25 MW). The Programme calls for diverse measures to attain those targets, including:
– evaluating the technological and economic potential of efficient renewables use
– providing subsidies from the state budget in order to compensate for the costs of grid connection for renewables
– installation of smart meters (18.9% of metering devices by 2020)
– increasing the availability of energy infrastructure – reducing the number of steps required to gain access to the grid (from 8 to 5) and reducing the delay of connection to the grid (from 276 to 40 days)
– raising public awareness on energy conservation and energy efficiency.

The State Programme is composed of seven sub-programmes:
– SP1: Energy conservation and energy efficiency improvement
– SP2: Development and modernisation of the power industry
– SP3: Development of the oil industry
– SP4: Development of the gas industry
– SP5: Restructuring and development of the coal industry
– SP6: Development of renewable energy
– SP7: Ensuring the implementation of the state programme.

The Strategy for Innovative Development of the Russian Federation for the Period until 2020 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategy) is developed on the basis of the provisions of the Concept for Long-Term Socio-Economic Development of the Russian Federation for the Period until 2020 (hereinafter referred to as the Concept) in accordance with the Federal Law “On Science and the State Scientific and Technical politics. ”

The strategy is designed to answer the challenges and threats facing Russia in the field of innovative development, to determine the goals, priorities and tools of the state innovation policy. At the same time, the Strategy sets long-term development guidelines for subjects of innovative activity, as well as guidelines for financing the fundamental and applied science sector and supporting the commercialization of developments.

In addition, the Strategy is based on the results of a comprehensive assessment of innovative potential and a long-term scientific and technological forecast. The provisions of the Strategy should be taken into account when developing concepts and programs for the socio-economic development of Russia.

The main objective of the Strategy is to build and maintain the forces of national security of internal and external conditions favorable to the realization of strategic national priorities. National interests of the Russian Federation for the long term are: the development of democracy and civil society, enhancing the competitiveness of the national economy; to ensure the inviolability of the constitutional order, territorial integrity and sovereignty of the Russian Federation; in the Russian Federation into a world power, which seeks to maintain strategic stability and mutually beneficial relations in a multipolar world.

In 2013, the government adopted the Methodological Recommendation for Emergency Situations (Plan), whose components related to nutrition are the following:

The type of life support of the population in the emergency zone; the type of ZhON in the emergency zone (activities to satisfy any primary need of the population in the emergency zone). Note- The types of life support of the population include medical support, water, food, housing, utilities, basic necessities, transport and information support

Supply of food and water to the affected population in disaster areas, evacuation areas and forces involved in emergency response is based on the physiological principle for the unemployed (and energy sufficiency)

The daily needs of the affected population for food, water, utilities, household fuel are calculated according to its predicted number and standards of emergency support. The total need for these types of livelihoods by multiplying daily requirements by the length of the primary life support period

When assessing the needs of the affected population for food, it should be considered that in the first 1.2 days after the disaster, before organizing the preparation of hot food in the emergency zone, it will be possible to use only dry rations, canned and other products that do not require heat treatment. Bread will need to be delivered from neighboring settlements by any means of transport. It is necessary to take into account the need to deliver ready-made baby food to infants and children up to 2 years of age, and for some categories of patients, special nutrition before their urgent evacuation from the emergency zone. In determining the volumes necessary for the affected population of bread, meat and fish products, potatoes, vegetables, pasta and cereals, fats, sugar, salt should be based on the need to organize two hot meals a day and once a day, canned foods or prefabricated rations. The food supply standards are given in tables P 1.1, P 1.2, P 1.5 of appendix1.

Upon receipt of information on the possible evacuation of the population in the evacuation areas, the condition of the housing stock of settlements and the degree of their readiness to receive the evacuated population shall be clarified: condition of water sources and water supply systems and their capabilities: condition of public catering and trade points, their production capacities.

The population who received severe and moderate lesions as a result of the accident after providing emergency medical care at specially developed medical centers is sent to medical institutions where they are provided with treatment and nutrition according to special diets of medical nutrition.

The Strategy for the Development of the Marine Activities of the Russian Federation until 2030 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategy) was adopted by the government in 2019. In the new version of the Strategy, taking into account the current political and socio-economic situation in the country and the world, the priorities, goals and objectives of the Russian maritime activities for the long term are determined, the forecast values ​​of the target indicators of the II stage of the Strategy are specified and the forecast values ​​of the target indicators of its III stage are determined.

The implementation of the goals and objectives of the national maritime policy defined by the new version of the Strategy will make it possible to strengthen Russia's position among the leading maritime powers by 2030 and achieve sustainable development of the main areas of maritime activity.

The Institute of Nutrition has been asked to test the validity of the study, while the European Commission's Directorate General for Health & Consumers has also been contacted to explain the European Union's position.

The government issued Order No. 1635-p on increasing subsidies by 260.1 million rubles (US$ 4 292 720) to support land reclamation in 54 provinces. Total amount of federal support allocated for land reclamation is 2 274 billion rubles (US$ 37 530 400). The subsidies are allocated with the framework of Federal Targeted Program “Development of Land Reclamation of Agricultural Lands for the Period 2014-2020.

By the Russian Government decree № 259-p from 28 February 2012 Russia has introduced and distributed around its regions the subsidies for agricultural development in the Russia’s regions for 2012. Total amount of subsidies is 6.9 billion Russian roubles or 179 million Euros.

The government approved the Amber Industry Development Strategy for the period up to 2025 (hereinafter - the Strategy).

The strategy contains an analysis of the Russian amber industry, the goals and main principles of state policy in the amber industry, a forecast of domestic demand for amber products, and economic indicators of the industry's development.

The strategy is planned to be implemented in two stages.

At the first stage (2017–2018), it is planned to solve the problems of preserving the potential of the industry and reducing the negative impact of adverse external economic conditions. It is planned to launch tools and measures of state support. This will save industrial assets, qualified personnel of the industry. It is planned to increase the processing of amber raw materials in Russia.

At the second stage (2019–2025), it is expected to achieve the level of leading countries in terms of finished product output and added value when processing amber raw materials. Amber enterprises will use the best available technology.

The strategy provides for a phased increase in such target indicators as the extraction of amber raw materials, the production of amber processed products, employment in the field of amber processing, the number of functioning tourist and cultural sites associated with amber.

As a result of the implementation of the Strategy, the processing of amber raw materials in Russia will increase, export opportunities of the industry enterprises will increase, and conditions will be created for technological modernization of enterprises.

COVID-19: The Russian Federal Customs Service announced the introduction of a zero import rate for goods preventing the spread of COVID-19.

The list of goods subject to a reduced rate is determined by the Eurasian Economic Commission (EEC) in Decision No. 21 dated 16 March 2020 and includes individual protective gear, disinfectants, diagnostic reagents and certain types of medical equipment and materials.

This exemption can be applied to the goods listed provided that they are imported to Russia and released for internal consumption during the period 16 March to 30 September 2020.

At the same time, EEC Decision No. 41 prohibits the exportation of individual protective gear, means of personal protection, disinfectants and certain other medical goods listed in this Decision until 30 September 2020.

Thus, only copies of the constituent documents and the foreign trade agreement (contract) for the supply of white sugar have to be attached to the application. In addition, any company with relevant contracts can now apply for a permit.

The money was allocated to subsidize credit organizations that provide preferential loans to enterprises of the agro-industrial complex. The preferential loan program for farmers was launched in 2017. The decree contains a provision that, should Russia’s food ban be lifted, country-specific 2016 TRQs for the U.S. and EU with regard to beef and poultry are to be distributed among eligible Russian importers within five working days.

The government approved the Strategy for the Development of the Forestry Complex of the Russian Federation until 2030 (hereinafter - the Strategy). This is an industry strategic planning document that defines goals and objectives, ways to achieve them, priorities, stages of implementation of state policy in the field of forestry development in Russia.

The strategy is aimed at increasing the long-term competitiveness of the forest industry, increasing the contribution of the forest sector to the country's socio-economic development, the efficient use, protection, reproduction of forests by achieving sustainable forest management.

The main directions of the Strategy are the development of export-oriented production of pulp, the growth of the production of container board and sanitary products for the domestic market, the development of the production of lumber, plywood-plate production, furniture, and wooden housing construction, oriented equally to the domestic market.

The government approved the Federal Scientific and Technical Program for the Development of Genetic Technologies for 2019–2027 (hereinafter - the Program).

The main goals of the Program are a comprehensive solution to the problems of the accelerated development of genetic technologies, including genetic editing technologies, the creation of scientific and technological reserves for medicine, agriculture and industry, the improvement of the biological emergency prevention and control system in this area.

Directions for the implementation of the Program: biosafety and ensuring technological independence, genetic technologies for the development of agriculture, medicine, industrial microbiology.

The program provides for the creation and development on the basis of scientific and educational organizations of laboratories and centers conducting research in the field of genetic technologies, their technical support, research and development using genetic technologies, including the development of biological drugs, diagnostic systems and immunobiological agents for healthcare, biotechnology for agriculture and industry.

It is expected that as a result of the implementation of the Program, scientific and technological reserves for medicine, agriculture and industry will be created. Using genetic editing technologies, plant and animal lines will be developed, including aquaculture, in demand in the real sector of the economy. It is also planned to develop models of human diseases using genetic technologies in vitro and in vivo, the functioning of bioresource centers that ensure the formation, storage and provision of collection samples in accordance with international standards, the creation of bioinformation and genetic databases, the creation of at least three world-class genomic research centers . The development of biological preparations, diagnostic systems and immunobiological agents for healthcare will be ensured,

The program provides for the formation of a plan for its implementation for each three-year period and a comprehensive research plan. The responsible executor and coordinator of the Program is the Ministry of Education and Science of Russia. Methodological, informational, analytical and organizational support for the implementation of the Program is assigned to the Kurchatov Institute, which is the main scientific organization of the Program.

Implementation of the Program will be financed within the framework of state programs “Scientific and Technological Development of the Russian Federation” (including within the framework of the national project “Science”), “Development of Education”, “Development of Health Care”, “Development of Industry and Increasing Its Competitiveness”, “Development pharmaceutical and medical industry ”for 2013–2020,“ Information Society (2011–2020), ”the State Program for the Development of Agriculture and Regulation of Agricultural Products, Raw Materials and food, as well as due to budgetary appropriations of the budgets of the constituent entities of the Federation and extrabudgetary sources.

The government approved the Strategy for the development of Russian seaports in the Caspian basin, rail and road approaches to them until 2030 (hereinafter - the Strategy).

The Strategy was developed taking into account the Concept of long-term socio-economic development of the Russian Federation for the period until 2020 (approved by the Government Decree of November 17, 2008 No. 1662-r), the Concept for the demographic policy of the Russian Federation for the period until 2025 (approved by Decree of the President of Russia of 9 October 2007 №1351), the national security Strategy of the Russian Federation (approved by the Decree of the President of Russia on December 31, 2015 №683), Program of action for the strategic interests of the Russian F eration in the Caspian region in the 2016-2018 years.

The main goal of the Strategy is to strengthen the economic and geopolitical presence of Russia in the Caspian Sea, expand and deepen economic and cultural ties with the countries of the Caspian basin, create conditions for additional socio-economic development of the Caspian region of Russia by increasing the flow of international trade passing through the ports of the Caspian basin.

Targeted directions for the implementation of the Strategy:

- development of the Russian Caspian transport hub and its inclusion in the international trade system;

- creating a sustainable transport and logistics corridor with Iran, India and the Gulf countries;

- socio-economic development of the Caspian region;

- development of export-oriented business in the Caspian region through the Russian Caspian transport hub;

- reduction of existing logistics costs;

- Strengthening the country's defense and security in the Caspian.

The strategy provides for the solution of regulatory, tariff, investment, operational and institutional tasks.

Regulatory tasks include improving the competitiveness of freight and passenger traffic through Russian Caspian ports by simplifying administrative procedures (including speeding up customs procedures during cargo transportation, prompt coordination of projects to modernize port infrastructure), creating favorable conditions for the development of domestic and international tourism in this region (including simplification of the customs regime).

Tariff tasks - the formation and administration of uniform competitive tariffs for transportation through the Caspian transport hub.

Investment objectives are the modernization of the existing and the creation of a new logistics and transport infrastructure for the development of freight and passenger transportation, including port infrastructure, as well as long and near road and rail approaches to seaports.

Operational objectives - the introduction of a planning and project management system that reveals the export potential of the Caspian region, in particular production and logistics clusters, by creating the necessary legislative and administrative conditions and institutions.

Institutional tasks are the creation of incentives for the development of agriculture and industrial production, which, together with the development of transport infrastructure, can provide a synergistic effect for the development of the region, including the formation of development institutions and support for such projects.

The strategy is planned to be implemented in three stages: the first stage (until 2020) - preparatory, the second stage (2020–2025) - the main, the third stage (2026–2030) - promising.

Target directions, tasks, mechanisms for implementing the Strategy are aimed at creating a sustainable transport and logistics corridor, developing trade and tourism, primarily with Iran, India and the Persian Gulf countries. As part of the promising stage of the Strategy implementation, it is planned to study the issue of developing trade relations with all the Caspian countries, taking into account the expansion of the capacities of the new deep-sea port (terminal).

The implementation of the Strategy and the fulfillment of its indicators will allow to ensure grain export volumes through the ports of the Caspian basin up to 7 million tons by 2030, and the volume of freight traffic on other dry cargoes up to 7 million tons; to attract the Russian tourist flow to the Caspian region - up to 30 thousand people a year; create more than 2 thousand new jobs.

The strategy for preventing the spread of antimicrobial resistance in the Russian Federation for the period up to 2030 was approved by the Government Decree of September 25, 2017 No. 2045-r (hereinafter - the Strategy).

The purpose of the Strategy is to prevent and limit the spread of antimicrobial resistance in Russia. The strategy defines the state policy to prevent and limit the spread of the resistance of microorganisms to antimicrobials, chemical and biological agents.

According to expert estimates, antimicrobial resistance is the cause of more than 700 thousand deaths in the world annually, by 2050 this figure may increase to 10 million.

In order to implement systemic measures aimed at preventing the formation of microorganisms resistant to antibiotics, a plan for the implementation of the Strategy (hereinafter referred to as the plan) was approved by a decree.

The plan, in particular, provides for improving state regulation in the field of the use of antimicrobial drugs in healthcare and veterinary medicine, developing and updating clinical recommendations on the provision of medical care for infectious and parasitic diseases, taking into account optimal antimicrobial therapy regimens, organizing and monitoring residual antibiotics in food raw materials and food products, conducting information campaigns on samples lemmas of antimicrobial resistance, increasing the level of professional training of specialists.

The Government has adopted an import ban for agricultural and food products originating from Ukraine. The ban is a copy of the similar trade restriction imposed on the United States, EU and a number of Western countries by Russian President Order No. 560 adopted on August 6th of 2014. The Ukrainian ban was introduced by the Russian Government Decree No 842 adopted on August 13th, 2015 when Ukraine joined Western countries in imposing sanctions on Russian goods and services. Its implementation was delayed until January 1st, 2016, in hope to change EU-Ukraine FTA terms. Multilateral negotiations aimed at this goal ended without tangible results in the middle of December 2015. The new ban includes meat and meat products, seafood, fruits, nuts, vegetables and processed products. The impact from the ban will not be significant. Once substantial, Ukrainian exports of these products shrunk in recent years as Russia imposed various restrictions using SPS arguments. The total amount of impacted Ukrainian agricultural and food exports will amount to $116.4 million. This comprises approximately 0.9 percent of Ukrainian agricultural exports. The complete list of banned agricultural products is provided in RSATO017 GAIN Report. It includes large product groups under the following HS Codes: HS 0201, 0202 0203 0207, 0210, 0301, 0302-0308, 0401-0406, 0701-0714, 0801-0811, 0813 1601, 190190 and 210690.

The government approved the Development Strategy for Agricultural Engineering in Russia for the period up to 2030 (hereinafter - the Strategy).

The Strategy was developed taking into account the forecast for the long-term socio-economic development of Russia for the period up to 2030 and the forecast for the scientific and technological development of Russia until 2030.

The Strategy actualizes the goals and objectives of the development of the industry, which were provided for by the Strategy for the Development of Agricultural Engineering for the period up to 2020 that was in force until now (approved by order of the Ministry of Industry and Trade of Russia in 2011).

The purpose of the Strategy is the achievement by Russian manufacturers of agricultural machinery of a share in the domestic market of at least 80% and a share of export deliveries of at least 50% of shipments to the domestic market.

Strategy Objectives:

- ensuring equal competitive conditions with foreign manufacturers of agricultural machinery;

- creating favorable conditions for the development of agricultural machinery exports, ensuring a stable growth in export supplies;

- stimulating the growth of investments in research and development of new types of competitive agricultural machinery;

- Improving the system of training engineering personnel for agricultural engineering;

- stimulating the development of the production of components for agricultural machinery.

The forecast indicators of the Strategy are determined on the basis of the indicators of the State Program for the Development of Agriculture and the Regulation of Agricultural Products, Raw Materials and Food Markets for 2013–2020 (approved by the Government Decree of July 14, 2012 No. 717) and the state program “Development of Industry and Increasing Its Competitiveness” ( approved by the Government Decree of April 15, 2014 No. 328).

Among the most important results of the Strategy is the realization of the potential of the domestic market with a further reorientation of domestic agricultural engineering products to the markets of the CIS countries and the countries of the European Union, North Africa, South Africa, Australia, China and North America.

The strategy for preventing the spread of antimicrobial resistance in the Russian Federation for the period up to 2030 was approved by the Government Decree of September 25, 2017 No. 2045-r (hereinafter - the Strategy).

The purpose of the Strategy is to prevent and limit the spread of antimicrobial resistance in Russia. The strategy defines the state policy to prevent and limit the spread of the resistance of microorganisms to antimicrobials, chemical and biological agents.

According to expert estimates, antimicrobial resistance is the cause of more than 700 thousand deaths in the world annually, by 2050 this figure may increase to 10 million.

In order to implement systemic measures aimed at preventing the formation of microorganisms resistant to antibiotics, a plan for the implementation of the Strategy (hereinafter referred to as the plan) was approved by a decree.

The plan, in particular, provides for improving state regulation in the field of the use of antimicrobial drugs in healthcare and veterinary medicine, developing and updating clinical recommendations on the provision of medical care for infectious and parasitic diseases, taking into account optimal antimicrobial therapy regimens, organizing and monitoring residual antibiotics in food raw materials and food products, conducting information campaigns on samples lemmas of antimicrobial resistance, increasing the level of professional training of specialists.

The conditions and procedure for the provision of palliative medical care, including the provision of essential drugs, including narcotic and psychotropic drugs, as well as medical devices, including those designed to maintain the functions of organs and systems of the human body for use at home, were clarified. The average standards for the volume and financial costs per unit volume of palliative care in outpatient settings, including at home, have been established. 

The amendments made to the Program also specify guarantees for citizens undergoing preventive medical examinations, including as part of a medical examination.

It has been established that regional authorities in the field of health care will have to arrange for citizens to undergo preventive medical examinations and medical examinations, including in the evenings and on Saturday, as well as provide citizens with the possibility of remote registration for medical examinations. Information on medical organizations, on the basis of which citizens can undergo preventive medical examinations, including medical examination, should be posted on the official websites of these authorities. The average standards of the volume of medical care during the passage of preventive medical examinations, including in the framework of the medical examination, have been clarified.

In addition, the deadlines for carrying out diagnostic instrumental and laboratory studies in the provision of primary health care, as well as the deadlines for establishing a diagnosis of cancer are set no more than 14 calendar days from the date of the research. The deadline for registering for oncologist’s follow-up for a patient with an identified oncological disease is also set - no more than three working days from the moment of diagnosis of the oncological disease.

The criteria for accessibility and quality of care are supplemented by indicators reflecting the proportion of newly diagnosed diseases during preventive medical examinations, including as part of the clinical examination, the proportion of newly diagnosed oncological diseases during routine medical examinations, as well as the proportion of patients who received palliative care and pain relief.

In 2013, the government adopted the Methodological Recommendation for Emergency Situations (Plan), whose components related to nutrition are the following:

The type of life support of the population in the emergency zone; the type of ZhON in the emergency zone (activities to satisfy any primary need of the population in the emergency zone). Note- The types of life support of the population include medical support, water, food, housing, utilities, basic necessities, transport and information support

Supply of food and water to the affected population in disaster areas, evacuation areas and forces involved in emergency response is based on the physiological principle for the unemployed (and energy sufficiency)

The daily needs of the affected population for food, water, utilities, household fuel are calculated according to its predicted number and standards of emergency support. The total need for these types of livelihoods by multiplying daily requirements by the length of the primary life support period

When assessing the needs of the affected population for food, it should be considered that in the first 1.2 days after the disaster, before organizing the preparation of hot food in the emergency zone, it will be possible to use only dry rations, canned and other products that do not require heat treatment. Bread will need to be delivered from neighboring settlements by any means of transport. It is necessary to take into account the need to deliver ready-made baby food to infants and children up to 2 years of age, and for some categories of patients, special nutrition before their urgent evacuation from the emergency zone. In determining the volumes necessary for the affected population of bread, meat and fish products, potatoes, vegetables, pasta and cereals, fats, sugar, salt should be based on the need to organize two hot meals a day and once a day, canned foods or prefabricated rations. The food supply standards are given in tables P 1.1, P 1.2, P 1.5 of appendix1.

Upon receipt of information on the possible evacuation of the population in the evacuation areas, the condition of the housing stock of settlements and the degree of their readiness to receive the evacuated population shall be clarified: condition of water sources and water supply systems and their capabilities: condition of public catering and trade points, their production capacities.

The population who received severe and moderate lesions as a result of the accident after providing emergency medical care at specially developed medical centers is sent to medical institutions where they are provided with treatment and nutrition according to special diets of medical nutrition.

The Government has enacted Federal Law No. 206-FZ “On plant quarantine”. The scope of this Federal Law shall be to ensure plant protection and protection of the territory of the Russian Federation against introduction and spreading of pests, and prevention of damages caused thereby. This Federal Law states that in the sphere of plant protection shall be applicable international agreements of the Russian Federation, international standards on phytosanitary arrangements, regional standards, guidelines and (or) recommendations in the sphere of plant quarantine. If by an international agreement of the Russian Federation are stated other norms that those envisaged by this Federal Law than shall be applicable the provisions of the international agreement of the Russian Federation. The Government shall have the following plenary powers: (a) elaboration and implementation of unified state policy; and (b) appointment of the authorized federal state bodies in the sphere of plant quarantine. Authorized federal executive body in the sphere of supervision and control in the plant quarantine shall have the following plenary powers: (a) organization and performance of state quarantine phytosanitary control (supervision); (b) analysis of phytosanitary risks; (c) phytosanitary certification; (d) establishment of phytosanitary state of the national territory; (e) application of provisional restrictions on import to the Russian Federation of produce subject to quarantine inspection; (f) phytosanitary disinfection; and (g) licensing of activities phytosanitary disinfection. The authorized federal executive body in the sphere of supervision and control in the plant quarantine shall provide access to information related to plant quarantine.

On January 21, 2020, Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a new Food Security Doctrine for Russia. According to the Russian Ministry of Agriculture, the emergence of new risks and threats to food security associated with economic sanctions, Russia’s accession to the WTO and enhanced integration processes within the Eurasian Economic Union prompted the revision of the Doctrine. In addition, as noted by Prime Minister Medvedev and the Ministry in the past, Russia has already met most of the targets of the Doctrine adopted in 2010, which was aimed at self-sufficiency.
The new section of the Doctrine devoted to national interests related to food security aims to prevent the import and distribution of genetically modified organisms for planting, and prohibits raising and breeding animals whose genetic code has been engineered or that carry genetic material of artificial origin as key provisions. The only exception to the ban is the import and sowing of genetically modified organisms for examination and research purposes, as well as the growing of such plants and breeding of such animals for examination and research purposes, according to the Doctrine.
Furthermore, the new Doctrine expanded the list of self-sufficiency indicators to include vegetables, melons and gourds with a value of 90 percent, fruit and berries at 60 percent, and seeds at 75 percent.

a. Mass screening and testing for COVID-19 will continue nationwide.
b. Masks must be worn in public at all times.
c. All resumed services must adhere to health guidelines from the Ministry of health (hand hygiene, mask wearing and social distancing).
d. Electronic payments and online banking services should be used whenever possible.

e. Individual sporting activity in open spaces is permitted however sports facilities shall remain closed.
f. Public and private transport will resume within the same province.
g. Bus operators will ensure passengers maintain social distancing and only passengers with masks will be allowed onboard.

c. Gyms and recreational centers will remain closed.

In Rwanda, NTDs include Soil-Transmitted Helminth infections (STH –Ascariasis, Trichuriasis and Hookworm), Schistosomiasis (SCH), Scabies and other ectoparasites (Tungiasis or Jigger disease), Podoconiosis, Rabies, Snakebite envenoming (SBE), Trachoma, Cysticercosis, Mycetoma, Lymphatic filariasis, Onchocerciasis and probably Human African Trypanosomiasis (HAT). All these neglected diseases are an obstacle to socio-economic development and quality of life of the Rwandan people.
This is the first NTD Strategic plan or NTD master plan (most used terminology in NTDs international community) in the country, to be implemented in six-year term for the period of 2019-2024. In compliance with the national vision, the MOH will be leading its implementation through Rwanda Biomedical Center (RBC). The goal is to make Rwanda free from NTDs as public health problem by 2024 through the implementation of WHO recommended public health strategies for prevention and control of NTDs. These interventions include preventive chemotherapy, case management, vector control and surveillance, provision of safe water, improved sanitation and hygiene and veterinary public health. This is only achievable through multi-sectoral collaboration, decentralization for community and local leadership engagement and ownership.

7. To enhance systems for the timely production of quality and credible health budget and expenditure information to inform policy dialogue and decision making.
