April 2012, The Government of Vietnam approved the Sustainable Development Strategy of Vietnam for 2011-2020. The overall objective of the strategy is to increase the sustainability and efficiency, coupled with the progressive, social justice, protection of natural resources and environment, socio-political stability, independence protection, protecting sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of the country. 
The specific objectives of this strategy include ensuring food security and food safety, sustainable rural and agricultural development, improving the quality of health care and sanitary conditions, using efficiently land and water resources, protecting the marine environment, coastal areas, developing forests, strengthening conservation and development of biodiversity and climate change mitigation and adaptation.

The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MARD) announced the set up of salt training programmes in production techniques. Salt farming is a traditional occupation; the country's salt production is expected to reach about 1 MMT for 2012, 20 percent more than last year (MARD, 27 February 2012).

According to a media report, a Steering Committee for Price Regulation will be established for conducting research and assist the government in reviewing major policies on price regulations. The committee will identify detailed measures to control the price of several commodities and services, including foodstuff, in accordance with the national macroeconomic stability goals (Viet Nam Net, 15 May 2015).
Rice export ban imposed from May to July 2008.

The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development has approved an agricultural land use plan for the Mekong Delta region, in response to climate change. The plan aims at promoting and exploiting the advantages of the sub-region in the agricultural production towards enhancing added value, sustainability and effective response to extreme weather events caused by climate change (Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, 08 May 2014).

Thailand’s Bank for Agriculture and Agricultural Co-operatives has approved THB 15 billion (US$ 464 million) in financial aid to rubber farmers. The Bank will also help 360 000 farmers by reconsidering their debts. Rubber prices have continued to fall in 2014 reaching a five-year low in August, because of domestic oversupply and rising stockpiles in China, the world’s largest rubber user. Furthermore, a new 10-year Rubber Development Plan started in September aims to reduce production costs and adopt efficient technologies to improve the quality of rubber products to fetch higher prices. Another goal of the plan is to reduce the total rubber output by 700 000 tonnes in seven years by encouraging farmers to grow alternative plants with higher economic returns and/or adopt mixed cultivation.

Vietnam’s import tariffs for ASEAN imports went into effect for the period 2016-2018 starting on September 1 , 2016. Accordingly, vegetable oils imported from a number of ASEAN countries have started enjoying a zero percent import tariff since September 1, 2016.

The Government of Viet Nam presents the National Action Plans to achieve the 17 SDG by 2030, with the overall goals and key tasks to be implemented during the 2017-2020 period and during 2021-2030 period. 
The main tasks include to enable the legal framework, to improve the effectiveness of State management and the human capacity, to strengthen research on and application of science and technology, and technology transfer to support the implementation of sustainable development goals, with particular attention being given to environmental, clean and new energy technologies, and to develop the database to monitor the SDGs achievement and facilitate the evidence based policy making.

Rice exporters (members of the Vietnam Food Association) are requested to stockpile 1 million tonnes of rice -milled basis- for a period of up to three months in order to support domestic market during the harvesting period for the main (winterspring) crop. Rice will be purchased at a price of VND 5 000/kg (USD 240/tonne) between 15 March and 30 April 2012. Companies buying rice under the scheme are to be provided with interest-free loans by banks.

The Vietnam Food Association (VFA) announced a Minimum Export Price (MEP) for 25 percent rice early this week. Price for a rice export contract should be no lower than US$ 340 per ton, FOB basis, in order to get final approval from VFA.
Viet Nam and Sri Lanka have agreed to strive for US 1 billion in two-way trade in the years to come (Viet Nam Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 14 October 2011).

Following a technical review and assessment, MARD/PPD notified USDA’s Animal-Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) that a pre-fumigation phosphine regime would be accepted for U.S. wheat, corn, and  Dried Distillers Grain (DDGs) starting September 1, 2017. Accordingly, U.S. exporters will need to comply with all agreed treatment procedures before they export their products to Vietnam.

On June 19, 2015, the Vietnam National Assembly ratified the Law on Animal Health which entered into force on July 1, 2016 and provides some new provisions on quarantine and hygiene inspection for food of animal origin. The Law stipulates that MARD is responsible for issuing the List of terrestrial animals and food of animal origin subject to quarantine and the List of terrestrial animals and food of animal origin exempted from quarantine.

Ensure an adequate supply of urea fertilizer for the coming winter-spring rice crop 2010-11. PetroVietnam Fertilizer and Chemicals Company (PVFCCo) closely with ministries has begun, three months ahead of schedule, to collect carbon dioxide from industrial smoke discharged from its fertilizer plant to increase the scale of production. The carbon-dioxide collection project will allow the company to increase its urea fertilizer output from 740,000 tones to 800,000 tones per year.

The Government will provide subsidies to rice farmers if their crops are damaged due to natural disasters, in addition to their regular annual subsidies, effective in 1 July 2012. Fertiliser and pesticides subsidies (70%) will be applied when losses top 70 percent, similarly 50 percent subsidies will apply for 30-70 percent crops losses. In addition, the Government will also pay for 70 per cent of the cost of reclaiming fallow land, or rehabilitating land for wet rice cultivation. The decree also regulates other subsidies for land used specifically for cultivating wet rice (Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, 15 May 2012).

Vietnam Trade Promotion Agency and Pakistan’s Directorate on Trade Development signed MOU on promoting bilateral trade. Accordingly, the Trade Promotion Authorities of the two countries will coordinate in implementing trade promotion programs, exchanging the list of exhibition and trade fairs to be organized annually at the respective countries to call for the interest and participation of the businesses.
Since March 19, 2017, Vietnam has stopped issuing import permits for peanuts (Arachis hypogaea), cassia seed (Cassia spp.), cocoa beans (Theobroma cacao), and beans (Phaseolus spp.) from Indonesia.

COVID-19: Viet Nam will begin nationwide social distancing within 15 days, starting 00:00 on April 1, with the principle of every household, village, commune, district and province going into self-isolation. Accordingly, the people are told to stay at home and should only go out in case of extreme necessity, such as buying food, foodstuff and medicine; emergencies; working at factories, production establishments, facilities trading in essential services and goods that are not subject to provisional closure; and other emergency cases. The Government leader also requested the strict observance of keeping an interpersonal distance of at least two meters and not gathering in groups of more than two people outside the workplace, schools and hospitals, and in public places.

The government has approved a plan to buy 1 million tonnes of rice (milled equivalent) from farmers to avoid a drop in price as the main rice crop harvest peaks in March and April with an estimated 20 million tonnes of paddy coming onto the market. The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has set aside about VND 8 trillion (US$ 376 million) for loans to private companies to buy paddy from 15 March to the end of April (IGC, 27 March 2014).

A ban placed on rice export to destinations where sales would be in competition with Government contracts.  According to the Vietnam Food Association, beginning on 10 August 2009, exporters would  not be permitted to sell rice to foreign companies that have signed government backed deals or to foreign traders who compete in the markets where Vietnam aims to sign such contracts.

The Vietnam National Nutrition Strategy

The Vietnamese Ministry of Education and Training is responsible for incorporating nutrition education into the school curriculum at all levels and providing capacity building for teachers as part of the Vietnam National Nutrition Strategy (2011–20).

According to a media report, under the rural training programme, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MARD) set to train 150 000-160 000 laborers during 2013 though its local departments. The Ministry of Finance allocated VND 920 billion (USD 43.4 million) to continue the programme until 2015 (Vietnam Net, 24 May 2013).

As of June 2016, Viet Nam does not have legal regulations in place governing the research and development or regulatory approval process for animal biotechnology applications. However, there is some research on gene technology for improving animal productivity, animal disease treatment, and the production of vaccine for animals utilizing biotechnology.

Vietnam Trade Promotion Agency and Pakistan’s Directorate on Trade Development signed MOU on promoting bilateral trade. Accordingly, the Trade Promotion Authorities of the two countries will coordinate in implementing trade promotion programs, exchanging the list of exhibition and trade fairs to be organized annually at the respective countries to call for the interest and participation of the businesses.

The procurement of one million tonnes of rice during June 15 - July 31 will be delayed until August 15, as enterprises participating in the program have procured only 850 000 tonnes due to rains which hampered rice harvesting in several parts of the country (Oryza, 01 August)

Purchase of 30,000 tons of salt for temporary storage at the price of VND750 per kilogram for the normal salt and VND800 per kilogram for better preserved salt (with a profit of 30% for salt producers).

Creation of food outlets with fair shop prices. The Go Vap District People's Committee has ordered the all district's administrative units (16 wards) to set up at least one outlet in every residential area to sell essential goods at fair prices, especially rice, petrol, milk products, and medicines.

Viet Nam approved the National Green Growth Strategy for the period 2011-2020 with a vision to 2050. Overall objective: Green growth, as a means to achieve a low carbon economy and to enrich natural capital, will become the principal direction in sustainable economic development; reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and increased capability to absorb greenhouse gas are gradually becoming essential indicators in social-economic development.

On November 11, 2013, Viet Nam's Ministry of Finance reduced the export tax on natural and synthetic rubber from 5 percent (synthetic rubber) or 3 percent (natural rubber) to 1%, with effect from December 26, 2013.
COVID-19: The government has decided to re-open schools from 5th September 2020 and re-nomalises the education system.

The Target Program for climate change adaption and green growth for the period of 2016 – 2020 (no.1670/QD-TTg) was approved on 31st October 2017, targetd to develop the competency of the country, adopt simultaneously the solutions to responding to climate change impacts, reducing greenhouse gas emission and protecting human lives and property. An amount of VND 15,866 billion (about USD 750 million) is allocated from the central budget capital. The main tasks include:  
-	Complete 42 projects on planting mangrove and watershed protection forests
-	Plant and rehabilitate 10.000 hectares of coastal mangrove and watershed protection forests for absorbing 02 million tonnes of carbon dioxide each year 
-	Build and improve from 6 to 10 reservoirs and dams with a volume of 100 cubic metres for the purpose of flood adjustment
-	Build and improve from 8 to 10 salinity control and freshwater storage systems 
-	Build complete intra-field engineering infrastructure of 100-ha irrigation area; design in the model for management and operation of water resource systems for green rice production
-	Develop research and experimentation on dryland farming crops for rice and breeding
The Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment presides over and cooperates with relevant Ministries and sectoral administrations, People's Committees. The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development is in charge of reviewing the list of new project proposals.

COVID-19: Prime Minister highlighted that rice exports must be controlled to ensure food security for 100 million Vietnamese in the current context. The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development accelerate agricultural production to guarantee food balance. The Minister of Industry and Trade to submit a report on rice export to the PM before April 5 which must ensure that domestic consumption demand will be met in any case, especially amid the adverse weather conditions and the COVID-19 pandemic. The Finance Ministry was assigned to buy 190,000 tons of rice, 90,000 tons of unhusked rice or more for stockpiling in accordance with the national reserve target in 2020 as approved, thus meeting demand in contingency cases.
The guaranteed purchase price for paddy rice remains at VND5 000 per kilogram (price set in MY 2010/2011).

The Prime Minister has ordered the Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development (MARD) to stock up on pesticides to protect plants, in order to protect paddy production and increase exports next year. After assessing current national reserves levels, specific amount of pesticides to be stock will be fixed.

Additional information:
Ministry will strengthen the examination of all substances to ensure the country import products of best quality. Every year, Viet Nam spends about USD 400-500 million on importing plant protection substances.

A memorandum of understanding (MoU) was signed between China, Lao PDR, and Vietnam on Health Animal Cooperation as a joint approach to prevent animal health risks due to geographical proximity and growing trade of animals and animal products. Main focus is on strengthening cooperation in veterinary research, veterinary drugs, veterinary biologics and trade of animal products (Ministry of Agriculture, 13 March 2012).

Under the one million tonnes rice purchasing programme approved by The Government in January, the paddy price is set at  VND 5 350 (USD 0.25) per kilo in Mekong Delta provinces. Commercial banks provides loans to food companies to enable them to buy paddy/rice for reserves while the Government fully subsidizes interest on these loans for three months (Ministry of Agriculture, 27 February 2013).

This Decision approves the Plan of Action to develop the agricultural and fishery product processing industry in implementation of Vietnam's industrialization strategy within the framework of Vietnam-Japan cooperation through 2020, with a vision toward 2030. This Plan of Action, consisting of six sections, establishes necessary measures to work out solutions to increase the added value in each step of the supply chain. In order to participate in the global supply chain, solutions should be adopted and implemented in order to create a number of typical products and develop and raise the quality of agricultural, fishery and food products. The orientations toward 2020 aim to turn Vietnam into a reliable supplier of safe and high-quality agricultural, fishery and food products. The objectives by 2020 are: to develop the world market's trust in Vietnam as a producer of safe and high-quality agricultural, fishery and food products for export and domestic consumption and to create 3-5 processed agricultural, fishery and food commodity items which can help build Vietnamese brands and image. As strategic issues it aims at ensuring raw material sources with stable quality and quantity.

On May 11, 2015, the Ministry of Health (MOH) issued Circular 8/2015/TT-BYT to amend and supplement the food additive managing provisions regulated in Circular 27/2012/TT-BYT (2012). Accordingly, seven new food additives have been added to the List of food additives allowed for use in Vietnam. In order to consolidate the amended provisions, MOH issued the Consolidation of Circulars on the Management of Food Additives 2/VBHN-BYT dated June 15, 2015.

The general objectives of this plan are:
a/ To develop medicinal plants into a commodity production industry based on science and technology application, renovation of equipment used in researches into selection and creation of strains, cultivation, processing, extraction and technology transfer, aiming to create high-quality products competitive in domestic, regional and world markets.
b/ To manage, sustainably exploit and use medicinal plant resources to achieve medical and social development objectives; to attach importance to the protection, preservation and development of precious and valuable medicinal plant genetic resources; to preserve, promote and enhance the protection of traditional knowledge about the use of medicinal herbs of various ethnic communities.

On 10th June, 2013, the Prime Minister of Vietnam issued Decision no. 899/QD-TTg approving the plan of restructuring the agricultural sector towards improving added value and sustainable development. The paper provides the overall long-term policy framework for agriculture and rural development. 
The major objective of agricultural restructuring is to develop a more vibrant and diversified rural economy with sustainable agricultural growth, high value creation, food safety according to international standard, higher competitiveness and farmer income, and technology-intensive agriculture. The major restructuring priorities should be considered as follows: 1) high value and competitiveness commodities, 2) further value addition of agricultural value chain, 3) Push to quality and food safety control, 4) technology-intensive agricultural growth, 5) consolidated land holdings, decent jobs for on-farm and non-farm employment. 
Key group of policy solutions include to 1) improve the efficiency of state management and institutional reforms, 2) encourage investments from private sector, 3) improve the efficiency of public investments, 4) strengthen the coherence of land policies, trade policies, monetary and fiscal policies to support agriculture transformation and rural poverty reduction.

Central Highlands province of Đắk Lắk has invested VNĐ26 billion (US$1.15 million) on drilling bore wells and building water supply projects. The move aims to provide water against drought to save dry plants and help local residents who face shortage of water for domestic use.

This Decision approves the master plan on hi-tech agricultural parks and zones through 2020, with a vision toward 2030. Pursuant to the Law on High Technologies of 13 November 2008; and in view to implement the Prime Minister's Decision No. 1895/QD-TTg of 17 December 2012. It aims to bring into play the comparative advantages in natural conditions, resources and socio-economic conditions of each ecological area in order to promote hi-tech application in agriculture, contributing to achieving the objectives of agricultural restructuring nationwide and in each region toward higher added value and sustainable development. Hi-tech agricultural parks constitute the technological core for development of hi-tech agricultural zones. To socialize to the utmost investment in the construction of hi-tech agricultural parks and zones; mobilize all economic sectors, especially enterprises, science and technology institutions and attract foreign investment sources. Its general objectives are: To promote development of agriculture toward modern and large-scale commodity production of high yield, quality, efficiency and competitiveness; to ensure national food and foodstuff security and boost exports.

MARD’s Crop Production Department (CPD) has recently approved 17 biotech corn varieties for growing in Vietnam. These approvals follow the first three biotech corn varieties permitted for cultivation in March 2015. This further reduces the competiveness of soybean cultivation as revenue from new corn varieties (including biotech varieties) exceeds revenue from soybean cultivation.

The National Action Program on Zero Hunger for 2018 – 2025 period (decision No. 712/QĐ-TTg) was approved on 12 June 2018. The Plan follows the UNs SDG2 to find long term, sustainable solutions to eliminate hunger in all forms by 2030 through national food security. 
The Plan targets reducing the number of stunted children under two years old to below 20 percent nationwide; aiming to get children under two years with low weight for their height or age to below 5 percent; encouraging farmers to develop a sustainable food system by participating in co-operatives and production chains; enabling households to increase production through large scale farming and gain higher incomes; and reducing foods lost and waste in different forms. 
Zero Hunger is funded by the national poverty reduction program to the tune of VND545 billion (USD23.7 million) plus.

According to a media source, the Vietnam Food Association (VFA) has increased the minimum export price (MEP) of the 25% broken rice to US$ 375 per tonne, up about 6 percent from the previous floor price of US$355 per tonne. The move is intended to prevent decline in domestic rice prices due to low export prices (Oryza, 21 April 2014).

The new 2020 import-export strategy has been approved, foreseen the balanced trade achieved by 2020 and the trade surplus by 2021-2030 period. The export strategy focuses on four product categories: (i) fuel and minerals, (ii) agriculture, forest and seafood, (iii) processed and manufactured industrial products, and (iv) new products. Imports will be closely monitored reduce trade deficit in the long run, and strengthen environmentally friendly and energy saving high technology and machinery’s imports (Ministry of planning and Social portal, 29 November 2012).

MARD approvals of agricultural biotechnology for use as food and feed: As of August 1, 2017, MARD has received 50 completed genetically-engineered (GE) event dossiers and has issued 21 certificates for use as food and feed events, all of which were for soybean and corn. The remaining 29 GE events for soybean, corn, cotton, canola, sugar beet, and alfalfa are still under review.

Interest free loans will be provided to domestic firms to buy one million tonnes of rice between 15 July and 15 September 2010 to help stabilize local market prices. Rice will be bought at VND 3 500 (USD 0.18) per kilogram.

This Decision approves the Strategy for management of systems of special-use forests, marine reserves and internal water reserves of Vietnam through 2020, with a vision toward 2030, with the following major viewpoints: a/ The systems of special-use forest zones, marine reserves and internal water reserves are national assets, where special values of nature conservation, standard specimens of the eco-system and genetic resources of organisms are stored and preserved, historical and cultural relics and scenic places are protected and scientific research is conducted to serve national interests. The Strategy for management of systems of special-use forest zones, marine reserves and internal water reserves through 2020 shall take over and further develop the achievements of the Strategy for management of the system of nature reserves of Vietnam during 2003-2010; b) The Strategy for management of systems of special-use forest zones, marine reserves and internal water reserves through 2020 must conform with the national strategies for socio-economic development and forest protection and development through 2020 and be incorporated in sectoral and local strategies and the national target strategy for response to climate change; c) The State encourages various forms of investment to attract organizations, individuals, scientists and international organizations and concurrently encourages the participation by communities in the buffer zones of special-use forest zones and protection belts of marine reserves and internal water reserves for sustainable management in accordance with law; d) Management of special-use forest zones, marine reserves and internal water reserves must be studied and gradually approach new management methods conformable with international standards and suitable to the actual conditions of Vietnam and each locality. To increase international integration and cooperation regarding special-use forest zones, marine reserves and internal water reserves.

Approval for Cotton Development Plan, with the area under the crop to reach 30,000 ha and output to increase to 20,000 tonnes in 2015. The plan also targets that the total area under cotton cultivation will increase to 76,000 ha, with a total output of 60,000 tonnes in 2020.  The Government will offer financial support for building infrastructure and irrigation systems in cotton-zoned areas. The State budget will also grant financial assistance for activities of cotton research and technology transfer.  The Government will encourage cotton processors to support cotton growers in mechanizing their cultivation progress from preparing land to harvesting, preserving and processing. A fund for stabilizing cotton prices will also be set up to ensure the benefits of growers .

According to media report, the Prime Minister approved the imposition of price ceiling on milk products for children. If the proposal is approved by the Government, prices of these products will be reduced by VND 50 000 (US$ 2.4) to VND 70 000 (US$ 3.3) per box (Viet Nam Net, 07 April 2014).

The GVN issued Decree 43/2017/ND-CP, dated April 14, 2017, regarding the labeling of goods, including all categories of food, beverages, and agricultural inputs circulated in Vietnam, both domestically-produced and imported. This Decree replaced Decree 89/2009 on goods labeling and took effect from June 1, 2017. Decree 43/2017 provides guidelines on label contents and presentation thereof of goods circulated in Vietnam, including imported goods. Accordingly, this Decree extends mandatory contents for virtually all types of food and beverage products circulated in Vietnam, including: food, foodstuff, irradiated foods, GE food, supplemental food, beverages (other than wine and liquor), wine and liquor, food additives, food ingredients, and micronutrients. It also provides mandatory contents for agricultural inputs such as veterinary drugs, pesticides, animal feed.

The GVN maintains suspensions on peanut imports from a number of countries, including Indonesia (since January 2017), Hong Kong (since October 2016), and the Sudan (since October 2016). In May 2017, GVN lifted its suspension on peanut imports from India.

The Ministry of Industry and Trade in Circular No 03/2015/TT-BCT has set an import quota of 102 000 tonnes of salt and 46 305 cartons of eggs (a dozen each) for this year. The quota is imposed on businesses that use salt in their production of chemicals, pharmaceuticals and medical products, while egg quotas are provided to companies that have business registration certificates and have demand to import eggs.

Mekong River Delta sets rice export target to 5.4 MMT annually during the period of 2012-2015. In order to fulfil the target, measures to ensure rice export by improving the quality of rice, diversifying rice products, and sharpening competitive capacity will be implemented (Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, 12 January 2012).

The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development has unveiled a draft plan to set up 11 parks across the country by 2020 to research and innovate agricultural technologies. The hi-tech agricultural parks (HTAPs) will be built in eight regions and according to the tentative master plan, at least 60 per cent of each of the parks must be earmarked for research and experimentation and display of agricultural models that use high technologies. The parks will undertake scientific and technological activities, train human resources, and innovate agricultural technologies.

Farmers purchasing mechanical machinery and equipment for agricultural production and processing, below-5-ton trucks, will receive interest rate subsidies.  Beneficiaries of the rate subsidies are farming households, individuals, cooperatives, and enterprises that are making short and medium-term loans in Vietnamese currency to buy machinery, equipment and materials for their agricultural production. Interest rate subsidies provided until December, 31, 2010.

On 11th March 2021, the Government of Viet Nam has approved the Fisheries Development Strategy to 2030, Vision to 2045. The Strategy aims to enlarge the scale of the fishery sector and to promote the international export. 
The specific objectives include: 1)  The annual growth rate of aquaculture production value will be achieved 3.0 - 4.0%; 2) The total output of annual aquatic products will be achieved about 9.8 million tons; of which, 7.0 million tons of aquaculture production and 2.8 million tons of fisheries production ; 3) The annual value of seafood export turnover will be 14-16 billion USD; and To create jobs for over 3.5 million workers. 
Ten National Programmes have been approved for the implementation of the Strategy

On August 11, 2014, following a near six month regulatory review by Vietnam’s Feed and Food Safety Committee, the Vietnam Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development (MARD) signed the first four Certificates for Food and Feed Safety for four genetically modified corn traits.
Export price of the 25 percent broken rice has been reduced to USD 350 per tonne to boost rice exports and to reduce domestic stocks.

The National Target Program on New Rural Development in the period of 2010-2020 (Decision 800/QD-TTg) was issued on 4th June 2010 to guide the public investment in the rural development in 10,000 communes in Viet Nam. A set of 18 criteria was issued to measure the achievement. The main contents are to "Build new Rural Areas with gradually modern social-economic infrastructures; appropriate economic structures and rational forms of production organisation which links agriculture with rapid development of industries and services; rural development associated with urban planning; democratic and stable rural society which is rich in national cultural character; natural environment being protected; security and order being maintained; people’s spiritual and material lives being improved; and socialist oriented". 
A deputy Prime Minister is in role of the Chairman of the National Steering Committee. The standing/coordinating agency is Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development. All other Ministries, Line Agencies and Provincial authorities are responsible to implement the assigned duties.

According to the Decision No. 1021/TTg-KTN, the Prime Minister requested localities and local banks to implement urgent policies supporting farmers 100% interest loans for salt production investments from June 1 to December 31.

Distibution of  137.8 million doses of bird flu vaccine to 42 provinces and cities nationwide to provide the first round of vaccination for domestic fowl. According to the National Steering Committee for Bird Flu Prevention and Control, the total number of bird flu vaccine doses to be provided for the country’s poultry stock in 2010 is estimated to be 338.9 million.

The plan also targets that the total area under cotton cultivation will increase to 76,000 ha, with a total output of 60,000 tonnes in 2020.  The Government will offer financial support for building infrastructure and irrigation systems in cotton-zoned areas. The Prime Minister granted approval for a National action plan to prevent, mitigate and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing until 2025. The plan aims to promote sustainable development of fisheries, contributing to ensuring national security as well as regional and international integration while. 
A database of the fisheries sector will be set up to verify, certify and trace the origin of domestic seafood while denying the import of fish products that are identified as being caught in IUU fishing. Fisheries surveillance forces at all levels will be strengthened to improve their capacity in patrolling, inspecting and handling law violations in the country’s waters. A roadmap will be built for the compulsory installation and operation of fishing vessel-monitoring equipment on all domestic fishing boats. 
During 2021-2015, one of the main tasks will be establishing three large fisheries centres along with fishing ports and a network of logistics facilities to receive foreign fishing vessels.

Viet Nam and the Customs Union of Russia, Belarus and Kazakhstan signed a Joint Statement for which the Customs Union will give priorities for Viet Nam in tariff advantages, create chances for the export of Vietnamese goods, including agricultural and aquatic products, garment, footwear and timber.

COVID-19: The government has decided to re-open schools in all 63 provinces from 4th May 2020 after 18 days without new infection case. The regulation on social distancing was removed on 24 April 2020.

Rice export quota increased to a record 7 million tonnes in 2009, some 2 million higher than the initial figure set earlier this year. The increase was due to ample supplies and to compensate for lower prices when compared with last year.
For CY 2009, the Vietnam Food Association (Vietfood) has fixed a minimum buying price of VND 3,500 per kg (USD 0.20/kg) for winter-spring rice for its member-companies.
COVID-19: 3 March 2020, Vietnam approved a plan to delay the collection of US$7.6 billion worth of taxes and land rent to help businesses hit by COVID-19. Notice 897/TCT-QLN

Food–based dietary guidelines – Vietnam

In 2013, Vietnam published the revised the '10 tips on proper nutrition for period 2013–2020' aimed at the general population. Vietnam uses a three-dimensional food pyramid to represent the messages of its guidelines. The pyramid is divided into seven layers according to recommended levels of consumption. Cereals and tubers are at the bottom, followed by vegetables, fruits, protein-rich foods, fats and oils. Sugar and salt are at the apex of the pyramid.

This Decision approves the master plan on the national special-use forest system through 2020, with a vision toward 2030, with the following major contents: a) The overall objectives are: to conserve and sustainably develop important natural eco-systems, values of natural landscapes, historical and cultural relics and scenic places and endangered, precious and rare species in the special-use forest system. b) Specific objectives are: to increase the total area of special-use forests from 2.2 million ha at present to 2.4 million ha by 2020, in line with the Strategy for management of systems of special-use forests, marine reserves and inland water reserves of Vietnam through 2020, with a vision toward 2030.

On March 1, 2017, Vietnam announced it was again suspending the import of five agricultural products (peanuts, cassia seed, cocoa beans, haricot beans and tamarind) from India after several consignments were found to be contaminated with the peanut beetle Caryedon serratus Olivier.

According to a media report, the government has secured an export contract for 200 000 tonnes of rice with Malaysia in 2014. VINAFOOD II, the state-owned rice export corporation, will be in charge of the operation (Oryza, 19 June 2014).

The Ministry of Science and Technology will increase the application of post-harvest technology in agricultural production in order to boost the competitiveness of agricultural products in global markets. The pilot project is focused on exporting surimi, a blended seafood product, to markets such as Japan and the Republic of Korea at a price of US$ 1 750 per tonne.

Free Trade Agreement signed with Chile. Under this agreement the 73% percent of Chilean exports will enter Vietnam duty-free, while the rest of the products will begin to benefit in year 3 or year 15. Only 4 percent of the products were not included in the agreement. About 75 percent of Vietnamese exports will enter Chile tariff-free immediatly and the rest of the products will be liberalized in tranches ranging from 6 to 11 years.
The Ministry of Industry and Trade has issued salt import quotas for 146,000 tones while another 24,000 tones are awaiting allocation.

The National Plan focuses on improving quality of vocational training to rural laborers in both non-agricultural and agricultural jobs. The training targets to create 5.5 million rural decent jobs, including 4.1 million off-farm jobs and 1.4 million agriculture base jobs. It contributes to enhance labour quality, to transform labor  and economic structure for industrialization and modernization of agriculture and rural areas, and implementing effectively agriculture restructuring plan, new rural development and sustainable poverty reduction.

According to a media report, the Ministry of Industry and Trade issued a new order to limit the number of rice exporters to a maximum of 150 and revoke export license to any exporter failing to export at least 10 000 tonnes for two consecutive years (Oryza, 08 August 2013).

New allocation for natural disasters and for price stabilization purposes. A fund equivalent to VND 500 billion will be created where a fifth (20%) is to be spent on reserving goods for relief aid during natural disasters and the rest (80%) will be advanced to traders for the purpose of price stabilization. This fund will function by providing loans (interest-free advances) at an interest-free rate to "Enterprises in Ha Noi"  for food reserve purposes so enable them to offer a 10% decrease in prices so consumers can cope with market fluctuations.

MARD signed decision number 558/QD-BNN-BVTV on March 1, 2017, and starting on May 1, 2017, MARD will stop issuing import permits for peanuts, cassia seed, cocoa beans, haricot beans and tamarind from India. MARD/PPD has imposed strict controls on all shipments of these five products entering Vietnam to prevent the spread of contamination by the Caryedon serratus Olivier.
The rice export ban has been lifted signaling improving supplies on the world market. The Government allows export contracts of up to 3.5 million tonnes until the end of September.

As of 9 June 2020, Viet Nam will continue to use Glyphosate herbicide to protect plants. A ban on the use of this product was supposed to be implemented on 10 June 2020 following Decision 1186 of 10 April 2019 from the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MARD), but this decision was cancelled and replaced by MARD Circular 06/2020 of 28 April 2020.

This National Nutrition Strategy for 2011 – 2020 is a multi-sectoral policy document, aiming to improve the diet of Vietnamese people in terms of quantity and quality, reduce malnutrition of children, and manage obesity/overweight. The vision to 2030 is to reduce child malnutrition below the level of public health significance and to remarkably increase the mean height in adults. In addition, increased awareness about proper nutrition and behavior change should be improved in the general population for the prevention of nutrition related chronic diseases and adequate food safety controls should be ensured.

This Decision approves the national food safety strategy to control food safety from production to consumption in order to protect health and rights of consumers and to meet the requirements of national development and international integration of the country.The strategy shall aim at raising awareness and practicing food safety for target groups; building capacity for food safety management system; improving food safety assurance in manufacture, processing and selling facilities; actively preventing acute food poisoning.

In January 2017, the Vietnamese government abolished the Decision No. 6139/QD-BCT that stipulated strict conditions for becoming a rice exporter.

Increase in Minimum Export Price (MEP) of rice. On 23 August 2010, the Vietnam Food Association (VFA) lifted the MEP of 5% broken rice by USD 30/ton, to USD 430 fob (free on board), and for the 25% grade by USD 20, to USD 390 fob. The increases follow the recent recovery in Asian rice export quotations. In late August VFA instituted a USD 20/ton increase for each grade and subsequently on 15 September 2010, VFA raised again the MEPs for 5% broken rice and 25% broken rice by USD 25/ton each, to USD 475 fob and USD 435 fob, respectively, to reflect strength in the international market.

COVID-19: Vietnam’s government approved a plan to export 400,000 tonnes of rice in April after rice exports were previously suspended and another 400,000 tonnes in May. The long-term objectives for agriculture will be reflected in three sustainable pillars:
•	economic: maintain robust agricultural growth and improve sectorial competitiveness, primarily via advances in productivity, efficiency, and value addition, and better meet the needs and preferences of consumers
•	social: continue to raise farmer incomes and rural living standards, reduce the incidence and severity of rural poverty, and ensure household and national food and nutrition security
•	environmental: improve natural resources management, reduce impacts, contribute to get environmental benefits and improve capacities to manage weather-related and other natural hazards in the context of Vietnam.

The specific objectives are: 
-	Growth of agriculture reaches 3% per year; productivity increases by 3,5% per year; ratio of agricultural workers decreases to under 40%; ratio of trained agricultural workers reaches 22%; 
-	Income of rural residents increases by at least 1,8 times compared to 2015; 50% co the communes meet standards for new rural areas; 15.000 agricultural cooperatives and cooperative associations operate effectively; most rural residents have access to clean water.
-	Climate change response and environmental protection is effective; emission from agricultural production is reduced; forest coverage reaches 42%.

The National Wetlands Policy aims to promote a coordinated approach for the management and conservation of wetland ecosystems in Zambia. Through the implementation of this Policy, it is anticipated that wetlands will be able to contribute much more than now to the sustainable development of the nation.
VISION: A functional, productive and resilient wetland system that will contribute to addressing climate change maintenance of biodiversity, provision of ecosystem goods and services and sustainable livelihoods.
In order to achieve the vision, the overall objective of this Policy is: To preserve and conserve wetland resources and protect the wetland environment in order to ensure sustainable utilization of Zambia’s wetlands.
In pursuit of this overall objective, the two thematic areas of focus for this policy are Wetland Conservation and Protection and Sustainable Socio-economic utilisation. The following are the specific objectives.
Wetland conservation and protection
Objective 1.1: To conserve wetland ecosystems so as to ensure their integrity, productivity and sustainability.
Objective.1.2: To Protect the wetlands and their catchment areas and improve the resilience of wetland systems to natural and anthropogenic shocks.
Objective 6.1.3: To promote research, inventorying and monitoring of wetland resources to inform effective management.
2 Sustainable Socio-economic use
Objective 2.1: To promote and support sustainable livelihood options in order to ensure productivity while protecting wetland resources
Objective 2.2: To promote stakeholder participation in effective management of wetlands and ensure equitable sharing of benefits.
Objective 2.3: To regulate investments and promote sustainable management of wetlands so that they are maintained for the foreseeable future.
Expected results:
a) Enhanced biodiversity conservation i.e. both flora and fauna.
b) Promotion of tourism.
c) Enhanced potential for fisheries and pastoralism,
d) Provision of water to support agricultural activities.
e) Provision of clean water free of pollutants and harmful chemicals to communities.
f) Provision of abundant freshwater (surface water) for domestic use.
g) Flood storage and protection
h) Provide carbon sequestration.
This Policy is divided into eight chapters starting with introduction in Chapter I. Chapter II presents the situation analysis, highlighting critical analysis and review of the situation on Zambian wetlands. Chapter III highlights the overall Vision of the policy while chapter IV presents the rationale. Chapter V outlines the Policy’s guiding principles. The Policy Objectives are outlined in Chapter VI and the policy measures are presented in Chapter VII. Finally Chapter VIII presents the implementation framework.

The Government of the Republic of Zambia (GoZ) is integrating climate change concerns into its agriculture policy agenda. Under its Zambia climate-smart  agriculture (CSA) strategy framework, the GoZ is promoting  the rollout of CSA practices that will sustainably increase  productivity, enhance resilience, and reduce or remove  greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The CSA investment plan  (CSAIP) aims to identify and fill knowledge gaps about CSA’s  local- and national-level benefits, specifically under  climate change, inform policy development, and prioritize  investment opportunities. The World Bank collaborated with  the GoZ to develop a CSAIP intended to support the  operationalization of the country’s climate commitments  toward development of a productive, resilient, and  low-emission agriculture sector. The CSAIP development began  with a participatory process that identified the agriculture sector’s policy goals. This report takes the next step by  assessing the impacts of a suite of CSA practices on  achieving the sector goals and on household welfare. The  report concludes with recommendations and proposals for  future CSA investments.

This NBSAP2 represents our commitment to achieving both the long-term and medium-term national development objectives enshrined in the Vision 2030 and Revised Sixth National Development Plan, respectively. Zambia’s NBSAP-2 will cover
the period 2015-2025, and its vision is “By 2025, biodiversity is valued, conserved, restored and wisely used, maintaining ecosystem services, sustaining a healthy environment and delivering benefits essential for all Zambians and the Zambian economy.” Based on national and provincial prioritization exercises, the five strategic goals of the CBD Strategic Plan were considered highly relevant to Zambia, and these provide the overarching framework for NBSAP-2. The 20 Aichi Biodiversity Targets were reduced to 18 national targets, which underscores the relevance of the CBD Strategic Plan and Aichi Targets (2011-2020) to Zambia’s priorities. The Strategic Goals and Targets of Zambia’s NBSAP2 are:
Strategic Goal A: Address the underlying causes of biodiversity loss by mainstreaming biodiversity across government and society. 
Strategic Goal B: Reduce the direct pressures on biodiversity and promote sustainable use.
Strategic Goal C: Improve the status of biodiversity by safeguarding ecosystems, species and genetic diversity.
Strategic Goal D: Enhance the benefits to all from biodiversity and ecosystem services.
Strategic Goal E: Enhance implementation of NBSAP2 through participatory planning, knowledge management and capacity building.

Following the expiry of the R-SNDP in 2016, the Government spearheaded the formulation of the Seventh National Development Plan which will cover the period from 2017 to 2021. The Plan departs from sectoral-based planning to an integrated (multi-sectoral) approach under the theme “Accelerating development efforts towards Vision 2030 without leaving anyone behind”. 
This document is organised as follows: Part I contains the overview of the 7NDP and the people’s voices on development; Part II outlines the development context: past performance and opportunities and challenges of Zambia’s development; Part III presents the current situation of the economy, at both national and sectoral levels; it also describes the macroeconomic framework in which the Plan will be executed. Part IV describes what it will take to move towards the Vision 2030, the conceptual framework, the goal and the strategic objectives of the 7NDP. Part V presents the strategic areas of the Plan, which are economic diversification and job creation; poverty and vulnerability reduction; reducing developmental inequalities; enhancing human development; and the creation of a conducive governance environment for a diversified and inclusive economy. Financing of the Plan is discussed in Part VI, while Part VII discusses the implementation and coordination as well as the monitoring and evaluation framework of the Plan.

The National Wetlands Policy aims to promote a coordinated approach for the management and conservation of wetland ecosystems in Zambia. Through the implementation of this Policy, it is anticipated that wetlands will be able to contribute much more than now to the sustainable development of the nation.
VISION: A functional, productive and resilient wetland system that will contribute to addressing climate change maintenance of biodiversity, provision of ecosystem goods and services and sustainable livelihoods.
In order to achieve the vision, the overall objective of this Policy is: To preserve and conserve wetland resources and protect the wetland environment in order to ensure sustainable utilization of Zambia’s wetlands.
In pursuit of this overall objective, the two thematic areas of focus for this policy are Wetland Conservation and Protection and Sustainable Socio-economic utilisation. The following are the specific objectives.
Wetland conservation and protection
Objective 1.1: To conserve wetland ecosystems so as to ensure their integrity, productivity and sustainability.
Objective.1.2: To Protect the wetlands and their catchment areas and improve the resilience of wetland systems to natural and anthropogenic shocks.
Objective 6.1.3: To promote research, inventorying and monitoring of wetland resources to inform effective management.
2 Sustainable Socio-economic use
Objective 2.1: To promote and support sustainable livelihood options in order to ensure productivity while protecting wetland resources
Objective 2.2: To promote stakeholder participation in effective management of wetlands and ensure equitable sharing of benefits.
Objective 2.3: To regulate investments and promote sustainable management of wetlands so that they are maintained for the foreseeable future.
Expected results:
a) Enhanced biodiversity conservation i.e. both flora and fauna.
b) Promotion of tourism.
c) Enhanced potential for fisheries and pastoralism,
d) Provision of water to support agricultural activities.
e) Provision of clean water free of pollutants and harmful chemicals to communities.
f) Provision of abundant freshwater (surface water) for domestic use.
g) Flood storage and protection
h) Provide carbon sequestration.
This Policy is divided into eight chapters starting with introduction in Chapter I. Chapter II presents the situation analysis, highlighting critical analysis and review of the situation on Zambian wetlands. Chapter III highlights the overall Vision of the policy while chapter IV presents the rationale. Chapter V outlines the Policy’s guiding principles. The Policy Objectives are outlined in Chapter VI and the policy measures are presented in Chapter VII. Finally Chapter VIII presents the implementation framework.

Objectives: (l) rehabilitation and construction of urban roads, (ll) creation of thousands of jobs for Zambian youths, and (lll) development of skills and knowledge in the use of paving blocks technology.

The Vision of the Second National Agricultural Policy is: “An efficient, competitive and sustainable agricultural sector, which assures food and nutrition security, increased employment opportunities and incomes. The rationale for the Second National Agriculture Policy is to provide a conducive environment that will stimulate sustainable agricultural development. The Policy provides a framework that will promote sustainable agricultural diversification, agricultural commercialization, private sector participation and inclusive agricultural growth. It is envisaged that this Policy will promote competitiveness, stimulate efficiency, increased productivity and profitability in the agriculture sector. It will thus contribute effectively to attaining food and nutrition security, employment creation, increased incomes and reduced rural poverty.

The Ministry of Finance has allocated K 254.9 million (US$ 39 815 400) to the electronic voucher (e-voucher) system which will allow farmers more flexibility of choice in the inputs they receive. A further K 1.1 billion (US$ 171 820 000) has been allocated to the Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP). Around 1 000 000 farmers are expected to access inputs through the e-voucher and FISP programmes in 2015.

COVID-19: Suspension of customs duties and VAT on additional medical supplies used in the fight against Covid-19: In order to expedite the provision of medical related devices needed to support the fight against Covid-19, Government will extend the list of medical supplies that are not subject to Import Duty and Value Added Tax for an initial period of 6 months. The complete list comprises 38 individual items which include testing equipment, protective garments, thermometers, disinfectants, sterilisation products and other medical equipment such as ventilators and patient monitoring devices.

The Food Reserve Agency (FRA) will off load stocks on the domestic market to millers and communities at the price of K 1,200 per Kg or  K 60,000 per 50 Kg bag. 

Objective: stabilize food prices and ensure stable supply of the staple crops.

The Strategic Plan covers a 5 year period, 2019 to 2023. The Vision of the Zambia SPARS, reflecting the future image of the national agricultural statistical system is: An efficient, responsive and coordinated source of agricultural and rural statistics’. The Mission of the Zambia SPARS, reflecting what the national agricultural statistics system should deliver, is: ‘To provide quality agricultural and rural statistics for evidence-based policy and decision making for enhanced user satisfaction’.
For the development of SPARS_ZAM, five Strategic Goals have been elaborated to meet the challenges (listed in section 3.2) which have been identified by stakeholders in the various subsectors of agriculture. These Strategic Goals, which also link to the specific Goals of the NSDS, establishing the close alignment of the SPARS and the NSDS, are:

SG2: Meet the national and international demand for agriculture statistics

The Government of the Republic of Zambia has officially released the Revised Sixth National Development Plan (R-SNDP) 2013-2016 which is the revision of the Sixth National Development Plan (SNDP) 2011-2015, launched by the Government on 04/02/2011.

The R-SNDP is primarily an investment plan which focuses on capital investment areas with a bias to rural development and job creation. It, therefore, identifies the main growth areas or sectors such as skills development, science and technology, agriculture, livestock and fisheries, energy, and infrastructural development particularly transport infrastructure while enhancing human development related sectors of water and sanitation, education and health.

The President of the Republic of Zambia, Mr. Rupiah Bwezani Banda, launched the Sixth National Development Plan (SNDP) 2011-2015. The theme of the SNDP is “Sustained economic growth and poverty reduction”. 

The objectives of the SNDP are to accelerate infrastructure development, economic growth and diversification, rural investment, poverty reduction and enhance human development. While recognizing the importance of all sectors, the SNDP contains only sector programmes that have been identified as critical to achieving the overall objectives of the Plan.

The National Health Strategic Plan (2011-2015) aims at improving the health status of people in Zambia in order to contribute to socio-economic development.  
Objectives:
1. To significantly improve public health surveillance and control of epidemics, in order to reduce morbidity and mortality associated with epidemics.
2. To halt and begin to reverse the incidence and prevalence of NCDs including the improvement of mental health services throughout Zambia.
3. To significantly improve the nutritional status of the population and ensure food safety, particularly for children, adolescents and mothers in child bearing age, so as to prevent diseases.
4. To promote and improve hygiene and universal access to safe and adequate water, food safety, and acceptable sanitation, with the aim of reducing the incidence of water and food borne diseases throughout Zambia.
5. To provide efficient and effective health education and promotion, in order to empower individuals, families and communities with appropriate knowledge to develop and practice healthy lifestyles.

The Government of Zambia introduced a wheat import quota of 75 000 tonnes in March to ensure that the county maintains sufficient supplies following a 26 percent production decrease in 2014. The country has been self-sufficient in wheat for the previous three years. The import quota is set to expire at the end of August in order to facilitate the procurement of the domestic crop, to be harvested from August/September.

COVID-19: The Government of Zambia will implement a waiver of tax penalties and interest to assist companies and businesses manage their cash flows during this period when they are faced with reduced revenues, Government has decided to waive tax penalties and interest on outstanding tax liabilities resulting from the impact of Covid-19. The Zambia Revenue Authority published guidelines on the criteria on who qualifies, the period of relief and other related modalities.

The Government of Zambia has recently increased budget allocations for the Food Security Pack Programme. In 2015, the Ministry of Community Development and Social Welfare has allocated to the programme ZMK 49 829 (US$ 5 million), targeting 30 100 households.

The Ministry of Agriculture will increase the irrigated hectarage by rehabilitating and constructing new irrigation schemes that would result in bringing a total of 18 000 ha under various forms of irrigation (furrow, drip, sprinkler). Multi-purpose dams (45 small and 2 large) and 50 weirs will be constructed, area under flood control will also be increased by promoting drainage (in-situ), use of pedal pumps for ground water and use of renewable energy pumps (solar, ram and wind mills). 

Objective: ensure efficient water-use and irrigation and increase availability of water for multi-purpose use.

In order to further promote crop diversification, the Government decided that extension services would continue to support farmers in growing crops suitable for the ecological zone. The Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP) will also be tailored to provide seeds for a variety of crops according to ecological comparative advantage.
Objective: achieve greater productivity and diversification in agriculture.

According to media sources, the Government has suspended the implementation of the e-voucher system that was supposed to be used for farmers in accessing subsidized inputs under the Farmer Input Support Pogramme (FSIP). The Government had decided to start implementing a pilot phase in ten districts as from 2013.

The implementation of the e-voucher system had to be suspended due to inadequate logistics. The e-voucher system requires that private agro business houses have electronic register of the 241 000 farmers as well as electronic voucher, while farmers needed to have either a phone or a computer. It also required the Ministry of Agriculture to create a redemption fund which would be recovered by the private suppliers once the farmers acquired the inputs in their respective districts.

During the 2014/2015 agricultural marketing season, the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) intends to sell 650 000 metric tons of maize on both the local and export markets (between November 2014 and April 2015). The FRA will sell maize at the following prices: ZMW 1,521/Metric ton for local market and US$ 240/Metric ton for export market.

Objective: the sale is in line with the Agency’s mandate to meet shortfalls in food supply on the local market and, therefore, helps stabilize food prices during the above highlighted period, as well as to create storage space by exporting the excess stock.

To increase the productivity and diversify the production of agricultural crops by small scale farmers, the Government will expand the scope of the Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP) to cover other crops besides maize such as soya, cotton, sunflower and rice. It will also mainstream the electronic voucher system to strengthen the private sector's role in supplying agricultural inputs.

The Ministry of Agriculture plans to train 300 financial service providers in rural finance, micro credit, etc. at the district level to promote village/rural banking services through training and sensitisation of 250 000 small scale farmers (of which at least 30% will be women) in rural finance, micro credit, processing and diversification, etc. 

Objective: increase access to banking services and credit in rural areas.

The Ministry of Agriculture will proceed to update the inventory of land and water resources at all levels. The expected outputs include: 20 districts with detailed land and soil resources maps, updated agricultural suitability maps, detailed water resources maps, the development of a detailed land and soil database and an additional one targeting water resources. The Ministry will also focus on initiating and strengthening Community Base sustainable Land Management (CBSLM) initiatives.

Objective: improve land-use planning and enhance community participation in integrated land-use systems.

The Ministry of Agriculture will develop new crop varieties suitable to the country’s different agricultural ecological zones and their subsequent multiplication and dissemination. In this regard, a total of 28 varieties of different crops will be developed. Approximately 20 000 farmers will be trained in seed and tuber multiplication, while other interventions under diversification will involve extension activities such as the promotion of 9 000 farmer field schools, as well as 9 000 demonstration plots and 3 200 field days.

Objective: promotion of improved productivity.

The Government shall endeavour through this Policy to provide a labour market management mechanism that will be able to respond effectively and efficiently to the demands of a liberalized market economy. Thus the objectives and strategies set forth in this policy are intended to ensure that the role of the institution with jurisdiction on labour matters in national development is streamlined to meet the aspirations of the Zambian people.

The National Agriculture Investment Plan (NAIP) aims to facilitate and support the development of a sustainable, dynamic, diversified and a competitive agricultural sector that assures food security at household and national levels and maximizes the sector's contribution to GDP. To achieve this objective, the following five impact indicators will be tracked between the current (2011) and five years time from now (2018): (i) reduction of rural poverty from 77% to 50%; (ii) increase in agricultural exports as a percentage of non-traditional exports from 41% in 2011 to 55%; (iii) reduction in chronic malnutrition of children under five from 45% to 30%; (iv) reduce soil erosion per hectare from 20 tonnes to 10 tonnes, and; (v) increase cereals production from the 3.2 million tonnes to 6.0 million tonnes.

According to a media source, the Minister of Agriculture of Zambia announced that the Zambian strategic maize reserves will double from 500,000 tonnes to 1 million tonnes. Moreover, the Government decided to limit exports in order to control staple food prices and to respond to global grain prices surge. The boosting of the strategic reserves through locally purchased maize would take place in four months from July to October 2012. The Government will moreover centralize the issuance of maize export permits to closely monitor sales outside the country.

The Minister of Finance allocated K 37.2 billion (US$ 7.44 million) for the construction of dams, irrigation projects and training of small scale farmers. The investment's goal is to reduce the country dependency on rain-fed agriculture which is highly dependent on weather variability.

The Ministry of Agriculture will establish and enact crop insurance, strengthen weather forecasting capability for agriculture by establishing weather stations in at least 100 districts, and carry out Post Harvest and Crop Forecast Surveys in a consistent and timely manner.

Objective: ensure stability of small-scale farmers' food and nutrition security through enhanced farmers' protection against disaster.

The Government of the Republic of Zambia recognises the crucial role that nutrition plays in health, education, and economic productivity; however, investment in nutrition has been limited. There has also been a lack of long-term sustainable activities, interventions, and funding related to nutrition.  As the government develops the second phase of the Most Critical Days Programme (MCDP II), advocacy efforts will help: • Reinforce government’s and cooperating partners’ long-term commitment to and investment in nutrition and ensure the appropriate use of resources intended for nutrition. • Strengthen capacity to deliver nutrition services and interventions and improve coverage. • Increase coordination of nutrition-related activities. • Prioritise and harmonise legislation to improve nutrition. • Ensure nutrition is enshrined in all sector policies, work plans, and budgets. • Improve accountability for nutrition across sectors. Nutrition advocacy efforts can contribute to increased visibility, commitment, and action for nutrition services and interventions.

The Government of the Republic of Zambia (GoZ) is integrating climate change concerns into its agriculture policy agenda. Under its Zambia climate-smart  agriculture (CSA) strategy framework, the GoZ is promoting  the rollout of CSA practices that will sustainably increase  productivity, enhance resilience, and reduce or remove  greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The CSA investment plan  (CSAIP) aims to identify and fill knowledge gaps about CSA’s  local- and national-level benefits, specifically under  climate change, inform policy development, and prioritize  investment opportunities. The World Bank collaborated with  the GoZ to develop a CSAIP intended to support the  operationalization of the country’s climate commitments  toward development of a productive, resilient, and  low-emission agriculture sector. The CSAIP development began  with a participatory process that identified the agriculture sector’s policy goals. This report takes the next step by  assessing the impacts of a suite of CSA practices on  achieving the sector goals and on household welfare. The  report concludes with recommendations and proposals for  future CSA investments.

The Government plans to continue the rehabilitation and construction of camp houses, step up efforts to increase farmer training and provide for mobility of extension staff through a budgetary allocation of K 13.3 billion (US$ 2.66 million) in 2011.

Objective: make extension services more accessible and tcontinue provision of frontline support to farmers,

Starting from 2013, the Government of Zambia plans to introduce a new system, the electronic voucher system (e-voucher), under the current Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP) to eliminate corruption and help farmers diversify from maize production.

The e-vouchers will be redeemable for the identified range of inputs, namely: seeds, fertilizer, fingerlings, stockfeed, agricultural lime, veterinary drugs, agrochemicals, agricultural equipment and implements.

The Minister of Finance and National Planning allocated ZMK 100 billion (US$ 20.4 million) the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) to purchase grains from farmers, particularly those in remote areas, providing them with market access to ensure future food production and household food security.

AGRITEX Plant Protection Research Institute is distributing 2 800 kilogrammes of carbarly and boom sprays required for containing the armyworm outbreak has hit some parts of the country affecting hundreds of hectares of maize and pastures in Mashonaland West, Mashonaland Central, Matabeleland North, Manicaland and Midlands provinces.

Zimbabwe will remove specified food supplies from zero rating and exemption. This means that the supply of several basic foodstuffs now attracts VAT at the rate of 15% with effect from 1 February 2017. Some of the items that have been previously removed from the VAT zero-rated include but are not limited to potatoes, rice, margarine, mahewu (fermented liquid mealie-meal porridge), meat and fish.

The Government is targeting to assist 1 million vulnerable rural households with crop input packs comprising 10 kg maize/sorghum seeds, 100 kg compound D and 100 kg Ammonium Nitrate. The programme is estimated to cost US$98 million.

The Grain Marketing Board announced a Free On Board (FOB) import parity related maize and wheat grain floor prices in foreign currency or the local currency equivalent. Hence, the GMB assumes the role of buyer of last resort.
Millers and any other grain merchants will compete in the purchase of maize and wheat grain direct from farmers, alongside the GMB, at prices not lower than the import parity related floor price.

The first objective of the strategy is to operationalize Commitment V of the Food and Nutrition Security Policy which states that the Government of Zimbabwe (GOZ) is committed to ensuring nutrition security for all through the implementation of evidence-based nutrition interventions that are integrated within a broad public health framework including health services, water and sanitation. The second objective is to contribute towards making further progress against the other Scaling up Nutrition (SUN) targets.
Crop input pack support for small scale farmers, under which 10 kg seed packs and two 50 kg bags of fertilizer are provided.

The resources earmarked for energy consists of US$482 million, on account of power generation, transmission, distribution and rural electrification projects, meant to address the major power shortages that are undermining economic activity, as well as provision of basic social services in the country. This should also include incentives for private sector participation through cost-reflective tariffs, effective revenue collection systems and measures to address operational efficiencies within the utilities.  In addition to energy, US$299.3 million will be allocated for ICT backbone infrastructure, followed by US$133.8 million towards transport infrastructure.

Banks recently unveiled a $1 billion loan facility package that was set to benefit crop and livestock farmers for the 2015-16 agricultural season. However, the banks announced that only farmers with collateral in the form of assets outside their farms such as title deeds for houses and business premises would be considered and that farmers should have a stop-order facility to make it easier for the banks to recoup their money when farmers sell their produce or possess evidence that they had produce held at local warehouses.

Zimbabwe’s Climate Change Response Strategy mainstreams climate change through a sectorial approach to ensure that each sector implements adaptation and mitigation actions. Each sector will therefore be able to direct its project proposals to the appropriate funding mechanism.
The Response Strategy is divided into six sections. These include an introductory section which comprises a brief profile of Zimbabwe and the Vision, Mission, Goal, Strategic Objectives, Pillars and Guiding Principles of the National Climate Change Response Strategy (Section 1).
This is followed by a synopsis of climate change across scales from global, regional, national to local level (Section 2); sector specific challenges, risks and impacts as well as relevant adaptation and mitigation measures (Section 3); strategy enablers such as capacity building; technology transfer; climate change education, communication and awareness (Section 4); climate change governance (Section 5); and finally a section on Action Plans, Implementation Framework and Resource Mobilization (Section 6).
The National Climate Change Response Strategy provides a framework for a comprehensive and strategic approach on aspects of adaptation, mitigation, technology, financing, public education and awareness. It will help to inform Government on how to strengthen the climate and disaster risk management policies.

Import duties have been restored on some food commodities thanks to the improved supply of basic goods and in order to protect local producers.
For basic commodities such as maize meal and cooking oil, the proposed import duty takes effect from 1st August 2011 while for other food stuffs such as potato chips, baked beans and mixed fruit jam, the rates will be applied from the beginning of September.  
The proposed duty will range between 10 and 25 %.
Duty on salt, rice and flour remains suspended until the end of 2011.

The Government of Zimbabwe removed regulations that fixed the procurement price of maize at USD 390 per tonne in April 2015, lifting price controls measures that were implemented in 2014. This follows the earlier removal of the maize import ban, imposed in 2014, in response to expectations of a reduced 2015 maize harvest and consequently larger import requirements in the 2015/16 marketing year (April/March).

The Medium Term Plan (MTP) is the premier economic and social policy document of Zimbabwe, it will guide all other government policy documents and sets out clearly the national priorities and investment programmes for the next five years 2011-2015.The MTP’s main goal is to transform the economy, reduce poverty, create job, maintain macroeconomic stability and restore the economy’s capacity to produce goods and services competitively, building upon the gains achieved since the launch of STERP in March 2009.

The Roadmap to a US$8 billion Industrial and Commercial sector outlines the plan to raise the manufacturing and commercial sector contribution to GDP from the current US$7.16 billion to US$8.03 billion by 2023, through the sector’s diversified 94 sub-sectors.

The maize producer price has been revised upwards by the Ministry of Agriculture, Mechanisation and Irrigation Development from US$310 to US$378,86 per metric tonne for the 2013/14 marketing season, representing a 28 percent increment.

The Zimbabwe Farmers Union (ZFU) has embarked on a capacity building programme to improve conservation farming practices in the country in a bid to increase yields. 4000 farmers in the Midlands and Mashonaland East provinces will benefit from the up-scaling conservation agriculture scheme that is being spearheaded by ZFU as part of efforts to improve agriculture production.

The 2016 National Budget is also prioritising cloud seeding to enhance rainfed crops, with US$200 000 having already been disbursed in support of a fairly wider programme. The proposal is to allocate a further US$300 000 for this purpose.

The Zimbabwe Leather Sector Strategy envisages transforming the Zimbabwean leather industry into a vibrant and internationally competitive sector, contributing to sustainable development through value addition. The document provides an overview of the current context and value chain of the leather sector, and it outlines a strategy framed around five main objectives: 1) strengthen value chain networking, coordination and policy advocacy; 2) improve access to finance across the value chain; 3) improve market intelligence and promotion of the value chain; 4) improve the quality and collection system of hides and skins; 5) improve value addition and output through technical training and establishment of clusters. The strategy identifies specific targets to be achieved by 2017 and it sets an action plan with specific activities in order to fullfil those targets.

The Tobacco Industry Development Support Institute will carry out a research on the impact of the golden leaf in the local economy to provide data for use in lobbying against the global anti-tobacco campaign, while challenging the World Health Organisations framework convention on tobacco control which seeks to significantly reduce production.

The National HIV Care & Treatment Programme Strategic Plan 2013-2017, themed “Towards Achievement of Universal Access to Quality HIV Care and Treatment Services”, was developed to facilitate and guide the scaling up of HIV care & Treatment services in Zimbabwe towards universal access as well as “ Zero HIV related Deaths, Zero New Infections and Zero Discrimination” The goals of this strategy are to reduce HIV related morbidity and mortality, improve the quality of life for all PLHIV and to contribute to the reduction of new HIV infections in Zimbabwe. The objectives of this plan are to: guide planning; setting of targets and time lines on when to achieve the targets; determining the resources needed to achieve the goals set in the plan; make it easier for partners to identify areas that they would want to support in the process of scaling up and assist with evaluation of progress made by all partners over a period of time.

Allocation of US$ 7 million in support of livestock development programmes targeting livestock breeding, training of livestock farmers and strengthening of veterinary services for animal disease control and prevention.
